We study a different aspect of this phenomenon: the effect of a temporary intervention can continue to evolve after the intervention has ended, to the point that its sign or ranking changes at later checkpoints.

This creates a basic problem for evaluating temporary optimization schedules. Such schedules are usually specified by an update rule and the interval over which it is applied. But when the intervention ends, the treated and reference runs generally enter the subsequent phase with different parameters and optimizer states. Their loss difference can therefore continue to evolve even though their explicit update rules are again identical. Evaluating an intervention when it is removed can consequently select a schedule that is inferior at the intended final training budget—or reject one that will eventually be beneficial.

papers.title: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
papers.abstract: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},\Sigma},U_n^\mathrm{\'et}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{\'et}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric \'etale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $\Sigma$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

papers.title: Stability theorems for $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets
papers.abstract:
We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $\eta$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $\eta\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $\eta$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant.
  Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.

papers.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
papers.abstract:
We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichm\"uller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous.
  Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

papers.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes
papers.abstract: Causal discovery promises to find which recorded variables drive a process target such as product quality, yield or energy use. Process data with known causes are rare, and in existing benchmarks the difficulty of identifying the causes of a target is either fixed by the recorded data or set for the whole graph. We present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes. Its generator is a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production, assembled from components that each model one phenomenon of process data, such as a control loop or a delayed effect. The graph is built around the target: without sensor error, every non-cause can be distinguished from the direct causes by conditioning on them or by time order. Each component is set independently, so the difficulty can be varied one condition at a time. We evaluate eight methods, from association measures to effect estimation, with an error analysis by the role of the selected candidate; all degrade as the difficulties combine, each in a way consistent with its assumptions.

papers.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.title: Safety Analysis of Parameterized Networks with Shared Counters
papers.abstract: We study networks with an unbounded number of processes sharing some natural counters that can be decremented, incremented and tested to zero. We look at two safety problems: the first one asks whether there is a network with an execution bringing a process in a given final state and the other one asks the execution to bring all the processes in the final state. In their full generality, these two problems are undecidable, but we show that decidability can be regained by either using a single counter or by forbidding the use of zero-tests (as it is is the case in Vector Addition Systems with States). For these decidable cases, we obtain low complexity results, the problems being solvable either in non-deterministic logarithmic space or in polynomial time.

papers.title: Linear Modeling of Hybrid Shipboard Power Systems under Pulsed Power Load Operation
papers.abstract: A model-based approach is a valuable tool in the power system design process, enabling the integration of component models and the evaluation of dynamic interactions. Simplified models support rapid preliminary assessments by allowing parameters and configurations to be adjusted. This paper investigates the effects of high-bandwidth loads in hybrid AC--DC shipboard power systems. The problem is addressed by developing a linear model aimed at capturing the relevant dynamics over the time scale of interest with reduced computational effort. A LVDC subsystem has been developed with a battery energy storage system that supports the grid during pulsed power load operation. A control strategy has been proposed to satisfy transient requirements. The proposed approach is validated under different pulsed power load conditions using a high-fidelity model developed in DIgSILENT PowerFactory, which preserves nonlinearities and includes converter switching effects and digital control implementation. The validation shows that the model captures the relevant transient behavior with significantly reduced simulation time, while maintaining acceptable accuracy, making it suitable for rapid preliminary design studies.

papers.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
papers.abstract: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM harness that selects among candidate routes on 659 five-minute windows; its best configuration recovers 79% of routes on test and 83% on few-shot, outperforming the best baseline on test and matching it on few-shot. Data and code at huggingface.co/datasets/HenryYHW/CANTraj and github.com/WangYuHang-cmd/GPS--CAN.

papers.title: $A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure
papers.abstract: Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$. At level $2$, we give explicit bracketing rules which make grounded partitions into affine crystal graphs of highest weights $2\Lambda_0$, $\Lambda_0+\Lambda_1$, and $2\Lambda_1$. We prove this by constructing explicit graph isomorphisms with the asymptotic model of Ariki and Mathas, whose vertices are Kleshchev multipartitions arising from Ariki-Koike algebras. Finally, we erase the $0$-arrows, which leaves the crystal graphs of the restrictions to the Levi subalgebra, and decompose them into finite strings. This decomposition gives new $q$-series identities at levels $1$ and $2$.

papers.title: Energy resolving optical transition-edge sensor approaching fundamental limits
papers.abstract: Transition-edge sensors (TES) have long held promise for exhibiting single-photon spectral resolution with near-unity detection efficiency, no read noise, and negligible dark counts. A TES detector capable of simultaneously achieving these traits could be revolutionary in fields including quantum computing, quantum sensing, biological imaging, and the detection of life on alien worlds by spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres. The applicability of optical TES detectors in these fields has been limited by energy resolution results that differ significantly from the theoretical expectations. We report significant enhancement of the single-photon energy resolution of tungsten (W) TESs by mitigation of athermal phonon loss during the photon-absorption energy down-conversion cascade. Implementing barriers to phonon loss dramatically increased the TES energy resolution (delta E). We achieve delta E of 34 meV - 61 meV, with resolving power (R = E/delta E) of 24 - 43, in a band spanning 1550 nm - 471 nm. All relevant electrical/thermal device parameters are explored in order to model theoretical limits to delta E imposed by noise, and provide an estimate of the athermal phonon trapping factor. Based on a simple model of electrical, thermal, and phonon escape noise sources, we estimate a phonon trapping factor approaching 90% for our best performing TES architecture. These results bring optical TES technology closer to theoretical predictions and to achieving the ambitious goals of photon-starved optical spectroscopy and fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.

papers.title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
papers.abstract: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schr\"odinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

papers.title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
papers.abstract: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast. Compared with conventional single-harmonic denoising using an autoencoder, the CHNN achieves superior noise suppression. These results demonstrate the potential of lower-harmonic signals for improving hyperspectral nano-FTIR imaging without increasing acquisition time.

papers.title: Emulating spatially extended systems using Fourier Neural Operator
papers.abstract: Operator Learning (OL) algorithms approximate underlying mathematical operators by mapping entire classes of input functions to their corresponding solutions. For instance, architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) have been trained on numerical datasets generated by isolated, stiff ionic models to provide a data-driven alternative to traditional numerical integration schemes. However, real-world biological and physical systems typically consist of interconnected spatial units arranged in complex, heterogeneous networks. Motivated by this observation, we generalize this data-driven framework to spatially extended systems defined on diverse graph topologies, ranging from Erdos-Renyi to Barabasi-Albert networks. Furthermore, we evaluate the proposed approach on empirical data, demonstrating its ability to accurately and efficiently model task-oriented neural activity.

authors.name: Duccio Fanelli
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Firenze

papers.title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
papers.abstract: We present NER-D, a cross-domain benchmark for German NER comprising 13 datasets spanning 9 domains, including General/Politics, Wikipedia, Legal, Medical, Historical, Financial, Agriculture and Archaeology. We examine the performance of both proprietary LLMs and state-of-the-art small open-source models using normal prompting and further examine the performance gains achievable via in-context learning and LoRA fine-tuning. Our results show that without any sort of optimization a proprietary model (GPT-5.4 mini) outperforms the smaller open-source models on 6 out of 13 datasets, but LoRA fine-tuning enables the smaller models to substantially outperform the proprietary baseline. We further analyze the influence of the domain and the tagset used in each task on the performance achieved in the different evaluation settings. Our benchmark will be available as a resource for the development of future German NER methods on both general and specialized domains.\footnote{We make our code, data, and models publicly available upon acceptance of this paper.

papers.title: Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
papers.abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.

papers.title: DesignSpecs: A DESIGN.md Dataset of Visual Design Specifications for AI Agents
papers.abstract: While AI agents increasingly generate and modify user interfaces, they rarely rely on a visual design specification for a certain project. The DESIGN.md format, which originated from Google's AI design tool Stitch and which was open-sourced in April 2026, addresses this gap by describing a visual identity through design tokens (such as named colors, text styles) and Markdown prose. To our knowledge, no large-scale research dataset of such design specification files exists. We present DesignSpecs, a dataset of 36,906 DESIGN.md files from 15,794 public, non-fork GitHub repositories, representing 17,240 unique file contents. We collected 613,207 files named DESIGN.md in October 2026. Because the same file name also denotes architectural plans and other design documents, we filtered those with YAML front matter, a design-system name, at least one recognized design token, and zero errors under the official linter. Our JSON Lines dataset provides file-level and deduplicated views of the original Markdown, links files to repositories, paths, and commits, and is released with related scripts. We outline research opportunities on visual design knowledge and design-aware AI agents. Dataset is available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jl-wei/DesignSpecs

papers.title: Riemannian geodesic motions and null foliations
papers.abstract: We study the non-collision problem: given a unit vector field $V$ on a complete Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, under what conditions on $V$ are the maps $F_t(p)=\exp_p(tV(p))$ injective for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$? If such a vector field exists, we call it a geodesic motion on $M$. This occurs, for instance, when $V$ defines a geodesic foliation of $M$, in which case, the geodesic motion is called stationary. We show that geodesic motions on the Euclidean plane are necessarily stationary, that generic geodesic motions on round spheres are non-stationary, and that compact hyperbolic $3$-manifolds admit no geodesic motions. The non-collision problem has a Lorentzian interpretation: geodesic motions on $M$ correspond to one-dimensional null geodesic foliations of the spacetime $(M\times\mathbb{R},g-dt^2)$. In the second part of the paper, we focus on codimension-one lightlike geodesic foliations of anti-de Sitter space $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,n}$. We give a complete characterization of such foliations by means of causal curves in the Einstein universe and prove rigidity in the projective anti-de Sitter case. The last part of the paper is dedicated to the study of one-dimensional geodesic foliations of $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,2}$. We give a complete characterization when the foliation contains at least one timelike leaf.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Sign: BiTE for Branch-Preserving Binary Threshold Expansion
papers.abstract: Binary neural networks (BNNs) reduce model storage and replace many arithmetic operations with efficient bitwise computations, but the single-sign activation limits their representational capacity. Each preactivation direction is compared with one threshold and reduced to one of two values, discarding variation within each sign region. We propose \textbf{BiTE} (Branch-Preserving Binary Threshold Expansion), which evaluates each feature direction against $K$ ordered thresholds and retains the resulting binary responses as separate inputs to the following learned operator. BiTE can distinguish up to $K+1$ ordered activation states while allowing the following operator to learn a separate transformation for each threshold response. It also enables a controllable trade-off between the number of independently constructed feature directions and the number of ordered responses extracted from each direction. On BinaryViT, BiTE improves mean final-epoch Top-1 accuracy from $74.60\pm0.30\%$ to $75.83\pm0.15\%$ on CIFAR-10 and from $42.80\pm0.46\%$ to $44.07\pm0.32\%$ on CIFAR-100, with nearly unchanged trainable parameter counts. A matched uniform-collapse control reaches $75.33\pm0.15\%$ on CIFAR-10, supporting the value of retaining the threshold responses separately relative to the evaluated scalar collapse. Binary VGG-16 experiments further show a favorable observed parameter--accuracy trade-off, including a configuration that achieves $0.64$ percentage points higher mean accuracy with $21.8\%$ fewer parameters than conventional width scaling. Overall, these results support branch-preserving threshold expansion as an effective way to improve binary representations and the observed parameter--accuracy trade-off.

papers.title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
papers.abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. In current discourse around ''world models,'' their attainment is framed as the achievement of internal consistency, cross-modal alignment, and physical grounding. Taken together, these demands converge on an ideal of the model as a universal translation machine capable of establishing lossless correspondences across linguistic, visual, and physical representation spaces. I show that this ideal presupposes a metaphysical commitment that I call a statistical ontology: the belief that reality has an underlying, computable statistical structure that can be recovered through sufficient data and modeling, rather than being shaped and accessed through situated human interpretation and labor. Tracing this commitment back to Warren Weaver's 1949 Memorandum on machine translation, I outline how translation was historically recast as code deciphering and, later, as the alignment of probability distributions across structured outputs. Finally, I contrast this paradigm with approaches in Translation Studies that foreground opacity, power asymmetries, and the translator's positionality. I argue that generative AI's statistical ontology is pre-Kantian, pre-critical and obscures the infrastructures and human labor that make machine translatability---as alignment---possible in the first place.

papers.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
papers.abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our results substantially expand the known phase space of cubic chiral semiconductors and may guide future efforts in the discovery and design of chiral materials.

papers.title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64
papers.abstract: DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It reconstructs CompCert C through nine reverse passes, combining deductively verified transformations with translation validation. Untrusted OCaml and Datalog analyses propose candidate reconstructions, while verified validators accept only candidates that satisfy the required semantic correspondence. The composed correctness theorem guarantees that every defined, safe behavior of an accepted C reconstruction is matched by the input CompCert assembly; under a safety assumption, the two programs are observationally equivalent. We evaluate DeCompCert on approximately 2.16 million lines of C. With exact function and call signatures, it reconstructs and recompiles all 3,173 eligible contexts under both unoptimized and optimized CompCert pipelines. Without retained signatures, its cumulative inference portfolio validates 2,606 of 3,164 contexts (82.4%), while the platform-plus-IDA configuration validates 2,407 contexts (76.1%). Native execution and output-quality experiments further evaluate the generated C and characterize the remaining limitations in signature recovery and source resemblance.

authors.name: Basavesh Ammanaghatta Shivakumar
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy

papers.title: Stratified Randomization Incorporating Historical Control Data
papers.abstract: Randomized controlled trials are often infeasible in rare diseases because of limited sample size, high costs, or lengthy durations. Hybrid control designs address this by combining a concurrent control arm with historical data. However, existing methods such as propensity score matching (PSM) borrow historical data only at the analysis stage, which limits power gains when covariate distributions differ between historical and concurrent data. We propose a stratified block randomization method for hybrid control trials. Within each stratum, more concurrent subjects are allocated to the treatment arm than to the concurrent control arm, and the difference is filled with historical controls so that the treatment and hybrid control arms are balanced 1:1; once the available historical controls in the stratum are used or a pre-specified overall cap is reached, allocation returns to 1:1. Historical controls are incorporated either by sampling or by weighting. We compared both methods with PSM in terms of type I error rate, power, and sample size via Monte Carlo simulations. The sampling method maintained the type I error rates when there was neither heterogeneity in the outcome model nor unmeasured covariates. It also had power comparable to or greater than that of PSM, particularly when historical controls were unevenly distributed across strata. The power of the weighting method increased with the pooled historical sample size, but its type I error rate was inflated when covariates beyond the stratification factors were present or when stratification factors were dichotomized from continuous covariates. The proposed method incorporates historical data at the allocation stage rather than only at the analysis stage, enabling more efficient use of historical data.

papers.title: Provable Cross-Modal Transfer of Hierarchical Concept Structure in CLIP Embeddings
papers.abstract: Contrastive vision-language models such as CLIP are trained to align images and text, not to represent taxonomies. Yet empirical studies show that CLIP embeddings exhibit hierarchical structure aligned with the hierarchy of semantic concepts. A theoretical characterization of why such hierarchy emerges from a non-hierarchical objective remains open. In this paper, we formalize this phenomenon as Hierarchical Angular Separation (HAS), a geometric property whereby each non-leaf concept embedding is more similar to its descendants than to off-branch concepts. Empirically, we show that HAS holds approximately in raw images and randomly initialized CLIP image embeddings, while in text embeddings it holds approximately only after contrastive learning. To theoretically explain this asymmetry, we analyze an unconstrained features model in which the image embeddings are fixed and only the text embeddings are trained. At the global minimizer, the text-side HAS violation percentage at each node is at most the image-side HAS violation and near-violation percentage. The key mechanism is the hierarchical co-occurrence structure of image-text pairs, which biases text embeddings toward root-centered image prototypes. For a linear contrastive loss, we derive a closed-form solution that makes this mechanism explicit. We extend the analysis to the InfoNCE loss and establish analogous guarantees under sufficient regularization. Synthetic experiments validate the theory and show that HAS is transferred even beyond the regimes covered by our analysis.

papers.title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass
papers.abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. We find a quantum efficiency of roughly 10 -- 40\% over this band, and fit these measurements to a quantum efficiency model constrained by these measurements and microscopy of the sensor layers. These measurements and the derived model informs this sensor's application within low-cost X-ray observatories, as well as motivates the development of commercial X-ray CMOS sensors without microlenses and deeper Si depletion layers.

papers.title: New Closed-Form Approximations in Statistical Mechanics Obtained by Symbolic Regression
papers.abstract:
Obtaining accurate and analytically tractable closed-form expressions for complex physical systems remains a fundamental challenge in statistical mechanics. In this work, we investigate three approximation problems in polymer statistical mechanics using two complementary symbolic regression frameworks: Deep Symbolic Optimization (DSO), based on reinforcement learning, and PyOperon, based on genetic programming with nonlinear least-squares constant optimization.
  First, for the force-extension relationship of the Worm-Like Chain (WLC) model, DSO achieves a maximum relative error below 0.15%, while PyOperon reduces it to 0.05%, outperforming the Marko-Siggia formula (approximately 17%) and the Petrosyan approximation. Second, for the logarithmic factorial, ln(n!), both frameworks recover the dominant structure of Stirling's formula directly from analytical data. Using residual learning on a continued-fraction expansion of the Stirling remainder, PyOperon reduces the maximum relative error by a factor of 1.3 x 10^4 compared with the most accurate of nine classical approximations for n in [1, 30]. Third, for the non-Gaussian radial probability density of the Freely Jointed Chain (FJC) model, physics-informed residual learning improves the approximation by factors of 11.2 over Darabi et al. (2023) and 4.6 over the steepest-descent approximation.
  The discovered expressions remain analytically tractable across all three applications. These results demonstrate the complementary capabilities of DSO and PyOperon for discovering accurate closed-form approximations in statistical and continuum mechanics.

authors.name: Alina Popova
authors.institution: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation

papers.title: Integrated Topology and Redispatch Optimization of Real-World Power Transmission Systems using Branch-and-Benders-Cut
papers.abstract: Transmission system operators can reduce congestion management costs by jointly optimizing network topology, generator redispatch, and transformer settings. The large number of switching decisions, detailed operational constraints, and security requirements under outages make this problem computationally demanding. We present a full mixed-integer linear programming formulation that combines line switching, substation reconfiguration, generator commitment and redispatch, and transformer settings with operational requirements. We solve the problem using an exact branch-and-Benders-cut algorithm. We integrate specialized subproblem solution methods, subproblem selection, cut filtering, partial decomposition, and techniques for enforcing network connectivity. A sequential switching heuristic provides initial solutions for the exact solve. An extensive computational study on 130 synthetic instances demonstrates substantial reductions in solution time compared with standard Benders decomposition and shows how heuristic warmstarting improves solution quality, especially when more switching actions are allowed. Results on real transmission networks illustrate how joint topology and redispatch decisions identify effective switching actions that sequential approaches can miss. Selected solutions generated by our approach were presented to system operators and subsequently checked using alternating current power flow calculations. All seven discussed solutions passed a first operator assessment, indicating the practical potential of the integrated approach.

papers.title: Composition of Near-Planar Infrastructure Network Instances with Certified Skewness Bounds
papers.abstract: Computational studies of optimization problems on infrastructure networks may require more suitable instances than are available. We propose a method to obtain additional instances by extracting and joining connected parts of existing networks, reusing their topology and parameters. Many infrastructure networks are near-planar, so added connections should preserve this property. We measure near-planarity by skewness, the minimum number of edges whose removal makes a graph planar. We derive bounds on the additional skewness caused by joining and give sufficient conditions under which none is added, and propose the corresponding strategy. We evaluate our approach on 100 sets of network parts extracted from each of PGLib-OPF and SNDlib. Within time limits, we show that no skewness is added for about half of the resulting power transmission networks and all considered telecommunication networks. Our method gives smaller mean upper bounds on added skewness than baselines that select vertices randomly, in order of decreasing degree, or using a Kamada--Kawai layout. Extraction and composition may also make the resulting optimization instances infeasible. To reduce this risk, we solve a simpler, tractable variant of the intended optimization problem during generation and restart if it is infeasible. On the generated instances, we solve security-constrained optimal transmission switching and survivable network design problems in full, demonstrating that the instances vary in computational difficulty with runtimes ranging from seconds to hours. The method thus extends the available benchmark sets with instances that inherit source data, have known skewness bounds, and cover a range of computational difficulty.

papers.title: Joint Optimization of Antenna Partitioning and Distortion-Aware Precoding for Massive MIMO-OFDM with Peak Cancellation and In-Band Distortion Compensation
papers.abstract: In massive MIMO-OFDM systems, peak cancellation (PC) reduces the peak-to-average power ratio but introduces in-band distortion, where compensation signals transmitted from a subset of antennas can suppress this distortion at the users. However, their effectiveness depends on the antenna partition and compensation precoder, while nonlinear power amplifiers (PAs) generate additional distortion. This paper proposes a joint optimization method for antenna partitioning and distortion-aware compensation precoding. To enable this joint optimization, we derive a covariance-based analytical model of PC and PA distortion to predict the per-user, per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plusdistortion- and-noise ratio (SIDNR). The predicted SIDNR is used to select the compensation precoder regularization, the disjoint antenna partition, and the number of compensation antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that joint optimization of the antenna partition and compensation precoder regularization improves BER and SIDNR-based spectral efficiency compared with fixed-partition designs, particularly at high signal-to-noise ratios.

papers.title: On the Same Track: Privacy Leaks in Electric Rail Transport via Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: Inertial sensors of smartphones are a well-known privacy risk, as they allow inferring sensitive user movements and activity without explicit permissions. Among these sensors, the magnetometer has received little attention, as it is assumed to measure mainly the Earth's magnetic field. In this paper, we show that electric trains generate distinctive magnetic fields that can be captured by a smartphone magnetometer. Apps deployed on the device can access these signals without user permission, enabling two novel attacks on passenger privacy: First, we are able to determine whether the user is riding an electric train (transport mode detection). Second, we can infer whether other victims are aboard the same train due to shared patterns in the magnetic field (colocation prediction). In an empirical evaluation across 217 train rides, we demonstrate that both attacks are effective, confirming a real-world threat. We discuss countermeasures and argue that magnetometer access should require explicit user permission in mobile operating systems.

authors.institution: Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data

authors.name: Pia Hanfeld
authors.institution: Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data

papers.title: What constrains the neutron-star crust? Present data, future measurements, and EOS doppelg\"angers
papers.abstract: The neutron-star crust plays a central role in pulsar glitches, thermal evolution, and stellar oscillations, yet its properties remain difficult to constrain. We use Bayesian inference with a unified crust-core equation of state to assess what present nuclear and astrophysical data tell us about the crust and what future stellar measurements can add. Within this model, present crust constraints are dominated by chiral effective field theory, with laboratory data providing additional information and current stellar observations having a smaller effect. The adopted theoretical bands determine how tightly the crust properties are constrained, while the treatment of neutron-rich surface energy affects their inferred values. Forecasts centred on a single reference equation of state show that more precise measurements of radius, tidal deformability, and total moment of inertia mainly constrain crust thickness. They provide little additional information about the crust-core transition, crust mass, or crustal moment of inertia and do not recover the precision lost when the chiral effective field theory constraint is removed. Two models with nearly identical global stellar observables can have crust masses and crustal moments of inertia differing by about a factor of two, yet remain indistinguishable at the assumed precision. Precise global measurements therefore need not uniquely determine the crust. Observations that directly probe the crust are needed to distinguish these models.

authors.name: Vishal Parmar
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Pisa

papers.title: Generative Design with Real-time Physics Explainability: Towards Product Definition in the Age of AI
papers.abstract: In this article, we explore opportunities from using generative AI in mechanical engineering. On the one hand, generative methods based on invertible neural networks have been recently proposed for the solution of inverse design problems, allowing to infer design parameters from performance labels. On the other hand, generative AI models have shown that they can act as real time capable surrogates for physics based simulations. Here we suggest that these two streams should be combined in a unified framework, where INN are used to control the design process from the customer requirements perspective and the generative simulation of the systems physics adds a layer of explainability, why the proposed design fulfils the requirements. As generative design is prone to hallucinations, we propose uncertainty quantification to fend off physically infeasible requests. Finally, validation with classical tools is a requirement for generative design process. To demonstrate the capabilities of our novel generative design paradigm, we develop two interactive environments, one for airfoil design based on simulator data and one for the combustor design space exploration based on measured data.

papers.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
papers.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

papers.title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.

papers.title: Hello Again: Exploiting Replay Protected Monotonic Counters to Brute-Force Windows Hello PINs
papers.abstract:
Windows Hello is the primary authentication mechanism on over one billion Windows 11 devices, supporting PINs as short as four digits. Such low-entropy PINs are viable only because the TPM's anti-hammering protection mitigates brute-force attacks. Most modern x86 platforms rely on firmware TPMs (fTPMs) that persist their non-volatile (NV) state, including the lockout state, to SPI flash. On newer platforms, rollback prevention of this state is delegated to the flash chip via Replay Protected Monotonic Counters (RPMCs), a JEDEC-standardized mechanism operating over a physically accessible bus.
  We present the first practical security analysis of RPMC in shipping x86 systems. Using low-cost interposer hardware, we identify multiple implementation flaws, two of which fundamentally undermine RPMC's security model: First, Winbond SPI flash - the leading NOR flash vendor with over 25% market share - leaks its HMAC key under voltage glitching, enabling arbitrary counter forgery. Second, AMD's NV controller does not verify RPMC increments, so an interposer can suppress them unnoticed. Moreover, AMD platforms without RPMC flash appear to lack NV rollback protection altogether: on two AMD desktops, reflashing an old image resets the fTPM's lockout counters.
  Both flaws enable rollbacks of the fTPM's NV state (AMD, Intel, or Pluton), including its lockout counters. We demonstrate this end-to-end on locked, encrypted hardware: our setup finds a 4-digit Windows Hello PIN in 40 hours instead of 69 days. A compromised PIN also grants access to device-bound keys and Hello-based enterprise SSO. The same primitive defeats BitLocker's TPM+PIN pre-boot protector, reducing the worst-case time for a default-length 6-digit PIN from 19 years to 20 days.

papers.title: Commercial AlGaAs diodes provide simplified feedback for adaptive femtosecond pulse compression
papers.abstract: Maintaining high peak power in ultrashort laser pulses is essential for efficient nonlinear interactions, particularly in multiphoton microscopy. Dispersion introduced by optical components broadens these pulses and degrades their peak power, thus motivating adaptive pulse compression guided by pulse-width-dependent feedback. However, the conventional second-harmonic generation feedback requires a nonlinear crystal, spectral filtering, and careful optical alignment. Here, we investigate commercially available AlGaAs laser and light-emitting diodes as alternative two-photon absorption feedback sensors. Their photocurrent exhibits a quadratic dependence on average optical power and inverse dependence on pulse duration, which is consistent with the analytical model predicting maximum response for the shortest, single-peaked pulse. Both devices generated a measurable photocurrent at sub-milliwatt average power levels and showed a weaker polarization dependence than second-harmonic-generation-based solution. All three feedback methods achieved comparable mean compressed pulse durations of 210-228 fs. These results demonstrate effective adaptive pulse compression with a substantially simpler feedback.

papers.title: Low-Temperature Heat Capacity of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Bundles with low dimensional gas systems
papers.abstract: Low-temperature heat-capacity data for pristine single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) bundles and for SWCNT/gas systems containing adsorbed Xe, Ne, N2, and CH4 were analyzed within a phenomenological framework. The data were fitted within the phenomenological form C(T) = C3T3 + C5T5, where the coefficients are interpreted as effective parameters of the coupled SWCNT-adsorbate excitation spectrum. Pristine SWCNT bundles exhibit a negative C5 coefficient, reflecting a non-Debye dispersive contribution associated with low-energy flexural-like modes. Gas adsorption systematically modifies both C3 and C5, indicating that the adsorbate's heat-capacity contribution may not be treated as fully independent. The Xe series suggests that mass loading, modified adsorbate-nanotube interaction, and changes in intertube coupling slightly reshape the nanotube vibrational response. Coverage-dependent measurements for Ne reveal a progressive shift from nanotube-dominated excitations toward domination of additional low-energy adsorbate modes in the phonon spectrum of the SWCNT-Ne system, while molecular adsorbates (N2, CH4) introduce translational, librational, orientational, and rotational degrees of freedom that generate correspondingly stronger perturbations.

papers.title: Squared Bessel particle systems with weak repulsion
papers.abstract: We study squared Bessel particle systems with repulsion parameter $\kappa>0$ and dimension parameter $\delta\in\mathbb R$. We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $\delta$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<\kappa<1$ and do not occur for $\kappa\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<\kappa<1$.

papers.title: Roton softening and crystallization in a mass-asymmetric electron-hole bilayer
papers.abstract: Whether roton softening drives a continuous transition into a density-ordered or supersolid state is a longstanding question in interacting quantum fluids. Here, we address this microscopically in a mass-asymmetric electron--hole bilayer in which exciton condensation competes with interaction-driven crystallization. Using self-consistent Hartree--Fock--Bogoliubov theory and its time-dependent extension, we show that increasing the carrier-mass ratio or interlayer distance induces a pronounced roton minimum in the homogeneous exciton condensate liquid. The system undergoes a first-order transition to a crystalline state, preempting the roton instability. In this metastable regime, strongly interacting holes first drive the crystallization of the itinerant electrons, and the system then evolves into a hole-crystal--electron-metal phase at larger interlayer distance. Supersolid solutions with coexisting interlayer coherence and charge density order are also found to be energetically competitive near the crystallization boundary. We further discuss our findings based on recent experimental setups in two-dimensional material heterostructures.

papers.title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
papers.abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $\epsilon$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $\epsilon$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $\epsilon$| ln(N/$\epsilon$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

papers.title: Efficient Poincar\'e Convolutions through Patch-Statistics Factorization
papers.abstract: Published implementations of the Poincar\'e convolution in Hyperbolic Neural Networks++ (HNN++) map every overlapping image patch to the Poincar\'e ball before evaluating its score. We show that the clipped score depends on each patch only through two statistics, its squared norm and its inner products with the filters, which a native convolution and a single-channel box filter compute directly. The factorized layer therefore evaluates the specified score exactly, without constructing ball-valued patches, and its single-precision outputs and gradients agree with double-precision evaluations at least as closely as those of the explicit reference. On an RTX A6000 under two versions of JAX, complete training updates of a Poincar\'e U-Net and a Poincar\'e ResNet-20 are 1.5 to 1.8 times faster than the faster of two explicit implementations that map patches to the ball (1.2 to 1.4 times against an explicit implementation that skips this mapping); on a V100, the gain over the gather-based one persists as the ResNet-20 is widened eightfold. In 15 paired training runs per task, updates are 2.0 and 1.8 times faster than a reference that follows the published execution order, with no consistent change in final segmentation or classification quality, and peak memory falls by 38 to 55% in a U-Net scaling study. Replacing the convolutions of the official PyTorch Hyperbolic U-Net makes its training step 1.4 times faster with half the memory. Evaluating an existing layer from its patch statistics thus makes Poincar\'e convolutional networks cheaper to train in the tested models and software stacks.

papers.title: Characterization of the GIGAPYX-4600 CMOS visible image sensor in the context of high precision astrometry
papers.abstract: To evaluate the potential of detectors for next-generation space astrometry missions such as the HWO and Theia, an extensive analysis of the performance of the GIGAPYX-4600 46-megapixel CMOS detector from Pyxalis was conducted at IPAG. The 5456x8320-pixel detector, featuring a 4.4-micron pitch and back-side illumination, constitutes a matrix of 24x36 mm. It has a measured gain of 13.3 electrons per ADU in low-gain mode. The saturation level of the detector in low-gain-mode is estimated to be approximately 52 000 electrons. This sensor demonstrates linearity errors of 0.90%, pixel response non-uniformity of less than 1.3%, and readout and quantization noise of 12 electrons in low-gain mode. Dark current was measured at 35 electrons per second at 35{\textdegree}C and inter-pixel capacitance remained under 3%. We demonstrated that inter-pixel capacitance effects can be effectively mitigated using spatially varying kernel correction algorithms. Radiation tests confirmed its robustness against protons and heavy ions, and no latch-up was observed. These measurements agree with the manufacturer figures. These characterization results validate the GIGAPYX-4600 as a strong candidate for high-precision astrometry. Further improvements are currently being developed for space implementation.

papers.title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions. To evaluate the framework, teleoperators intervened across three SDL fault scenarios. In the first study, comparative trials showed that the decoupled controller was associated with shorter completion times and reduced rotational motion. In a second study, teleoperators performed an aiming task with and without reference-path guidance. Users were more target-driven and risk-tolerant without guidance but showed behavioral differences under different guidance strategies. These findings suggest that controller configuration and reference-path design influence operator performance during SDL fault recovery, informing teleoperation interface optimization. This work demonstrates the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving. These findings also provide a foundation for future studies in shared autonomy and semi-autonomous intervention.

papers.title: Reconciling global and local spin models
papers.abstract: Magnetic interactions based on first-principles calculations can be casted either into global spin models, where the interactions are configuration-independent, or into local spin models, where the effective parameters depend explicitly on the underlying spin configuration. Although these two perspectives often yield seemingly inconsistent results, we demonstrate that they can be reconciled by restricting the analysis to transverse spin fluctuations. We develop a projection scheme that systematically removes spurious longitudinal contributions from local interaction matrices, thereby establishing a rigorous connection between the projected local interactions and the underlying global multispin Hamiltonian. Applying our approach to the prototype systems (i) a Cr trimer on Au(111) (ii) Fe and Cr dimers on Cu(001), we show that the projected local interaction parameters quantitatively reproduce those obtained from the global four-spin model. This work provides a unified framework to interpret local and global spin models on equal footing and resolves long-standing ambiguities in the identification of effective interactions such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in a non-collinear framework.

papers.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Space-Filling Input Design for Nonlinear System Identification
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to space-filling input design for nonlinear system identification, in which an agent learns a control policy that actively drives the system to explore its state space. Classical input design, developed mainly for linear models, minimises the covariance of the estimated parameters. For nonlinear black-box models, however, the dominant error is the bias induced by the model structure over the region of interest, which motivates space-filling strategies that seek to cover the system state space. Existing space-filling approaches rely on predefined input signal classes and require solving explicit optimisation problems. Unlike these methods, the proposed approach requires no input class to be selected and no frequency band to be tuned for the system at hand, satisfies an amplitude bound by construction, and adapts to varying initial conditions through its observation-based policy without re-optimisation. The learned excitation signals exhibit physically meaningful behaviours, such as resonance excitation and amplitude modulation. The approach is evaluated against tuned swept sine and crest-factor-optimised multisine excitations, and against a state-of-the-art space-filling multisine design, on two nonlinear benchmark systems: a mass-spring-damper with nonlinear stiffness and a Van der Pol oscillator. Under the same amplitude bound, the learned policy achieves the best overall space-filling performance on both systems and distributes its samples more uniformly than the state-of-the-art design.

papers.title: How rigid is maximum cardinality search? Stability and locality of MCS orderings under edge updates, verified in Lean
papers.abstract: For which sets F of edge modifications do a graph G and the modified graph share a maximum cardinality search (MCS) ordering? We prove that they do whenever, along every proper common MCS prefix, each unchosen vertex's neighbour count in the second graph exceeds its count in the first by zero or one. In particular, inserting or deleting any matching, or flipping a single edge, preserves a common ordering, and under the same hypothesis every common MCS prefix extends to a full common ordering without backtracking. Neither part of the hypothesis can simply be dropped: inserting a triangle, a P_4 or a 2P_3 shows that the +1 bound cannot be relaxed to +2, and a disjoint mixed insert/delete pair shows that the one-directional condition is needed. For the canonical ordering (smallest-index tie-breaking) under a single-edge update, an insertion can first change the ordering only strictly between the endpoints' positions, and a deletion only at the later endpoint; when no break fires, the ordering is unchanged. A boolean-adjacency executable refines the abstract probe-then-repair update. All of these results, including the four obstructions, are proved in Lean 4 over Mathlib, re-checked by independent kernel checkers, and registered in the Palomar registry. On paper we further show that the first break of an insertion is located in O((deg(v)+1) log n) time, independent of the window length. We claim no worst-case asymptotic speedup over recomputation.

papers.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
papers.abstract: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.

papers.title: From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
papers.abstract: Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices. We show that, while equivalent matrices have isomorphic associated graphs, the converse can fail for Butson matrices. We prove that a character decomposition determines the graph spectrum from the singular values of entrywise powers. For prime phase, we also observe that the spectrum depends only on the order and phase; for composite phase, a switching preserving the Butson property can change it. We show that Orrick's closed-quadruple and Hall-set switchings correspond to Wang-Qiu-Hu switching, up to graph isomorphism. Going in the other direction, we characterise when the Godsil-McKay and Wang-Qiu-Hu reflections preserve the Butson property and give phase-multiplicity conditions for the corresponding graph switchings. Finally we also relate block switching to cyclic graph switching under a phase-balance condition, automatic at prime phase. These results provide a basis for transferring tools and techniques between matrix switching and graph switching.

papers.title: TReC: Evaluating Move-Induced State Changes in Instruction-Conditioned Go
papers.abstract: When a Go model predicts a move different from the expert's, coordinate distance measures how far the prediction lands from the reference. We introduce Transition Representation Consistency (TReC) to compare how the two moves change a board-state embedding. Both moves are executed from the same position under the game rules, and TReC is the cosine similarity between the two resulting representation changes. In experiments with a frozen KataGo network on 680 mid-to-late-game positions from five games, the gap between the highest and lowest candidate per position has a median of 0.01 to 0.08 for the direct successor-state cosine and 0.88 to 1.33 for TReC, depending on the evaluator layer. TReC follows coordinate distance only weakly: the rank correlation between a candidate's distance to the reference and its TReC, computed within each position, has a median of -0.19 over these positions.

papers.title: Contrastive latent representation learning with denoising score matching
papers.abstract: Contrastive representation learning methods operate by pulling different views of the same data sample together while pushing them away from views of different samples. A fundamental challenge is the estimation of the repulsive force, which typically requires large batch sizes, can exhibit high variance, and is susceptible to the curse of dimensionality. We introduce ScoreCLR, a contrastive representation learning method that offers a novel way to estimate this repulsion term. We consider the framework of representation learning by maximizing the mutual information between two latent views of a sample. By deriving the gradient of the Shannon entropy with respect to the encoder parameters, we obtain an equivalent objective that involves the score of the latent representation. We then use denoising score matching techniques to estimate this score with a lightweight network that is trained jointly with the encoder. We further propose regularization techniques using different noise levels and a Gaussian prior on the latent representation. ScoreCLR replaces the batch of explicit negative samples in contrastive methods with a learned repulsion whose cost is linear in the batch size rather than quadratic. On CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100 it does so with minimal loss of linear-probe accuracy compared to SimCLR under a shared recipe, while producing projector outputs of higher effective rank, closer to the Gaussian prior.

papers.title: A Cantilever-Based Method for Probing Adhesion Force and Kinetic Detachment Energy in Cohesive Granular Materials
papers.abstract: Interparticle adhesion plays a critical role in the flow behavior of cohesive granular materials, yet quantitative characterization at the particle scale remains challenging. Here, we present a cantilever-based method that combines a glass-beam cantilever for force measurements with a novel catapult mode for energy measurements, enabling the determination of both quasi-static detachment force and kinetic detachment energy. Applied to three different cohesive materials: polymer-coated silica particles, wet granular media, and cross-linked poly(2-ethylhexyl acrylate) (PEHA) microparticles, this method reveals a fundamental decoupling between force and energy, suggesting that both quantities are equally critical for characterizing grain properties.

papers.title: An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.
