papers.title: I2C-GRPO: Insight Importance Checklist for Reinforcement Learning in a Multi-Agent DDoS Alert Triage Workflow
papers.abstract:
Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used for investigative tasks over incomplete evidence, such as cybersecurity alert triage, but reinforcement learning (RL) for such tasks is difficult: intermediate steps have no verifiable labels, rollouts are costly, and outcome rewards are sparse. We propose Insight Importance Checklist (I2C)-GRPO, a checklist reward for intermediate investigation steps. For each decision point, a panel of expert LLMs proposes investigative actions, their atomic forensic insights are extracted, and a separate three-model ranker panel orders the insights by importance. A reward model checks which ranked insights a candidate action targets and returns their consensus-weighted coverage. Because actions are scored without being executed, the reward is a proxy for expected investigative value, and training reduces to a one-step contextual bandit over fixed investigation prefixes. From a soft-computing perspective, the reward is an additive fuzzy measure whose rank-exponent weights act as an ordered weighted averaging (OWA)-type operator; one exponent sets its orness, i.e., how strongly the reward concentrates on the top of the judges' consensus.
  We train an open-weight Qwen3-4B Triage Agent within a fixed multi-agent Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) alert-triage workflow on DARPA 2000 LLDOS 1.0 and test it on an independent CSE-CIC-IDS2018 DDoS trace. Across three training seeds, the agent reaches a mean F1-score of 0.869, 5.9 and 9.7 points above uniform insight weights and DIVA, and a false-positive rate of 4.9% versus 16.4% for GPT-5-mini. Within the weighting family, false positives fall only at the highest-orness weighting evaluated. All claims are limited to DDoS alert triage; the code, task contexts, and ranked insight dataset will be released.

papers.title: A Tumour-Aware Multimodal Framework for Explainable Prediction of IDH Mutation in Gliomas from Multi-Sequence MRI
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status is essential for glioma diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. Although recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated promising performance, many rely on whole-brain feature extraction and provide limited interpretability. This study proposes a tumour-aware multimodal framework for explainable, non-invasive prediction of IDH mutation status from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The proposed framework integrates four MRI sequences (T1, T1CE, T2, and FLAIR), tumour subregion segmentation, quantitative radiomic descriptors, and clinical information within a unified deep learning architecture. An ablation study was conducted to evaluate the contribution of tumour-aware learning, radiomic features, and clinical variables. Model performance was assessed using multiple complementary evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, balanced accuracy, receiver operating characteristic analysis, confusion matrix evaluation, and Grad-CAM visualisation. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed multimodal framework consistently outperformed the baseline MRI-only model, with the Clinical Fusion model achieving the strongest overall predictive performance. The integration of tumour-aware learning, radiomic descriptors, and clinical information progressively improved classification performance, while Grad-CAM visualisations indicated that the model predominantly focused on biologically relevant tumour regions. These findings suggest that tumour-aware multimodal feature integration enables accurate, interpretable, and non-invasive molecular profiling of gliomas and provides a promising foundation for future clinical decision support in precision neuro-oncology.

papers.title: Eleven Trans-Neptunian Objects and Eight Candidates Discovered by TESS
papers.abstract: We report a blind search for trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) in Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) full-frame images from 2018 July 25 through 2026 November 6. We search 572 CCD fields near the ecliptic across 95 TESS sectors. After modeling and subtracting Gaia stars with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve package, we stack the residuals along curved trial paths and link detections across sectors. We identify eleven new TNOs, each detected blindly in two to five TESS sectors and independently in archival ground-based images, with arcs of 2-20 years. They have V = 20.8-22.1, heliocentric distances of 25-57 au, inclinations of 16-27 deg, and diameters of about 120-910 km for an assumed albedo of 0.08. They lie 9-26 deg from the ecliptic, and the largest is 5 deg from the Galactic plane. Eight additional objects linked across two or three TESS sectors lack secure independent recovery in the archives examined and remain candidates. The search recovers 314 known TNOs and Centaurs, with an empirical recovery fraction of 50% at V = 21.6 before quality cuts. Nine were discovered after TESS imaged them, including 2026 ED138 6.8 years before its discovery by Rubin. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of TESS for finding bright outer Solar System objects and extending their observational arcs.

papers.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
papers.abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_{\omega}$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_{\omega}$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.

papers.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
papers.abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.

papers.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
papers.abstract: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically. This survey introduces a unified formalism that describes every QGNN as an encoder, a graph-conditioned circuit, observables, and an optional classical head, together with a circuit-level condition for permutation equivariance and a resource model for comparing costs. We organize the literature into five architecture families (convolutional, equivariant, message-passing and recurrent, Hamiltonian, and hybrid) and compare them by qubit cost, symmetry, scalability, and evidence. We then review symmetry and geometric inductive biases (permutation, rotation, and Lorentz), the results on expressivity, trainability, noise, and scalability, and applications in high-energy physics, chemistry, finance, healthcare, earth observation, and transportation. An audit of datasets and evaluation practices leads to a minimum reporting protocol. Our main finding is that the design space is rich and symmetry is the best-supported inductive bias, whereas the evidence remains thin: results are mostly simulated, on small graphs, at parity with classical models or with fewer parameters, and no advantage has yet been established on tasks over classical graph data. We identify five open challenges and a research agenda covering provable advantage, equivariant and geometric designs, fault-tolerant implementations, and shared benchmarks. The coverage extends through 2026 and emphasizes recent work.

papers.title: PTMTD: A Topology-Aware Temporal-Graph Attention Network for Joint Cyber-Attack Detection and Relay-Level Localization in Power System Protection Networks
papers.abstract: The digitization of protection relays exposes power grids to sophisticated cyberattacks, yet existing GNN detectors omit temporal encoding, rely on static topologies, and lack relay localization. We propose PTMTD-a Pearson-driven Temporal Multimodal Topology-aware Detection Network-coupling a dilated TCN with multi-head GATv2 in a dual-head architecture for simultaneous 37-class detection and four-relay localization. PTMTD constructs its graph from measurement correlations (no impedance data) and is trained with a composite loss jointly optimizing both tasks. On the MSU-ORNL benchmark (78,377 samples, 37 classes), it achieves 99.27% accuracy, 99.25% macro F1, and 95.98% localization, outperforming GraphKAN, LSTM, GCN, and Random Forest by 5.64-11.15 percentage points (p < 0.05). Ablations confirm gains from temporal encoding (+2.38%), graph attention (+2.69%), residuals (+2.07%), and correlation-driven supervision. With 639k parameters and 2.5 ms CPU inference, PTMTD is lightweight and deployment-ready. While validated on a transmission testbed, the architecture applies to microgrids with similar relay structures. Code and models are publicly available.

papers.title: General $\delta N$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
papers.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $\delta N$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

papers.title: Data-Driven Sparse Identification and Robust Tube-Based Predictive Control for Multivariable Chaotic Systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the data-driven synchronization and robust control of multivariable chaotic systems subject to strict actuation constraints, modeling uncertainties and bounded input disturbances. Using empirical data collected from a four-dimensional chaotic Rossler response system, Sequentially Thresholded Least Squares (STLSQ) sparse regression is employed to recover a nominal control-affine model, achieving an identification accuracy of R^2 = 1.0000 across all channels with root-mean-square error within [4.15e-6, 8.33e-4]. To establish a mathematically rigorous bridge between data-driven identification and robust synthesis, all structural discrepancies in the drift vector field and input matrix are unified into a single lumped uncertainty field delta(x,u). A computable scalar bound delta_bar is established based on library truncation error, regression residuals, input bounds, and Lipschitz constants (Lemma 1). We subsequently prove that input-output feedback linearization maps delta(x,u) into a state- and control-dependent additive disturbance d(z,nu) in Brunovsky canonical coordinates, bounded by ||d(z,nu)||_2 <= alpha_1 delta_bar + alpha_2 delta_bar ||nu||_2 with closed-form expressions for alpha_1 and alpha_2 (Theorem 1). This certified bound, together with a bounded input disturbance and a zero-order-hold margin, yields a compact disturbance set that seeds a robust tube-based model predictive controller. We prove that the resulting tightened quadratic program is recursively feasible, that the physical actuator limit (|u_i| <= 1100) remains inactive under an explicit sufficient condition, and that the closed-loop tracking error is Input-to-State Stable (ISS) with an asymptotic gain that is linear in delta_bar plus a term due to the exogenous input disturbance (Theorems 2 and 3).

papers.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
papers.abstract: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. Nominal results include 41.711 microwatts biased neuron-core power, 3.338-pJ positive terminal energy for a 1.4-microsecond cell read, and 0.531-mV selected-state drift over a 5-ms extracted-tile hold. Commit and coupling errors are reported separately. The software checkpoint records 27.976% mean intersection-over-union on a held-out six-class DSEC split; this is not hardware accuracy. Component layouts and simulation evidence quantify local implementation costs and expose storage replication and service scheduling as scaling constraints. A detailed SPICE-calibrated behavioral forward simulation of one full-resolution DSEC frame achieves 24.26% mean intersection-over-union, versus 26.22% for the matched PyTorch reference, using a compact 5-fF bank variant and external count/voltage calibration. Physical full-network operation, system energy and mismatch robustness remain unverified.

papers.title: Multiplicity of Positive Solutions for Singular Anisotropic Elliptic Equations with Variable Exponents
papers.abstract: We study anisotropic elliptic Dirichlet problems with variable exponents, singular nonlinearities, and subcritical superlinear reactions. Our contribution is a direct variational construction that combines Nehari geometry and fibering maps without requiring global differentiability of the singular energy, and the result establishes the existence of two positive weak solutions for sufficiently small \(\lambda\), distinguished by their energy signs.

This feature leads to nonlinear elliptic equations with nonstandard growth. Variable-exponent Lebesgue and Sobolev spaces provide a natural functional framework for these models, allowing the growth of the underlying energy to vary from point to point; see [9, 7].

papers.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
papers.abstract: Modern power systems are undergoing a huge shift in generation mix, including inverter-based resources that are fundamentally changing the stability dynamics of the grid. Thus, synchronous Generators (SG) are gradually being displaced by Grid-forming inverters (GFM) that are proposed as a solution to continue supporting grid stability. However, the effect of GFM placement in the network on frequency performance and how well aggregate-frequency assessment captures placement sensitivity observed in local frequency metrics remains unclear. This paper evaluates all SG and droop-controlled GFM assignments in the IEEE 39-bus system. A reduced-order model is used for the exhaustive search with load disturbances applied separately at every eligible load bus while considering nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) derived from both device rating weighted aggregate frequency and local bus frequencies. Results reveal that at fixed GFM penetration, placement produced up to 104 mHz variation in worst-case local nadir and 0.21 Hz/s in maximum local RoCoF. Aggregate-frequency assessment reduced the apparent across placements by 89\% for nadir and 88\% for RoCoF at 50\% GFM penetration. These results indicate that aggregate-frequency assessment alone may obscure favorable or adverse placement effects on local frequency performance.

papers.title: Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
papers.abstract: Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $\rho=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.

papers.title: DiffusionSSD: Achieving Extreme Visual Compression with Dual-stage Diffusion and Cross-level Near-Data Processing
papers.abstract:
Growing visual data overwhelms storage on resource-constrained edge devices, making compression essential. Traditional codecs offer inadequate rate-distortion performance, motivating the exploration of diffusion codecs. Diffusion codecs face two limitations: (1) At the algorithm level, diffusion decoders preserve perceptual quality under extreme compression, but require substantial computation. (2) At the architecture level, in NPU-centered devices, neural codecs occupy the NPU, interfering with other AI applications. Meanwhile, the complex codec pipeline incurs long I/O paths, leading to additional overhead and energy cost.
  To address these issues, we propose DiffusionSSD, a cross-level near-data processing framework for extreme visual data compression on edge devices, using an algorithm-architecture co-design method. Specifically, (1) at algorithm level, we present Dual-stage Diffusion, a lightweight solution tailored for diffusion codecs that employs patchification and single-step diffusion, reducing computation cost while preserving perceptual quality; (2) at architecture level, we introduce a Cross-level Near Data Processing architecture that integrates the proposed computational universal flash storage (cUFS) and LPDDR-PIM, enabling codecs to be entirely offloaded to data side while reducing visual-data movement and avoiding SoC redesign; (3) at system level, combining both the algorithm and the underlying architecture, we propose a Patch-Workload co-aware scheduling scheme to enable more efficient system-level execution. Experiments show that Dual-stage Diffusion maintains comparable perceptual quality while reducing computation cost by up to 92.7%. Compared with NPU+DRAM and near-data-processing design such as SmartSSD, cUFS+PIM improves coding throughput by 2.32 times and 2.91 times on average, respectively.

papers.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
papers.abstract: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compared MP-20 baselines (63.24%), while same backbone comparisons show improved structure recovery over coordinate-based ordering. Furthermore, we demonstrate property-conditioned inverse design for wide-bandgap semiconductors, where ESG achieves a much higher stable, unique and novel (S.U.N.) rate and stronger target-property alignment than the coordinate-based baseline. These results establish topology-guided sequence construction as an effective route to improving crystal generation and property-directed design at fixed model capacity.
