papers.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
papers.abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs up to 32 candidate plans, and chooses an answer using a trained validator. On its own, LuthorSQL reaches 68.03% execution accuracy on BIRD's hidden test set at 0.84 s per question on a single GPU, maintains its accuracy in 9 GB with 8-bit quantized weights, and transfers zero-shot to Snowflake, BigQuery, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB within 3.1 points of its native SQLite accuracy. Combined with Claude Opus 5.5 in a pre-registered confidence cascade over 227 questions on databases published after Opus's training cutoff, LuthorSQL answers nearly half of all questions locally and cuts API cost by 33.3% at the same accuracy. Finally, contamination probing shows that Opus reproduces 48-92% of public benchmark gold queries verbatim without seeing the schema; however, its tool-assisted accuracy holds on renamed schemas and reaches 95.6-97.4% on post-cutoff databases. Code and data: https://github.com/IAMIbrahimmemon/luthorsql

papers.title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
papers.abstract: This paper presents a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (CARL) controller for battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and photovoltaic (PV) ramp-rate smoothing. Rapid PV power fluctuations caused by cloud transitions can introduce operational and stability challenges in power systems. To mitigate these impacts, grid codes impose ramp-rate limits (RRL) on PV power injected to the grid. BESSs can support such grid codes by absorbing or supplying power during rapid variations. However, the extent to which BESSs can reduce PV-induced variability depends on (i) the BESS power and energy capacities; and (ii) the adopted controller. Thus, BESS sizing and controller design are coupled. Conventional moving-average control can increase battery usage due to filter-induced lag, while ramp-rate control is reactive and does not account for the long-term impact of actions on battery state of charge and future ramp events. Optimization-based methods can reduce BESS requirements by anticipating future PV variations, but their performance depends on accurate PV forecasts. To address these limitations, the CARL controller learns a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment. Ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints are incorporated into a causal feasibility interval that guarantees feasible actions by definition. A full-horizon input-convex neural network (ICNN)-based optimization is developed as a noncausal benchmark for the minimum achievable BESS requirements. Evaluation using three real-world PV datasets shows that, at a 10\%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduces peak BESS power by 8.7--10.4\% and energy capacity by 47.5--62.6\% relative to conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining the grid-codes compliance.

papers.title: The M\"obius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
papers.abstract: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular M\"obius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the M\"obius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the M\"obius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
papers.abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical features, calorimeter images, and longitudinal shower sequences. Models that follow the longitudinal development of the shower reach the highest accuracy, which points to the value of physically informed representations. The hybrid QLSTM gives the lowest reconstruction error, with an RMSE of 0.294 GeV. Under matched-data conditions with only 1,500 training events, the QLSTM improves on the classical LSTM by 52.7% and also surpasses an LSTM trained on the full set. These observations indicate that longitudinal representations are central to calorimeter energy reconstruction and give preliminary evidence that hybrid quantum-classical sequence models can be more sample-efficient for regression in high-energy physics.

authors.name: Alfredo Raya
authors.institution: Universidad Michoacana de San Nicolás de Hidalgo

papers.title: Fair and Efficient Distributed EV Charging Coordination Using Threshold Cryptography and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Distributed coordination of electric vehicle (EV) charging with the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) keeps EV constraints private but assumes that every participant follows the algorithm. This assumption fails in practice, where a biased operator or a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker can send inconsistent signals to different EVs, and compromised EVs can deviate from their prescribed updates. We first prove that attacks by such arbitrarily malicious, i.e., Byzantine, participants do not prevent convergence and therefore remain undetected, and derive the most damaging attack in closed form. We then propose a framework that combines a threshold-signed broadcast with upload recomputation, which detects every deviation without false alarms at linear instead of quadratic communication cost. To keep the optimization running, each affected EV recovers locally with a certified, fleet-aware machine learning price forecast, and we prove that the optimization remains convergent with a recovery cost bounded by the shape of the forecast error. Simulation results with real-world load, price, and charging data show that a biased operator raises the annual cost of disadvantaged EVs by 132.7% and lowers that of advantaged EVs by 49.3% without changing the aggregate load, whereas the defense limits all cost changes to 2.6%. An external MITM attacker raises the cost of its victims by 57.6%, the peak load by 5.8%, and the grid cost by 15.8%, whereas the defense keeps them within 1.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% of benign operation. With up to 70% of the EVs attacked, the recovery converges in at least 97.8% of the runs.

papers.title: PerfArena: Ranking LLMs by Code Performance
papers.abstract: Industry now relies on LLMs to write a large share of production code. Although that code is mostly, but not always, correct, correctness alone does not determine whether it is fit for repeated and extensive use, which depends on what the code costs in time, memory and energy. Most code-generation benchmarks nonetheless evaluate correctness in isolation, and most performance-oriented benchmarks cover few languages and rarely measure energy consumption. To address this gap, we present PERFARENA, an open-source, reproducible arena that ranks LLMs by the performance of their generated code across multiple languages and competitions. PERFARENA executes the solutions of each LLM on a Unix-like host and reports correctness together with latency, peak memory, and energy consumption. Correctness oracles, performance oracles, profilers, and code-generation workflows are pluggable in PERFARENA, enabling the integration of new judging backends and measurement tools without changing the pipeline. We evaluate PERFARENA on two competitions: CLBGComp, 10 compute-intensive benchmarks from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game, and LeetCodeComp, 99 LeetCode problems whose accepted solutions differ measurably in latency. Currently, PERFARENA holds 9,455 correct and measured solutions from 13 state-of-the-art LLMs across 7 programming languages. Across both competitions, got-6-astra is the only LLM that no other LLM beats significantly in latency, energy consumption, or peak memory, solving 99.7% of LeetCodeComp and 100% of CLBGComp. All PERFARENA leaderboards and measured solutions are publicly available, providing a continuously updated reference that helps developers choose an LLM per language and metric, instead of relying only on correctness rates or pricing.

papers.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
papers.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

authors.name: Shijian Lu
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Ming Yang
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AI and the Two Margins of Work: Why Job Losses Show Up Before Job Creation
papers.abstract: Technological change acts on labor demand at two margins: adjustment within established activities and the creation of additional activities, often by new firms. Payroll statistics record the first promptly and the second late. In the computing era, firms that entered in 1978 or later held 42 percent of payroll by 1998 and entering cohorts kept about 80 percent of their payroll after five years; in the industries most exposed to automation, incumbents contracted before entrants accumulated, a sequence that is precise early in the period and suggestive by its end. We develop a model in which one AI capability lowers the full cost of acceptable output in existing production and makes additional projects worth attempting, with founder effort separate from hired hours. If operating products re-scale instantly, automation displaces no aggregate hours; if they take time, hours fall first and recover as incumbents re-expand and new products arrive, with the long-run sign set by income effects. Establishment job flows through the first quarter of 2026 show no gradient on language-model exposure on either margin, which is what the model predicts under the observed adoption path and also what no effect on payroll would look like; studies with founding-task exposure find entry rising 10 to 20 percent. We propose a net reinstatement ratio and show that statistics which record new work late overstate displacement for years.

authors.name: Mark Esposito
authors.institution: Mohammed Bin Rashid School of Government

papers.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
papers.abstract: Answer continuation often returns a diagnosis already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning. We study this behavior in MamaReason, adapted from dense Gemma 4 31B, on MamaBench's 217 paired maternal and child-health presentations. An explicit-commitment extractor identifies a diagnosis in 75 of 94 failed RL first passes and 75 of 93 failed SFT first passes. The continuation matches that diagnosis in 67/75 RL cases and 58/75 SFT cases, using diagnosis strings alone. Reading these commitments without additional generation recovers 30 of the 40 RL pairs restored by continuation under the archived correctness labels. Recurrence controls distinguish routine mentions from repeated answer selection. An offline second-commitment trigger measures the tradeoff between earlier readout and paired accuracy. The resulting decomposition separates diagnostic content already present in a trace, completion of an accepted answer, and paired diagnostic correctness. For clinical language-model evaluation, these are distinct outcomes that become visible when the same reasoning trace is examined through multiple readouts.

papers.title: Dualizing involutions on Kazhdan-Patterson covers of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(r,F).$ Let $r,n \geq 2$ and $\widetilde{G}$ be an $n$-fold Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $G$. Let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth representation of $G$ and $\pi^{\vee}$ be the contragredient of $\pi$. Let $\tau$ be an involutive anti-automorphism of $G$ satisfying $\pi^{\tau}\simeq \pi^{\vee}$. In this case, we say that $\tau$ is a dualizing or duality involution. When $r=2$, it is known that any lift of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution if and only if $n=2$. In this paper, we study the dualizing property of the lifts of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ and prove the following: (i) When $r \geq 2$ and $n \geq 3$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is never a dualizing involution. (ii) When $r=2t$ and $n=2$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution. (iii) When $r=2t+1$ and $n=2$, we show that there is a unique lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ which is a dualizing involution.

papers.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
papers.abstract: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $\tau=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $\alpha$ satisfying $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(\alpha;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

papers.title: A BMO Extension of Oskolkov's Criterion for Rectangular Trigonometric Fourier Sums
papers.abstract: We give a sufficient condition in terms of sectional BMO for almost everywhere Pringsheim convergence of rectangular trigonometric Fourier sums. For continuous functions, the condition includes Oskolkov's criterion, and an example shows that the inclusion is strict.

papers.title: Cross-Fitted Doubly Robust Estimation with Student-t Outcome Engines: ECM Algorithms, Monte Carlo Evidence and Schistosomiasis Programme Data from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
papers.abstract: Routine data on preventive chemotherapy for schistosomiasis are confounded, clustered, heavy-tailed and heaped. We study how cross-fitted augmented inverse probability weighted (AIPW) estimators behave, and how they should be computed, when least squares is replaced by Student-t outcome engines: Huber and t iteratively reweighted least squares, and a two-component t scale-mixture regression fitted by an ECM algorithm, alongside a residual-clipped augmentation. We give four short propositions (exact AIPW bias, the efficiency bound, the estimand of clipping, monotone ascent of a scale-constrained ECM), a single-file Python implementation with cluster-level cross-fitting, cluster-robust standard errors and a cluster bootstrap, and a Monte Carlo study with up to 1000 replications per cell. Robust outcome engines leave AIPW unchanged (RMSE differences at most 0.002), whereas clipping cuts RMSE by 26-45% under symmetric contamination, under-covers, and, as a plasmode experiment built on real covariates and residuals shows, shifts the estimand when residual laws differ between arms. One-sided artefacts that differ between arms bias every estimator. Heaped data also break naive code: the MAD scale collapses and the mixture likelihood is unbounded, and we give simple guards. Applied to 1485 rounds in 362 health zones of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (ESPEN, 2014-2025), integrated delivery appears to raise programme coverage by 17.4 percentage points, yet epidemiological coverage differs by only 0.9: the gap comes from targeting denominators, a real differential artefact that no outcome engine can remove.

papers.title: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
papers.abstract: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. The four arguments have substantially different provenance. In particular, the last is a consequence of a known construction, not a priority claim. The two longer constructions are recorded in detail for independent mathematical scrutiny.

affiliations.raw: Novosibirsk State University

papers.title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
papers.abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. Each item pairs premise audio and text with a hypothesis, an NLI label, and English glosses. The author assigned labels, so the dataset is an exploratory resource rather than a mature benchmark. The NLI experiments use the reference text; the audio is evaluated separately. XLM-RoBERTa baselines with five-fold item-level cross-validation reach 44.7% on Pidgin and 46.2% on Camfranglais (chance 33.3%). Still, neither is statistically distinguishable from hypothesis-only input, so hypothesis wording may account for much of the accuracy. Under disjoint-item cross-variety transfer, where a test item's counterpart is never seen in training, accuracy is 40.1% (Pidgin to Camfranglais) and 45.6% (Camfranglais to Pidgin). A counterpart-leak audit raises this to 60-64%, illustrating how counterpart leakage can overstate transfer. Zero-shot Whisper transcription of the recordings performs poorly: the best word error rates are 66.6% for Pidgin and 45.5% for Camfranglais, and with automatic language identification, Whisper Large-v3 labels 93 of 114 Pidgin recordings as Yoruba or Swahili. Together, the results suggest that such resources need disjoint-item evaluation and hypothesis-only controls, and that speech recognition must be adapted to these varieties before spoken NLI can be tested end to end.

papers.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.

papers.title: Pressure dependent DFT study of mechanical, thermal, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of EuCd2As2: a magnetic semimetal
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the pressure-dependent physical properties of EuCd2As2, a magnetically and topologically rich compound with potential applications in spintronics and optoelectronics technologies. We have investigated the structural, mechanical, thermophysical, acoustic, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of this material at pressures of 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 GPa. The calculated lattice parameters at zero pressure are in good agreement with experimental values. The mechanical stability of EuCd2As2 is maintained over the investigated pressure range. The elastic constants, bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus are found to be tunable with applied pressure. The compound undergoes a brittle to ductile transition at higher pressures. The Debye temperature, melting temperature, and Gr\"uneisen parameter are found to be strongly pressure-dependent. Phonon thermal conductivity has been evaluated. The electronic properties of EuCd2As2 were studied through band structure and density of states (DOS). The effect of pressure up to 8 GPa was investigated for the ferromagnetic (FM) phase. At 0 GPa, the calculated FM band structure exhibits no band gap at the Fermi level, which confirms the semimetallic nature of EuCd2As2. The net magnetic moment of 6.96 {\mu}_B per unit cell was obtained for this compound indicating its potential for spintronics application. The optical properties, including the dielectric function, refractive index, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity, reflectivity, and loss function, are calculated. The calculated optical spectra indicate strong absorption in the visible and ultraviolet regions, suggesting that EuCd2As2 may have potential for optoelectronic applications.

authors.name: M. A. Afzal
authors.institution: Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences

papers.title: ProdPilot: A Layered Model Context Protocol System for Automated Production Readiness and Deployment of Vibe-Coded Projects
papers.abstract: AI-assisted development environments turn natural-language requests into working applications, yet the projects they produce often fail on their first deployment for operational reasons: credentials in source files, missing security middleware, no container definition, no health endpoint and no delivery pipeline. Automated repair of such defects usually relies on free-form model generation, which varies between runs and is seldom checked independently. This paper presents ProdPilot, a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and React projects against 50 production readiness rules, repairs violations through a bounded loop, gates the result and deploys it. Each rule is classified by what its fix requires: 28 fixes are fixed templates, 16 are filled with values extracted from the project and only 6 are written by the IDE agent's model, so 88.0\% of the ruleset needs no model-written content, and across 499 real repositories 93.5\% of the violations found fall in those classes. A fix, however it was produced, is accepted only if the checker that flagged the rule now passes. In a full-chain run over 23 sample projects, template and extraction fixes that were applied as written passed their checkers in 87.6\% and 95.0\% of cases, and independent verification rejected 25 of the 237 fixes reported as applied. A deployability model trained on 684 real deployments ranks held-out projects at 0.909 ROC AUC, a gated project was deployed, smoke-tested and connected to an active CI/CD pipeline in 82 seconds, and the unchanged server worked from the IDE agents in VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf, where live agents resolved all six delegated rules on the first attempt under the same verification. ProdPilot itself runs no model.

papers.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
papers.abstract: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.

papers.title: Availability-Aware Historical Feedback Learning for Electric Arc Furnace Temperature and Chemical Composition Prediction
papers.abstract: Electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking plays an increasingly important role in recycled and lower-carbon steel production. However, variability in charged materials, energy input, and operating conditions makes accurate prediction of molten steel temperature and final chemical composition challenging. Intermittent or delayed measurements limit the information available for timely prediction. This study develops an availability-aware historical-feedback learning framework for predicting EAF endpoint temperature and the final concentrations of twelve chemical elements. Eight industrial data sources are integrated into three progressively enriched predictor representations comprising 19 static, 39 temporal, and 47 history-informed features. Historical outcomes are incorporated only when eligible under an assumed 60-minute measurement-release delay. Using 19,738 temperature heats and 3,341 chemistry heats, twelve tuned regression algorithms are evaluated through chronological forward validation. The proposed historical-feedback representation reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) in 147 of 156 matched algorithm-target comparisons. For temperature prediction, ExtraTrees achieves an RMSE of 12.290 degrees C, representing a 5.54 percent reduction compared with its temporal-only counterpart. Historical-feature ablation and feedback-delay sensitivity analyses demonstrate the importance of recent outcome information and its availability. In a separate retrospective later-period evaluation, lightweight adaptive residual correction reduces temperature RMSE from 12.502 to 12.275 degrees C without retraining the underlying model. Exploratory deep learning comparisons and target-specific feature-attribution analyses provide additional insights into predictive behavior. The results establish historical outcome availability and sequential feedback as important considerations for EAF endpoint prediction.

papers.title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of high-entropy alloy (HEA) strength can guide composition and processing decisions; however, obtaining tensile-test data for HEAs can be costly and experimentally demanding. This study proposes Robust Outcome-aware Sequential Experimentation for High-Entropy Alloys (ROSE-HEA), a sample-efficient framework for predicting ultimate tensile strength (UTS) from alloy composition and processing conditions. Its acquisition policy anticipates how possible UTS outcomes update predictions and the support for complementary Gaussian process (GP) descriptions. It then reassesses the worst-case expected predictive risk remaining across a reference domain to select informative candidates. A retrospective evaluation on 501 HEA records compares ROSE-HEA with expected-improvement (EI) and upper-confidence-bound (UCB) Bayesian optimization (BO), random GP sampling, and eight conventional regressors across 30 matched runs with shared initial observations and test conditions. Starting from 25 initial observations and acquiring 100 additional responses, ROSE-HEA achieves the lowest mean root-mean-square error (RMSE), at 152.84 MPa, and the highest mean R^2, at 0.7443. Mean RMSE is reduced by 6.16% and 6.37% relative to EI and UCB, respectively. The selected observations improve prediction across six regressor families and provide broader design-space coverage. ROSE-HEA also surpasses the strongest conventional regressor's mean predictive performance using 125 rather than 185 observations, corresponding to 32.4% fewer training observations. These findings demonstrate the potential of outcome-aware robust sequential learning to improve UTS prediction in HEAs under constrained training budgets.

papers.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
papers.abstract: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.

papers.title: Everything is an Operational View: UI as a Projection over Context in Agentic Systems
papers.abstract: The emergence of generative AI has enabled Generative User Interfaces (GenUI) that dynamically construct interfaces from user intent, yet existing approaches rely on request-response pipelines that fragment context and limit transparency and control. This paper proposes AFS-UI, which reconceptualises UI as projections over context built on an agentic file-system abstraction that organizes data, capabilities, and interaction state within a unified, persistent workspace. In particular, AFS-UI addresses key limitations in current systems, including heterogeneous resource discoverability, incompatible operation semantics, tangling projection and context, rigid source composition and substitution, and limited evolvability. Within this framework, interfaces become dynamic, inspectable views over shared resources, supporting both human and agent interaction through a common operational surface.

authors.name: Jieshan Chen
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: Agentic-Teacher: An Agentic Data Engine for Failure-Driven VLA Post-Training
papers.abstract: Improving a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model requires demonstrations that address its weaknesses and provide effective supervision for learning. Coding agents can autonomously generate demonstrations through environment interaction, yet successful execution alone does not ensure effective supervision for VLA learning. We introduce Agentic-Teacher, an autonomous data engine for failure-driven VLA post-training. Given a VLA checkpoint, a task specification, and configured environment tools, the engine analyzes failed rollouts, selects intervention states, and iteratively develops closed-loop code policies through execution feedback. Validated policies become reusable demonstration generators that collect successful continuations from states where the VLA struggles. To make these demonstrations suitable for learning, Agentic-Teacher introduces temporally correlated action noise to broaden state-action coverage, removes idle frames while preserving gripper transitions, and filters trajectories using the frozen base model's flow-matching loss. The resulting demonstrations are combined with successful VLA rollouts for post-training, yielding an updated policy that operates without coding-agent assistance. Agentic-Teacher thus connects the weaknesses of a target VLA to both the generation and curation of its training data. In simulation, it improves $\pi_0$ success rates from 79.4% to 87.8% on LIBERO-10, from 80.4% to 90.6% on MetaWorld-10, and from 0% to 30.0% across three RoboCasa tasks.

authors.name: Ya Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Data-driven exploration of the strength-ductility synergy in refractory high-entropy alloys
papers.abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have attracted increasing attention for their exceptional ability to retain strength at high temperatures. However, current research mainly concentrates on compositions close to equimolar alloys, leaving a large part of the composition space unexplored. Here, we develop a multiscale framework based on a data-driven dislocation genome method that constructs energy landscapes for edge dislocation motion across various compositions. The local configurational force derived from the energy landscape is incorporated into dislocation dynamics simulations, revealing a scaling law connecting macroscale strength and atomic-scale local resistance governed by fluctuations in the local configurational force. Based on this scaling law, a new solid-solution strengthening model for edge dislocation in BCC alloys is developed, followed by a data-driven exploration of refractory alloys considering both strength and ductility. The developed method and theory are adaptable, allowing for extension to other BCC alloy systems and guiding high-throughput alloy design.

authors.name: Yin Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Feasibility of Pareto-Improving Damping Control of Forced Oscillations: The Active-Power Case
papers.abstract: Damping control of a forced oscillation may reduce amplitudes at certain locations while increasing them elsewhere. This paper introduces Pareto improvement as a criterion for assessing such control: at least one nodal oscillation amplitude decreases, while none increases across all other nodes. The analysis considers active-power forcing sources and active-power control injections in connected swing networks with positive inertia and damping. Necessary conditions for Pareto improvement feasibility are derived from the normalized nodal responses. It is proven that for every network with a single oscillation source and a single actuator, at least one positive forcing frequency is shown to preclude Pareto improvement, regardless of the amplitude and phase of the control input. A three-node counterexample shows that this limitation does not persist with multiple actuators. PSS/E simulations of a 6-bus benchmark system and a modified IEEE 39-bus system validated the analysis. These findings suggest the value of assessing control effects across the network and further investigating multi-actuator damping control.

papers.title: Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified? A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly combine sensed time series with external text such as expert reports and news, yet how reliably models use text that agrees or conflicts with the sensed history remains unclear. We introduce the first real-world diagnostic benchmark organized by text-history relationship: 1,762 text-window pairs across sensor telemetry (Weather), web-service traffic (Wikipedia), and market data streams (Finance), each labeled Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified by whether the text's direction agrees with the historical trend, opposes it, or is not stated. Across ten pretrained models evaluated zero-shot, we investigate text selection and combination under text-history relationships (RQ1) and error diagnosis and horizon-scaled revision control (RQ2). For RQ1, we compare two types of text on paired Weather windows: one directly forecasts temperature changes, while the other describes related weather conditions, such as winds and fronts. Under Aligned, the first type yields the lowest error for most models. Under Conflicting, it increases most models' error above the no-text baseline; we therefore add only its stated magnitude and timing to the second type. Compared with either type alone, this combination lowers mean absolute scaled error (MASE) for six models and raises directional accuracy (DA) for seven. For RQ2, an error decomposition attributes the error increase to oversized revisions, and a training-free rule that limits them outperforms forecasts both with and without text for the four models with this trade-off, lowering MASE by 4.49%-21.98% and raising DA by 2.99%-9.71%. Our dataset is available at https://github.com/Shelton1202/ACU-Bench.

papers.title: State-of-Charge Targets for Storage Participation in Two-Settlement Markets: Reliability, Price, and Compensation Impacts
papers.abstract: As energy storage assumes a larger role in electricity systems, market operation must coordinate its use across time to support reliability during periods of system stress. Minimum state-of-charge (SOC) targets provide a means of preserving energy for these periods, but their design shapes reliability, operating efficiency, and storage compensation. This paper evaluates alternative SOC target designs in a California-based day-ahead and real-time electricity market model. The comparison examines targets based on day-ahead schedules or rolling centralized dispatch, enforced at the individual-resource or system level, across seasons, stress conditions, and participant information settings. The results show that retaining more energy does not necessarily reduce load shedding: targets that restrict discharge can limit storage support during shortages. Under critical summer conditions, individual targets derived from rolling centralized dispatch reduce weekly load shedding by approximately 83--84\% relative to operation without targets. Lower RT clearing costs and average prices can coexist with higher storage compensation, reflecting the role of day-ahead positions and real-time deviations in determining settlement outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating energy retention with timely discharge and network deliverability when designing SOC requirements for storage participation in electricity markets.

papers.title: Can Agents Keep Up with Time? An Empirical Analysis of Temporal Adaptation After a Conversational Hiatus
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly serve as persistent personal assistants across modern web platforms, managing schedules, applications, and multi-step plans over weeks or months. Users often return to an ongoing conversation after a long conversational hiatus, while earlier bookings and preparation notes stay on record. During this hiatus, scheduled dates may pass even though the retained records remain unchanged and event outcomes go unrecorded. Existing evaluations of long-horizon agents focus on fact retention and explicit state updates. Whether agents perceive the passage of time and adapt their advice accordingly therefore remains unknown. We frame this ability as temporal state perception and use, which means perceiving the current time and applying it when interpreting dated records. To study it, we design session-rekindling tasks that keep the earlier conversation fixed and vary only the follow-up date and the way temporal information reaches the agent. Experiments across five model routes and five temporal-information conditions show that agents can obtain the current time but often fail to use it. They reliably query the clock and even note in their reasoning that the scheduled date has passed, yet many still tell users to prepare for the expired event. Supplying explicit temporal context reduces this error, and providing the computed date relation removes it entirely. Keeping up with time therefore depends on turning perceived time into updated plans. Based on these findings, we design a session-rekindling benchmark that provides temporal-awareness guidance for designing long-horizon agents. The code can be found at https://github.com/Adoreu2/session-rekindling-benchmark.

authors.name: Ming Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
papers.abstract: Moving a scene generator to a new game engine requires more than exporting its final output: planning, construction tools, and stored experience may also depend on the original backend. We present SceneAgent, a multi-agent framework for reusing the construction process and its experience across backends. A canonical SceneContext maintains the evolving world, while backend adapters isolate coordinate conventions, asset bindings, and export. Structured handoffs let fresh Builder sessions query this persistent state without inheriting the full construction transcript. Across generations, human-approved traces are distilled into asset-ID-free Layout skills and semantic Content skills that can be retrieved and recombined. We introduce GameSceneBench, comprising 69 indoor and outdoor prompts. Under a common asset and evaluation protocol, SceneAgent obtains human tie-adjusted preference scores of 78.2-89.4% against five baselines. Ablations show that reusable skills and the multi-agent protocol primarily improve prompt alignment and scene completeness, with additional runtime. Deployment in a second engine preserves the shared construction protocol and skill library while replacing backend integration components. Together, these results support separating persistent scene state, task-local reasoning, and reusable experience for portable scene construction.

papers.title: Alleviating Interview Stress: Effects of Robot Persona and Reactive Backchanneling on High-Pressure Mock Interviews
papers.abstract: High-pressure job interviews induce anxiety and impair performance. Existing mock training suffers from a trade-off among cost, standardization, and physical presence. This study investigated how a robot interviewer's verbal persona (supportive vs. challenging) and nonverbal backchanneling (active vs. negative) affect users' psychological states and facial expressions in a simulated interview. In a 2x2 between-subjects experiment (N=28), participants interacted with a NAO robot. Subjective measures (state anxiety, self-efficacy, social presence) and objective facial emotion recognition were collected. Results showed that a supportive persona reduced task load, increased perceived robot warmth and mind perception, and decreased perceived surveillance and robot discomfort. Active backchanneling increased non-neutral (p = .021) and anxiety-tension facial affect (p = .048). A significant interaction effect between persona and backchanneling was found on social presence (p = .045). The subjective-objective consistency was 67.9%, indicating complementary measurement modalities. The findings provide preliminary support for the social buffering hypothesis in human-robot interaction.

authors.name: Zhuoran Gao
authors.institution: First Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: CardioTrace: Motion-Aware Cine Synthesis via Coupled Tracing and Segmentation
papers.abstract: Cardiac cine MRI provides time-resolved visualization of cardiac motion and is essential for evaluating ventricular function and anatomy. In routine clinical acquisition, however, cine sequences are frequently temporally sparse or degraded by arrhythmia, motion, and scan-time constraints, which can hinder reliable quantification and downstream analysis. We present CardioTrace, a motion-aware cine synthesis framework that generates a full cardiac cine sequence from limited input while explicitly modeling and tracing cardiac motion. CardioTrace couples two complementary pathways: a pixel-translation branch that directly predicts cine frames in a residual formulation, and a flow-field branch that estimates time-resolved deformation fields from a reference phase to provide interpretable motion correspondences across frames. To further preserve anatomical plausibility, a segmentation branch supervises clinically meaningful cardiac structures at key phases, and a cross-branch consistency objective encourages the synthesized appearance dynamics to follow the explicit motion guidance, mitigating temporal drift and unrealistic shape transitions over long sequences. The framework also supports prompt-style conditioning to incorporate auxiliary patient or acquisition information, improving robustness across heterogeneous multi-center data. Experiments on public cardiac cine MRI datasets demonstrate that CardioTrace improves perceptual quality and temporal coherence over representative GAN- and diffusion-based baselines, while better preserving ventricular morphology throughout the cardiac cycle. \textit{Our codes are available after review}.

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $\chi(1)_p$ of $\chi(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $\chi$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2\pi i/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $\chi_P$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $\chi_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: Any Channel Count, One Token Stream: Incorporating Spatial Audio Understanding and Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models
papers.abstract: Audio phase relations encode source locations, yet existing large audio-language models (LALM) reduce audio to single-channel content to stabilise general audio understanding, leaving spatial information for direction, distance, and source-relation questions unused. We present SpheraAudio, which accepts recordings with any channel count -- mono, stereo, First-Order Ambisonics (FOA), or higher -- and maps them into a single token stream. A spatial encoder turns complex multichannel spectra into spatial tokens interleaved with audio tokens at corresponding temporal positions. Spatial Multimodal RoPE (SMRoPE) makes each token's modality identity and temporal slot visible to rotary attention without altering the language model's original RoPE. Training runs in three stages -- spatial-encoder pretraining, projector alignment, and joint supervised-and-reinforcement learning -- progressing from geometric supervision to language-based spatial decisions, with answers trained as explicit spatial chain-of-thought: step-by-step geometric reasoning over the heard scene. Current benchmarks tie questions to a fixed channel-count format and score answers without spatial reasoning evidence. We introduce SpheraQA, which spans mono, stereo, and FOA recordings and organises questions hierarchically from single-attribute perception through cross-source relations to multi-step reasoning, scored programmatically against simulated scene geometry and real-recording annotations with step-by-step solution references. Across SpheraQA and public spatial-audio benchmarks, SpheraAudio sets a new performance standard for spatial audio understanding. It supports high-precision localisation, tracking, and reasoning over static and moving sound sources while preserving strong general-audio capabilities. We will release code, SpheraQA, and evaluation metrics to support reproducibility.

papers.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defects to their accepted fixes and review context. We present PrivacyPR, a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests (PRs) from 1,469 repositories, created between June 2018 and January 2024. Each PR includes its commits, diffs, review discussion, and LLM-generated labels for privacy relevance, fix type, and GDPR principles. PrivacyPR provides 1,169 high-confidence privacy fixes and 1,643 non-fix PRs, together with Verified, a manually checked split of 250 privacy fixes and 250 non-fix PRs, and Small, a 100 + 100 subset for evaluation. On Verified, both annotators endorsed 72% of the LLM's GDPR-principle assignments. Beyond supporting empirical study of how privacy defects arise and are fixed, PrivacyPR provides a benchmark for privacy-aware code review on real, developer-accepted fixes. Its evaluation harness reverts each fix to reintroduce the defect. On Small, two coding agents detect only 42-51% of defects under a generic review prompt, but 88-91% when explicitly asked to check privacy, while flagging 11-15% of non-fix PRs. These results show that privacy defects can be detected by coding agents, but that detection depends strongly on review intent and comes with false alarms. Data, code, reviews, judge verdicts, and an extensible evaluation harness are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23744765.

authors.name: Aditya Bhardwaj
authors.institution: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar

papers.title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=\lambda \Delta +\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\delta_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $\lambda >0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(\alpha, \theta)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $\alpha\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

papers.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
papers.abstract: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution. To interpret these structures and the trained network, we propose a conditioned atomic response mapping analysis, revealing both the global structural descriptors and the local atomic environments that govern target properties. Overall, GaDiT establishes a general framework for interpretable generation, inverse design and structure-property discovery for disordered atomic structures.

authors.name: Yongkun Yang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
papers.abstract: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals the systematic localization of itinerant $d$-quasiparticle states at the Fermi level, consistent with the emergence of a soft Coulomb gap, while the underlying band structure and symmetry are preserved. Transport reveals Efros-Shklovskii variable-range hopping governed by a colossal soft gap with characteristic temperature $T_{\mathrm{ES}}>50{,}000\,\mathrm{K}$ and screened Coulomb interaction strengths as high as 1.6 eV. Together, multiple lines of evidence indicate that interacting Anderson behavior is a native characteristic that survives to temperatures as high as $500\,\mathrm{K}$ in high-entropy materials.

papers.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
papers.abstract: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $\mu$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $\mu$s per round.

authors.institution: Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research At MIT

authors.name: Xiaoming Sun
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Resource Engineering

papers.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
papers.abstract: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
papers.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $\pi_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $\pi_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

authors.name: Fangzhou Zhao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Zekai Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The random KKM mapping principle and its applications
papers.abstract: Based on the recently developed random Brouwer fixed point theorem and the theory of stable compactness, we establish a random Knaster--Kuratowski--Mazurkiewicz (KKM) mapping principle in Hausdorff topological $L^0$-modules. As consequences of this principle, we obtain several results on fixed points, minimax problems, variational inequalities, and conditional games. These results solve a large class of noncompact problems in random functional analysis and its applications.

papers.title: Antihelical Edge States in Photonic Metacrystals
papers.abstract: Antihelical edge states represent a gapless form of boundary transport in which modes with opposite spin counterpropagate along a given boundary, while modes sharing the same spin propagate in the same direction on opposite boundaries. Here we show that such states arise naturally within a modified Kane-Mele framework realized in an electromagnetic-dual photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy. Reversing the spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor coupling on one sublattice reorganizes the bulk spectrum into a spin-polarized Dirac semimetal characterized by spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones rather than a bulk gap. This bulk reorganization generates tilted edge-mode dispersions in zigzag ribbons and gives rise to antihelical edge transport coexisting with bulk states. Full-wave simulations confirm the corresponding bulk and edge behaviors. Extending the analysis to finite geometries, simulations further reveal discrete corner-localized modes. A realistic design based on split-ring metaatoms is proposed to realize the required staggered bianisotropy and spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones. Furthermore, we show that the tensorial freedom of the bianisotropic constitutive relations enables continuous manipulation of the electromagnetic pseudospin basis while preserving the antihelical boundary transport. These results provide a practical route for engineering unconventional gapless boundary transport in photonic Dirac systems.

authors.name: Jian-Wen Dong
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Optoelectronic Materials and Technology

papers.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
papers.abstract: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by $n$ material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length $\varepsilon \to 0$ and matches it exactly at $n$ chosen states for any $\varepsilon$. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces ($n=2$) accurate strength reproduction requires $\varepsilon$ commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length $l_{ch}$, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures. We introduce a neural-network (NN) strength function that is learned directly from strength data, is physics-constrained by construction, and provides far more calibration parameters than analytic surfaces; the calibration is generalized to any number of strength states and to enforce openness in chosen directions. A single architecture captures synthetic data from the Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager, Mogi-Coulomb and 3D Hoek-Brown surfaces and experimental data for graphite, natural rubber and styrene-butadiene rubber. The resulting PFSS is accurate up to $\varepsilon = 10\,l_{ch}$, whereas that of the exact analytic surfaces performs comparatively poorly even at $\varepsilon = 0.5\,l_{ch}$. Finite-element simulations validate the theory across fracture regimes. By decoupling strength fidelity from the regularization length, the approach substantially reduces the mesh resolution required for phase-field fracture simulations of large structures.

papers.title: Signal Scaffolding: Unlocking the Potential of Lightweight Models for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.abstract: With the rising demand for edge devices, lightweight self-supervised monocular depth estimation methods have continued to evolve; however, existing methods generally suffer from poor accuracy. We find that the root cause may lies in the failure of conventional training regimes to fully exploit the inherent potential of lightweight models. To address this, we propose a novel three-phase training strategy for lightweight self-supervised monocular depth estimation, termed Signal Scaffolding (SS). Without introducing any additional dataset or parameters, we apply SS to ReForgeDepth, a lightweight network of our own design. Experiments on the KITTI and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off and running in real time on edge devices. These results suggest that lightweight models can be improved further within their existing capacity, and that the central question may be less about how parameters are allocated than about how to unlock this latent potential through training.

authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Xin Gao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Symbolic Regression Fitting for Roche Lobe Radius
papers.abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius $R_{\rm L}/a$, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over $10^{-5}\leq q\leq10^5$, the expression reduces the root mean square error from $1.97\times10^{-3}$ for Eggleton's formula to $5.95\times10^{-4}$, while its maximum relative error is $1.39\%$, compared with Eggleton's $0.83\%$. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of $0.331\%$. The formula is monotonic, recovers the $q^{\frac{1}{3}}$ scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within $0.036\%$ of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of $10^7$ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes $0.217$~s compared with $0.450$~s for Eggleton, a speed-up of $2.08$. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.

papers.title: Accessible 3D Printed Archimedes System for Accurate and Precise Density Measurements and Uncertainty Analysis
papers.abstract: Accurate and precise density measurements are important for characterizing solid materials and for evaluating physical properties that are strongly affected by porosity. While several methods are available for determining density, measurements of small or irregularly shaped samples can be limited by sample geometry, balance precision, liquid density, and other experimental sources of uncertainty. In this study, an accessible Archimedes density measurement system was developed using 3D printed components and an analytical balance for the measurement of solid and liquid densities. The measurement of solid densities requires knowing the exact density of the liquid. Therefore, copper, vanadium, and indium standards were used to measure the densities of ethanol (0.8116 +/- 0.0005 g/cm3), distilled water (0.9982 +/- 0.0013 g/cm3), and hexanes (0.6748 +/- 0.0016 g/cm3), all of them showing strong agreement with literature values. Uncertainty analysis indicates that the relative uncertainty in the measured solid density decreases with increasing sample mass and balance precision, while higher density liquids can further reduce the required sample mass. The uncertainty of the immersed mass measurement was found to have a greater influence on the calculated density than the uncertainty of the air mass measurement. An open-source Archimedes LS software was developed to analyse liquid and solid densities including the corresponding uncertainties. These findings demonstrate that an accessible 3D printed Archimedes system combined with an open-source software provides a practical approach for improving the consistency and comparability of density measurements between laboratories.

papers.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
papers.abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly optimizing discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding-control parameters, and the limited generalization of static rewriting strategies under semantically complex scenarios. To address these issues, we propose RAG-FGO, a dynamic optimization framework for generative retrieval strategies. RAG-FGO formulates query rewriting as a non-differentiable black-box optimization problem in a mixed discrete-continuous space, and represents prompt templates and decoding parameters as adaptively optimizable query-rewriting agents. The framework performs global search to enable semantic jumps and structural reorganization that escape local optima, while applying local perturbations for fine-grained alignment and precise refinement. In addition, RAG-FGO introduces an elite-preserving memory pool that accumulates high-quality strategies across iterations, thereby mitigating the impact of stochasticity and noisy feedback on optimization stability. Experimental results on a diverse suite of benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, supporting its applicability to complex semantic retrieval tasks.

papers.title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Cost Immersion Cooling System
papers.abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, open-source, single-phase immersion cooling testbed for studying liquid cooling of data center hardware. A 500 W titanium heater, standing in for server load, is submerged in a glass tank of mineral oil, a dielectric fluid. The heated oil is circulated by a magnetic drive pump through an air-cooled radiator. An ESP32 microcontroller logs three DS18B20 temperature sensors (heater surface, bulk fluid and ambient) and switches the pump, fan and heater through a relay module. The complete system costs INR 35,318 (about USD 380), built entirely from components available in India. At quasi-steady state under the full 500 W load, the heater surface reached 118.3 {\deg}C while the bulk oil stayed at 29.3 {\deg}C, only 8.0 {\deg}C above ambient. Thermal-resistance analysis shows that the heater-to-oil interface, limited by natural convection, accounts for about 92% of the total resistance (178.0 vs 16.0 m{\deg}C/W). The external loop therefore has spare capacity. CAD files, firmware and data are openly available, so the setup can be reproduced and used to compare dielectric fluids, loads and flow arrangements.

authors.name: Nikhil Meena
authors.institution: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences

papers.title: Flow structure, heat transport, and dissipation in vertical-field magnetoconvection at similar Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: We employ direct numerical simulations to investigate the effect of a vertical magnetic field on the flow structures, heat transport, and dissipation rates in Rayleigh--B\'enard convection of a low-Prandtl-number fluid ($\mathrm{Pr} = 0.025$) at an approximately fixed Reynolds number ($\mathrm{Re} \approx 880$), maintained by adjusting the Rayleigh number to compensate for the Lorentz force. As the Hartmann number increases, the flow becomes more anisotropic, which strengthens the positive convective heat fluxes relative to the negative ones and thereby raises the Nusselt number, accompanied by a thinning of the thermal boundary layers. The total viscous and thermal dissipation rates are dominated by the boundary layers, whereas the total magnetic dissipation rate is dominated by the bulk. With increasing Hartmann number, the boundary-layer fraction of the viscous and magnetic dissipation rates increases, whereas that of the thermal dissipation computed from the temperature fluctuations decreases, owing to the suppression of temperature fluctuations near the boundary layers. The dissipation rates deviate from log-normality and are well described by stretched exponential distributions, whose tails become more extended with increasing Hartmann number.

authors.name: Akanksha Bhardwaj
authors.institution: Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
papers.abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. We observed that the SleepXAI model achieves strong classification performance on both datasets. Among the evaluated methods, Integrated Gradients (IG) consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across all five sleep stages on Sleep-EDF and across all AHI groups on DREAMT, outperforming all other evaluated methods under the Spearman rank correlation metric. These findings highlight the importance of attribution method selection as a key factor for ensuring reliable and clinically interpretable automated sleep staging systems.

papers.title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI
papers.abstract: Governments are writing rules for artificial intelligence that decide what counts as an automated decision or a harm, often before the people they affect have a chance to question them. We introduce AI-Voyager, a public-interest system for human-AI civic reasoning, in which people and AI work together to understand, contest and shape the rules that govern AI. A resident can find their city's rules on AI in hiring or upload their country's AI strategy, read it as an affected worker would, open the passage behind any answer, and draft a revision. Its architecture turns 3,653 governance documents from city, state, federal and national governments into passages that keep their page and edition, and retrieves evidence through bounded agentic search that verifies each statement. On 360 new questions that require finding the relevant documents, it reached 83.0% macro recall, against 80.5% for the strongest baseline, 73.7% without iterative search and 99.1% on a benchmark with fixed documents. In a study with 24 participants new to two AI bills, most proposed changes asked how provisions would apply. Participants chose lenses for the kind of explanation they wanted, and citations signaled grounding but rarely led them to check the source. By binding AI assistance to the exact text of public documents, this work introduces a grammar of operations and a design space that inform how such systems are designed and evaluated, and how people take part in governing AI.
