papers.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
papers.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

papers.title: Quantum Shock and Train-Time Constrained Quantization: A Geometric Study of Finite-Resolution Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Finite-resolution interfaces map Variational-Circuit angle to discrete codebook. Since Pauli rotations are periodic, so Euclidean rounding may produce wrong codeword near a chart boundary; error due to coordinates alone cannot measure how much the final state was changed. Herein we define a metric, Quantum Shock, for Pure State it is defined as the average of the square of the Fubini-Study distance (over all inputs) between the pre-deployment and deployed states. This value is limited by constant multipliers of the mean of infidelity and provides upper limits on displacement when observing bounded quantities and margin based predictive stability. Extensions to the analytical Bures-angle for mixed-states were derived, along with a finite shot stability bound. The proposed Train-Time Constrained Quantization allows a delay in applying a penalty for selecting a codeword aligned with periodicity until after task only optimizations. Three small binary tasks were evaluated on a four qubit, two layer classifier using ten matched seeds, K = 4, 8, 16 and exact expectation values from simulation under noiseless conditions and state vector simulations. On our primary evaluation, T-CQ exhibited smaller average local quantum shock compared to circular post-training quantization for each task and code-book size tested. The re-execution on the x86-64 platform using K=8 preserved the direction of the mean-shock comparison but had varying magnitudes.

papers.title: Cracks in Embeddings: Robustness and Stability of JEPA-Based Chest X-Ray Representations
papers.abstract: Self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) models are increasingly used for medical imaging, however there is a limited understanding about robustness of these models toward real-world image changes. We test four JEPA-based chest X-ray encoders, trained on 78,468 NIH ChestX-ray14 images, under six tests: two black-box adversarial attacks (SPSA, Boundary Attack), three image corruptions (Gaussian noise, brightness shift, contrast shift), and a label-scarcity test, measuring embedding change and classification AUROC. These perturbations cause severe, model-dependent damage: encoder-level Cosine Similarity drops as low as 0.33, and AUROC falls by as much as 0.12 in the worst case (I-JEPA under the Boundary Test). We test two ways of training the small predictor on top of each frozen encoder to address this. Adversarial fine-tuning, trained on clean and perturbed images together, raises embedding consistency above 0.97 in nearly every case and improves AUROC, relative to the same perturbed baseline, for most models, with the largest gain of $+0.10$ on I-JEPA. A Vector-Quantized codebook method, trained only on clean images and evaluated on perturbed test images for the first time, instead degrades under distortion for all four models, most noticeably for I-JEPA ($-0.15$ AUROC on average), showing that its discrete bottleneck alone does not provide the robustness that comes from training on perturbed data directly.

papers.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
papers.abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

papers.title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
papers.abstract: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. In particular, we explore how their orientation affects their sunlight exposure in these conditions, since most studies to date do not account for orientation, turbulent shear flow, and wind-waves at the water surface. We find that in all cases, particles prefer certain orientations, and this causes the average sunlight exposure of the particles to be 5 to 40\% higher than would be expected if their orientations were random. Further, we find that the mean irradiance depends on the ratio of the particle mixing length $L_m$ to the light decay lengthscale $\lambda$, and the nature of this dependence differs between disks and rods. Disks experience disproportionately greater mean irradiance at smaller $L_m/\lambda$ due to the vertical variation in their orientations. These results have important implications for accurately estimating the sunlight exposure of particles in the surface boundary layer.

papers.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
papers.abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in typing, achieves a state-of-the-art character error rate of 25.13% on emg2qwerty's cross-user benchmark, a 5.4% relative improvement over the previous best with 6.7 times fewer parameters, while running strictly causally with no future context.

papers.title: Bayesian Semiparametric Regression for Count Data Using Zero Altered Moment Models
papers.abstract: We develop a Bayesian semiparametric regression framework for count data that can accommodate both underdispersion and overdispersion without specifying a full parametric probability model. The model is built from the first two conditional factorial moments of a zero altered distribution. Covariates may enter the conditional mean and the conditional dispersion separately, thereby allowing the dispersion to vary across observations. We turn the moment restrictions into an adjusted exponentially tilted empirical likelihood (AETEL) criterion and combine this criterion with Gaussian priors to form a Bayesian empirical-likelihood pseudo-posterior. The adjustment improves numerical feasibility and a two-block Metropolis delayed acceptance sampler allows for faster runs of the MCMC chains. This reduces unnecessary exact evaluations without changing the AETEL target. Using existing Bayesian exponentially tilted empirical likelihood (ETEL) theory, we state a first-order posterior normal approximation and verify the moment, smoothness, and Jacobian rank conditions needed for the asymptotic inference. Simulations under zero inflated Poisson and Conway Maxwell Poisson data exhibit small bias, accurate uncertainty estimates, and near nominal interval coverage for both overdispersed and underdispersed counts. Applications to various datasets illustrate how the Bayesian analysis can identify covariate dependent dispersion using finite sample posterior inference.

papers.title: A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $\epsilon$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.
papers.intro:
The goal of this paper is to extend the quantitative graph discretization framework of Burago, Ivanov and Kurylev [6] to the Steklov and Neumann eigenvalue problems on compact domains with smooth boundary in complete Riemannian manifolds. Near the boundary, ambient geodesic balls are truncated by the domain, introducing an anisotropy that must be taken into account in the discrete energy. For the Steklov problem, an additional difficulty arises from the need to approximate the L2L^{2}-norm on the boundary, rather than in the interior. This leads us to consider two discrete Steklov problems. The first one, using an averaged trace, is more robust. The second one, using restriction to boundary vertices, is more classical but requires additional assumptions on the discretization parameters.

papers.title: Does the Ranking Hold? A Practitioner-Facing Audit of Hallucination Detectors on Small, Quantized, On-Device LLMs
papers.abstract: Hallucination detection for large language models is dominated by methods evaluated on 7B-70B research models with abundant sampling budgets and exact-match or ROUGE correctness labels. The small models practitioners actually ship on-device, Phi-3-mini, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-2B-Instruct, typically at 4-bit precision, sit outside this evidence base. We present a reproducible one-GPU audit of four detectors spanning three paradigms: length-normalized token-margin calibration, a lexical n-gram baseline, and two sampling-based consistency methods (semantic entropy and SelfCheckGPT-NLI) on two small open instruction-tuned models (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) loaded at 4-bit NF4 quantization on a single Colab T4 GPU, evaluated on closed-book TriviaQA. Cross-model ranking transfer is poor: Spearman rho is -0.80 and Kendall tau-b is -0.667, meaning the detector ranking actively inverts between the two models, and the cheap lexical baseline is statistically indistinguishable from the sampling-based consistency detectors on both models under bootstrap 95 percent confidence intervals. As a second, methodological contribution, we show that the standard token-overlap-to-multiple-choice correctness labeler for TruthfulQA-Generation produces near-chance AUROC (0.46-0.59) for all four detectors on both models, a labeler failure, not a detector failure, since the same detectors reach 0.69-0.89 AUROC on TriviaQA under the identical pipeline. We release the harness, prompts, and per-item scores and frame the detector choice explicitly as a fairness-of-error-rates allocation problem for practitioners deploying on resource-constrained, on-device hardware.

papers.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution. Second, we extend DTS to multi-objective sampling, so that a single search produces samples spanning an entire Pareto front. We instantiate both adaptations on de novo crystal generation: improving the stability of crystals generated by different models, using pretrained conditional models to generate crystals belonging to rare space groups or with high bulk modulus, and generating crystals along a Pareto front of high dielectric constant and high bandgap materials. Across these tasks, DTS-based inference-time adaptation successfully improves model outputs without modifying the models themselves.

authors.name: Vineet Jain
authors.institution: Delhi Pharmaceutical Science and Research University

papers.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions
papers.abstract: Generating an evaluation suite from an agent's specification is diversity-driven search: a generator fills a descriptor space (requirements $\times$ personas $\times$ scenario kinds), and the suite it emits is an archive, then scored like a benchmark by its mean pass rate, which throws away the search's product. We inject 7 controlled defects into a $\tau^2$-bench agent across two domains. Coverage yields a ceiling: if a defect's traced footprint holds $b$ scenarios that pass at baseline, it can itself contribute at most $b/N$ to a suite of $N$. For 4 of 5 traceable defects that ceiling lies at or below the detection threshold $\theta = 0.10$, so no within-footprint effect can move the suite past it; in both domains the tool-removal defect destroys every covered scenario it can (exactly its ceiling) while the suite-level pass rate moves the other way. Defects split into two regimes: trace-aligned ones, where per-cell scoring recovers the tool-removal defect in full and reveals a second as a significant improvement, and trace-orthogonal ones, whose footprint is behavioural: forced escalation is detected in retail at a traced coverage of exactly zero. Diversity along the generator's own axes helps only where it aligns: at fixed suite size a happy-path-only suite detects nothing, while a kind-diverse one detects the orchestration defect in 5 of 20 draws. Evaluation archives should be scored per cell and should publish coverage as a first-class property.

papers.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
papers.abstract: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.

papers.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.

papers.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
papers.abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. Paired targeted interventions show that false-drop causes significantly greater degradation than false-keep, while a non-deleting baseline can still fail when incorrect labels steer generation. On a frozen 102/102 calibration/test split, a simple deployment-matched gate reaches 0.655 accuracy versus 0.641 for always hard-drop and 0.662 for test-informed oracle selection. Global-accuracy crossovers require gold labels and are model- and task-specific diagnostics, not deployment thresholds. Deletion should instead be treated as cost-sensitive: validate query-critical false-drop risk on matched data, or default to label-free retention when such validation is unavailable.

papers.title: JaRS: Contrast-Free Localization of Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Jacobian Row Sums
papers.abstract: Diffusion models sometimes memorize and reproduce regions of their training images, raising privacy and copyright concerns. We aim to localize these regions. Existing contrast-based methods use the diagonal of the denoiser Jacobian, which reflects the posterior variance of each pixel. However, a small diagonal entry is ambiguous: it signals either memorization or averaging over many neighboring pixels in smooth or predictable regions. To resolve this ambiguity, these methods subtract a reference map, which requires a second evaluation with a null prompt or an earlier checkpoint. Unconditional models have no null prompt, and earlier checkpoints are unavailable in general. We show that Jacobian row sums (JaRS), unlike the diagonal, separate memorization from local averaging without a reference map. Pairing JaRS with an image-level detection score that uses the same statistic at an early denoising step yields JaRS+. Across Stable Diffusion v1.4 and v2.1, Realistic Vision v5.1, and an unconditional diffusion Transformer (DiT), JaRS+ outperforms contrast-based localization methods.

papers.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
papers.abstract: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. In deployed agent systems, the same execution may be exposed through composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories, changing what execution evidence is directly observable to the verifier. It therefore remains unclear whether correct verifier judgments persist across such abstraction boundaries. We introduce Verification Transport, a reliability test that measures judgment stability under abstraction-induced changes in execution observability. We construct matched native, abstracted, and restored views of the same frozen executions while holding the task, realized trajectory, outcome, ground truth, evaluation criterion, and verifier fixed. Across four agent-evaluation benchmarks, seven verifier backbones, four verification protocols, and three abstraction boundaries, we find substantial transport failure, reaching about 31% under macro abstraction and delegation. Verification protocols exhibit distinct failure modes: direct verification more often produces incorrect verdicts, whereas evidence-grounded and deliberative protocols tend to abstain under limited observability. This suggests that lower transport failure rates do not necessarily imply greater reliability. Restoring the corresponding execution provenance recovers 85.5% of transport failures, while recovery is lower when provenance is lossy or unavailable. These results show that native-view accuracy alone is insufficient to characterize verifier reliability when execution evidence crosses abstraction boundaries.

papers.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable supervision and reward-guided behavioral refinement provide a general and effective training paradigm for compact mathematical reasoners.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: WISE-VAULT: Decade-long Mid-Infrared Variability of WISE AGN
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) variability provides a powerful probe of accretion processes and dust reprocessing in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), as it is less affected by extinction than optical flux. Using multi-epoch photometry from \textit{WISE} and NEOWISE spanning over a decade, we investigate the MIR variability of $\sim$4.5 million color-selected AGNs. Variability is quantified using maximum--minimum amplitudes ($\Delta W1$), excess variance, reduced $\chi^2$, and structure function (SF) analysis over timescales of 0.5--10 years. We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability ($\Delta W1 > 0.5$ mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability ($A_{\rm var} > 0.5$ mag). A subset of these sources shows flare-like behavior, identifying them as candidate changing-look AGNs or tidal disruption events that warrant further spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up. The SF analysis shows radio-detected AGNs exhibit the highest variability amplitudes, followed by X-ray detected and the overall AGN sample. The variability amplitude is strongly anti-correlated with the Eddington ratio, indicating enhanced variability in lower accretion rate systems. A weak positive dependence on radio-loudness further suggests a contribution from non-thermal emission in radio sources. These results demonstrate that MIR variability provides a robust diagnostic of accretion physics and an efficient means of identifying extreme and rapidly evolving AGN phenomena. The full catalog of variable AGNs is made publicly available.

papers.title: CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes, Bipodality and the Parallel Wall Property
papers.abstract: Coxeter cell complexes are a simultaneous generalization to cube complexes and the Davis complex of a Coxeter group. We show that 1-skeleta of CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes isometrically embed into a CAT(0) cube complex. When the resulting cube complex is finite dimensional, we show that the condition of bipodality (satisfied by both CAT(0) cube complexes and Davis complexes of Coxeter groups) implies local finiteness of the cubulation. To this end, we show a Parallel Wall Theorem for bipodal CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes satisfying a uniform bound on the size of a collection of pairwise intersecting walls. In particular, our methods give a new, purely geometric proof of the Parallel Wall Theorem for Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety
papers.abstract: Safety in robotics does not solely depend on geometric constraints, but also on semantics: the given task, environment properties, and interactions between objects in the scene. We present a framework based on vision-language models (VLMs) to infer task- and scene-dependent safety constraints for robot manipulation. We provide the VLM a structured safety tool based on an RGB-D observation and a natural-language task instruction that first decides whether the task should be rejected since its execution may result in a non-recoverable hazardous outcome. Otherwise, it identifies preventable object-pair hazards and specifies the spatial relations that must be avoided. Open-vocabulary segmentation and depth information are then used to ground the detected objects in 3D and construct continuous risk fields that represent the corresponding hazardous regions. These fields are integrated with an obstacle avoidance module that corrects nominal robot motions during execution while accounting for the risk field. We evaluate the framework on preventable hazards, tasks requiring rejection, and safe variants in simulation and the real-world. Project website: https://vlm-hazard-riskfield.github.io

papers.title: Optimal Dividend Problem for a Threshold Dependent Surplus Process with Bounded Dividend Rate
papers.abstract: We study optimal bounded-rate dividend payments for a diffusion surplus process whose drift and volatility change at a fixed surplus threshold. Optimal strategies admit an exhaustive classification into zero-threshold, positive single-threshold, two-boundary, and three-boundary configurations. The latter two configurations have separated dividend regions, which arise because the interface can reverse the monotonicity of the derivative of the value function with respect to the initial surplus. Multiband optimality requires an upward change in drift. Without prescribing a strategy in advance, we construct the unique bounded classical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman transmission problem by varying the derivative at zero surplus and selecting the unique value for which the resulting solution agrees in both value and derivative with a bounded solution at a fixed sufficiently large surplus level. Verification identifies this solution with the value function and determines the optimal feedback strategy. For each configuration, we derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and characterize the switching boundaries through explicit formulas or equations in one unknown obtained by matching the value function and its derivative. The analysis also shows how changes in the drift and volatility of the upper regime affect the optimal value and dividend strategy. Numerical analysis illustrates how model parameters affect the optimal dividend regions.

papers.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
papers.abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. We introduce MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer that represents both rows and cells as tokens, adds the log-ages of rows and the names of foreign-key relationships to attention, and routes cells and rows to experts by column metadata rather than by values. A label-blind LLM agent complements the model: it reads the target database's schema and column statistics and adds validated single-row derived columns, without access to labels or model scores. On 21 RelBench tasks with leave-one-database-out pretraining on six databases, the MoREGT backbone improves on the Relational Transformer pretrained on the same databases by 2.25 points of mean AUROC and 5.83 points of mean nMAE. The agent's columns raise mean AUROC from 78.45 to 79.63 and lower mean nMAE from 27.91 to 26.98, the highest means on both metrics among the compared methods, including RT-J, which pretrains on about 400 times as many databases.

papers.title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection in tabular data poses significant challenges due to heterogeneous feature types-mixing numerical, categorical, and textual attributes, which complicate learning meaningful representations of normality. Recent work has applied large language models (LLMs) to this problem by serializing table rows as text sequences, yet these approaches rely on one-shot supervised fine-tuning that offers limited signal to tighten the model's description of normality. We propose DiSPaT, a self-play fine-tuning framework that strengthens the model's understanding of normal data. Building on the theoretical foundation of f-divergence minimization, we derive a tight approximation connecting our training objective to reducing the distributional gap between real normal data and model-generated samples. DiSPaT operates through an alternating optimization: at each iteration, the current policy generates synthetic samples that serve as pseudo-anomalies, while a critic discriminator learns to distinguish these from real normal samples; this signal drives policy updates that progressively align the model distribution with the true normal-data distribution. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that DiSPaT consistently outperforms prior LLM-based methods, deep learning approaches, and classical unsupervised detectors for tabular anomaly detection.

papers.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
papers.abstract: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

papers.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
papers.abstract: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

papers.title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
papers.abstract:
The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of M\"obius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$. Our destination formula computes it as the closure of a unipotent orbit, determined by the Cartan data and a bounded Levi factor. The stratified convergence principle organises these destinations into families of translated Schubert varieties attached to boundary points of a compactification of the group. Over the complex numbers, the destination relation is the support of Brion's limiting graphs in the wonderful compactification, providing scheme structures, multidegrees and diagonal intersections.
  For discrete groups, the union of destination relations determines proper discontinuity and whether a largest domain exists. It relates Quint's flag limit set, Conze--Guivarc'h, Kulkarni and Myrberg sets to the recurrent set, while balanced choices of cells yield domains for every discrete subgroup, without Anosov hypotheses. For symmetric-power actions of non-elementary Kleinian groups on $\mathbb{CP}^N$, we compute the largest domain by a multiplicity bound at points of the classical limit set; for $N\ge3$ it strictly contains the Kulkarni domain, which equals the equicontinuity region. We also obtain nonempty largest domains for Zariski-dense cusped Hitchin groups with unipotent elements, and examples of strongly irreducible groups with no largest domain.

papers.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
papers.abstract: Agentic forecasting systems based on large language models (LLMs) are now competitive with expert human forecasters, but these systems still suffer from a critical limitation: the inability to produce forecasts that are logically consistent. For example, forecasts for related events often fail to satisfy the axioms of probability, which in turn implies that related forecasts cannot simultaneously be correct and undermines their utility for decision makers. Enforcing consistency is not trivial -- naive approaches (e.g., projection onto the set of consistent forecasts) can degrade accuracy. We argue that the key to overcoming the apparent tradeoff between consistency and accuracy lies in the reasoning which supports each forecast. We finetune a supervisory language model that leverages this reasoning to jointly reconcile inconsistencies while improving the accuracy of related forecasts. On ForecastBench, our method improves the Brier score of a retrieval-augmented GPT-5.1 forecaster by 9.3% while reducing measures of structural inconsistency by 82-90%. We interrogate our method via a comprehensive series of baselines and ablations, and find that no alternative method matches our gains in consistency and accuracy simultaneously.

papers.title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
papers.abstract: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $\gamma\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schr\"odinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.

authors.name: Bowen Chen
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Physical-Risk-Aware Decentralized Agents for Constrained Vehicle Communications
papers.abstract: Decentralized V2X resource control is challenging because each vehicle has only local observations, while reliability depends on network-wide interactions. We develop a physical-risk-aware spatio-temporal graph attention (PA-STGAT) framework for agentic V2X control. Each vehicle perceives its local interaction graph, retains short-term temporal context, and independently selects its PC5 resource and power. Network outcomes are used during centralized training to refine the shared policy. Transmitter-specific credits map reliability failures to individual vehicles. A dual-priced graph term further converts network violations into coordination signals for discrete resource selection, with higher priority on short time-to-collision links. Experiments show higher raw-policy reliability than the tested graph-based baselines. Under filtered execution, PA-STGAT meets the nominal empirical communication requirements across all five seeds, with tradeoffs among utility, delivery reliability, resource occupancy, and filter-induced repair. Compared with GNN+MATD3, it requires fewer resource repairs but achieves lower utility and mean delivery reliability. Mechanism ablations show that removing dual-priced graph coordination causes resource-selection collapse. Density and mobility tests characterize the operating limits of empirical constraint satisfaction.

authors.name: Haoran Peng
authors.institution: United States Department of the Navy

authors.name: William Weijia Zheng
authors.institution: Hunan University of Arts and Science

papers.title: Orthogonal Scores and Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Possibly Misspecified GMM
papers.abstract: We develop Neyman orthogonal scores for GMM models that remain valid when the moment conditions may fail to hold. Existing score constructions typically require the moment conditions to hold exactly, which may fail in over-identified models, where the number of moment functions exceeds the number of parameters. We construct \emph{misspecification-robust} orthogonal score that has a closed form; it is the conventional orthogonal score plus adjustment terms, for the estimation of the Jacobian and of the weighting matrix, which are proportional to the population moment and vanish under correct specification. The moment functions may depend on nonparametric or machine learning first steps, and we show that double/debiased machine learning (DML) combined with the proposed scores and cross-fitting provides uniformly valid inference for a low-dimensional GMM estimand, while the conventional DML standard errors are inconsistent when the moment conditions fail. We illustrate the results in the partially linear instrumental variables (PLIV) model and in the local average treatment effects (LATE) model with multiple instruments.

papers.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon business workflows fail in two ways: errors accumulate as a chain of activities lengthens, and the knowledge an activity needs is written in a different vocabulary from the user's request. We study whether such workflows can be made reliable without changing the language model. Our method keeps the backbone fixed and moves the workflow definition, state and domain knowledge into versioned control assets outside the model. A state machine and machine-checkable acceptance gates enforce these assets during execution; an independent auditor grades the resulting trace. The assets are updated only after a regression check and human approval .We evaluate the method on three deployed workflows exceeding 200 steps. On Domain A, a 120-case end-to-end evaluation set shows unattended completion rising from 50% to 100%, retrieval recall from 56% to 91.67%, and end-to-end latency dropping from 440 to 159 minutes, with scenario-analysis recall rising from 45% to 93%. Two other domains were taken over by teams that did not write the assets, one in four days and one in seven days. A controlled ablation separates the two failure sources. The code is available at https://github.com/ZTE-AICloud/Co-Sight/tree/master/Co-Sight%20Harness.

authors.name: Xijun Zhu
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Ego2Flow: Benchmarking the Traffic-System Impact of Autonomous Driving on Maps Distilled from Real-World Roads
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving is predominantly evaluated through ego-vehicle safety and task completion. Its deployment in urban traffic, however, creates sustained interactions among vehicles whose collective effects remain insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Ego2Flow, a closed-loop benchmark for assessing the traffic-system impact of autonomous driving on maps distilled from real-world cities. To construct realistic 3D urban environments for sustained closed-loop traffic simulation, we develop an agent-guided map distillation framework that integrates real-world maps and observations with complementary geographic information. Through an iterative feedback mechanism and a traffic information graph that jointly guide scene generation, the framework preserves lane topology, critical road geometry and decision-relevant visual conditions while simplifying nonessential details and completing unobserved regions. Using our proposed framework, we generate and publicly release six CARLA maps from the Argoverse 2 dataset, covering the corresponding real-world regions and enabling paired comparisons of driving behavior under real and simulated observations. On these maps, Ego2Flow evaluates how autonomous driving policies affect traffic efficiency, safety, stability and energy consumption across diverse road structures. Compared with existing construction methods, our framework achieves the lowest average displacement error between planning outputs from paired real and simulated observations. We further benchmark representative driving policies to characterize their system-level impact on urban traffic. Project Page: https://github.com/Fisher-007/Ego2Flow.

authors.name: Hangyu Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
papers.abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. Together the files hold 2.18 million populated cells, and the rubrics 791 criteria. Agents work in a container with spreadsheet tools, and an agentic judge that can open the file applies the rubric. Completeness and exclusivity criteria require set-valued answers to be found in full and with nothing extra. We rank models by strict pass@1, the share of attempts that meet every criterion. Across 20 model configurations, including frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI, the top-scoring one, Gemini 4 Argon, passes only 38.3% of attempts, and the median score is 19.3%, leaving wide headroom. We release the evaluation harness and three public tasks; the other 67 are held out to protect the leaderboard from contamination.

papers.title: TailGuard-GDS: Tail-Safe Control of GPU Storage Data Movement
papers.abstract:
AI runtimes move state between NVMe storage and GPU memory on critical paths. GPUDirect Storage (GDS) removes host staging, yet our eight-H100 measurements show it is not consistently tail-optimal for semantically identical GPU-buffer operations. The preferred path varies with operation, request size, concurrency, placement, and resource contention; bandwidth and tail-latency winners can disagree. Frameworks specify what moves and when, while GPU I/O stacks expose mechanisms; neither combines phase semantics with measured tail behavior to choose a delivery plan.
  We present TailGuard-GDS, a runtime that selects a semantically equivalent plan per application phase. It profiles plans varying backend, request shape, and placement, minimizes GPU-visible tail latency under phase constraints, and revisits decisions as conditions change. Resource reuse keeps policy lookup and switching at microsecond-scale overhead.
  Integrated with PyTorch FSDP and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, TailGuard reduces FSDP step p95 by 18.4% and GPU-idle p95 by 25.3% versus the strongest fixed path. Across five eight-GPU ZeRO-3 workloads, step p95 falls 7.9-24.6% versus fixed host staging and 28.4-42.6% versus fixed GDS. Against tuned DeepSpeed AIO, TailGuard reduces step p95 by 5.6% and raises estimated throughput by 6.1%.

papers.title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations
papers.abstract: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Observation-to-observation models avoid this dependence, but most omit the recursive filtering cycle that lets DA systems carry a background state through sparse, irregular observations. We introduce WeatherDreamer, a world model that learns this cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems, without reanalysis. It infers a latent state from observations, carries it forward hour by hour with learned dynamics, corrects it each hour with new observations, and can predict what any of its observing systems would measure at any location. At held-out stations, its ensembles beat NOAA's Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) for temperature, dew point and wind out to 12 h and are better calibrated than GEFS and the ECMWF ensemble. Precipitation, cloud-top height and solar irradiance, never inputs at inference, are inferred with skill matching or exceeding operational products at short leads. Against the first guess of NOAA's Gridpoint Statistical Interpolation (GSI) DA system, WeatherDreamer's short-range departures are within 10% of GSI's at surface stations and within 25% for moisture-sensitive microwave channels, but up to five times larger for temperature-sounding channels. Never given observation errors, its learned update assumes errors close to known instrument and retrieval errors of microwave sounders and scatterometer winds. WeatherDreamer also separates viewing geometry from atmospheric state, recovering 83-96% of observed limb darkening and producing seamless nadir-view imagery. Producing an hourly global analysis in about 1.5 minutes on one GPU, WeatherDreamer shows that assimilation and forecasting can be learned together directly from observations.

papers.title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
papers.abstract: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.

authors.name: Xuechun Zhang
authors.institution: Fourth Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects. We validate that feature rankings capture meaningful local-environment information through a series of atomic swap perturbations: perturbing individual atomic sites and re-ranking features reveals spatial decay consistent with the GNN's interaction cutoff, confirming that weights encode neighbor-shell effects rather than global stoichiometric artifacts alone. Results demonstrate that feature attribution methods can remain physically interpretable even under overfitting, provided validation is rigorous. This work establishes a foundation for trustworthy interpretability in materials GNNs and sets the stage for scaling to multiple chemistries and testing generalization across compositional spaces.

papers.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction
papers.abstract: Medication prediction from electronic health records is a fixed vocabulary structured prediction problem, yet recent clinical RAG systems often treat it like open ended case based reasoning: retrieve similar patient admissions and ask an LLM to infer a medication set. This retrieval object is indirect the model receives retrieved patient records while the target is a discrete set of medication class labels. We propose a more task aligned retrieval object: a tabular population prior ranked medication class candidates from a sparse condition medication co occurrence table estimated from training admissions. Using PACERAG as a fixed downstream pipeline and replacing only its patient retriever, this drop in swap improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338 (+11.5% relative) and Jaccard from 0.218 to 0.237 on 1,004 heldout MIMIC IV admissions, with no additional LLM calls and no inference time patient index. A non LLM top k baseline reaches F1=0.248, confirming the prior is predictive before LLM integration. Aggregate population statistics can provide a more task aligned, efficient, and auditable retrieval source than patient level nearest neighbors for fixed vocabulary EHR set prediction.

papers.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
papers.abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $\Omega_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $\sigma_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $\sigma_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.

papers.title: Trainable sparse dendritic networks reveal regime-dependent roles for shunting inhibition and morphology
papers.abstract: Neural circuits must compute with noisy inputs and adapt their responses to context. How dendritic structure and synaptic integration support these functions remains unclear. We introduce DendriNet, a trainable rate-based framework with sparse excitatory and inhibitory contacts, controllable dendritic architecture and alternative integration rules. In image-classification tasks, shunting networks transmit and rely on distal dendritic signals more strongly than additive networks. Distributing limited contacts across compartments improves classification in small populations, whereas greater serial dendritic depth provides no benefit on clean images within resource-matched trees. Robustness depends on input statistics: deeper shunting trees better tolerate independent pixel noise, while addition better tolerates strong global scaling. In a contextual task with gain variation and noise, shunting improves accuracy under the training corruption but depends less on context-specific inhibition than a separately tuned additive network. Learning leak conductances partly restores shunting accuracy on dim, noise-free inputs outside the training distribution. At AlexNet width, shunting integration and learned sparse connectivity support smaller deployed networks with accuracy comparable to retrained dense layers. These results distinguish the local action of synaptic integration from the computational roles acquired by inhibitory pathways through learning, and suggest experiments on dendritic function and design principles for brain-inspired networks.

papers.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. To address this, we propose CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator for text relevance (REL) and audio quality (OVL). Following a reason-then-predict paradigm, CoTTAGE first generates an audio-grounded rationale to diagnose errors before predicting scores. Supported by over 10K newly collected human OVL annotations, CoTTAGE is first trained via supervised fine-tuning and then refined with reinforcement learning using a Thurstone-based preference objective that converts sampled score distributions into pairwise preference probabilities and rewards agreement with rankings derived from human judgments. Across six benchmarks spanning REL and OVL, CoTTAGE achieves state-of-the-art correlation with human judgments while producing human-preferred explanations to accelerate TTA development.

papers.title: Vector bundles on spin K\"ahler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
papers.abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin K\"ahler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.

papers.title: Per-Agent-Safe Navigation of Globally Driven Robot Collectives via Affine Field Design
papers.abstract: Safe navigation of robot collectives requires coordinating motion and deformation so that the collective can traverse constrained environments while ensuring each robot's safety. Existing controllers for swarmalator collectives largely rely on local control, where each robot receives an individual command, which causes the control and communication requirements to grow with the number of agents. We introduce a broadcast control formulation in which a single spatially affine field governs both the motion and deformation of the collective. The scalar component of the field regulates collective size, and its spatial gradient generates collective translation through non-reciprocal interactions. Both components enter the collective dynamics directly, which allows per-robot wall, actuation, and cohesion constraints to be enforced using control barrier functions within a single quadratic program for the whole collective. The resulting controller continuously adapts the collective size to the local environment, and enables safe passage through corridors narrower than the unconstrained collective without pre-planned resizing. We further derive how the available actuation budget determines the reachable speed and minimum passable corridor width, and we demonstrate that two independently driven collectives can simultaneously traverse a shared junction using distinct fixed phase labels without inter-collective coordination.

authors.name: Steven Ceron
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
papers.abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York, Washington, Norfolk, Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE). DySENSE offers an effective foundation for energy-efficient cities, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for city, energy, and building science. The data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skl24/MUSE2 and https://github.com/kailaisun/DySENSE

papers.title: Reusing Locomotion Training Recipes Across Humanoids via Body-Aligned Virtual Joints
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has enabled robust humanoid locomotion, yet training recipes (rewards, architectures, hyperparameters) remain hard to reuse across robots with different native joint coordinates, since policies output native joint angles while action scales, bounds, gains, and penalties are defined in those robot-specific coordinates. Existing transmission models convert native targets into actuator commands but do not standardize the coordinate interface exposed to the policy. We introduce a body-aligned virtual joint space upstream of this mapping: policy actions and observations follow a common anatomical convention, and a deterministic kinematic layer maps virtual targets to native ones, leaving the existing transmission and low-level control stack unchanged. Under a single unmodified recipe on three humanoids with different leg-axis layouts, it is the only interface that tracks accurately, keeps the feet aligned with the travel direction, and trains stably on all three, and on Unitree G1 hardware it reduces heading drift by nearly a factor of six.

authors.name: Yisoo Lee
authors.institution: Korea Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
papers.abstract: While analytical theories of transcriptional feedback loops have been well established, exact stochastic analyses of post-transcriptional feedback loops remain relatively scarce and are notoriously challenging. Here, we develop an exact theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation, in which reversible protein-mRNA binding modulates both translation and mRNA stability. We derive the state-dependent protein burst-size distribution, the steady-state protein number distribution in terms of confluent Heun functions, and an exact criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations. By comparing transcriptional and post-transcriptional networks, we reveal a reversal in their relative advantages in noise suppression and rhythm transmission: negative feedback favors post-transcriptional regulation, whereas positive feedback favors transcriptional regulation. Our results reveal how the regulatory pattern fundamentally shapes gene expression fluctuations and dynamic responses.

papers.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
papers.abstract: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Pad\'e model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

papers.title: Fibonacci Non-Abelian Quantum Hall States with Pair Structure - a classification of chiral 2-cluster many-body wave-functions
papers.abstract:
Fibonacci anyons support universal topological quantum computation. They have been proposed to emerge in fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, such as the filling-fraction $
u=	frac{2}{3}$ state described by an effective $SU(3)_2$ Chern-Simons theory, and the $
u=	frac{2}{5}$ state with a $3$-cluster structure (an $n$-cluster structure means that $n$-electron bound states form a Laughlin-type wave function of the form $(z^{(n)}_i-z^{(n)}_j)^m$). In this work, we systematically classify FQH wave functions $P(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ in the $Nightarrow\infty$ limit, through a generalized pattern of zeros (gPOZ) approach, where the wave function is determined by the leading order of zero along with the accompanying leading polynomial that develops as successive number of $z_i$'s are brought together. Within this approach, we obtain a $(
u,h,c)$-classification of wave functions with a $2$-cluster (pair) structure. Among these wave functions, those with $(h,c) = (	frac12,	frac12)$, $(	frac32,	frac{7}{10})$, $(3,	frac45)$ correspond to gapped FQH states with filling fraction $
u$ and edge-state chiral central charge $c+1$, while others with $c<0$ may be gapless. We find that even a $2$-cluster structure can give rise to Fibonacci statistics, for $(
u,h,c) = (	frac14,	frac32,	frac{7}{10})$, corresponding to the $(5,4)$ minimal model, and for $(
u,h,c) = (	frac17,3,	frac45)$, corresponding to the $(6,5)$ minimal model. We further construct an ideal $4$-body Hamiltonian whose ground state is the $(	frac14,	frac32,	frac{7}{10})$ state.

papers.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.

authors.name: Andrew W. Lo
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: A Surrogate Boundary Condition for Improved Accuracy and Performance of Local Modeling in Radiation Transport Simulations
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of tokamak designs is computationally expensive due to the complex CAD geometries required to accurately model them. Design iteration of port plugs using global transport in the full model is impractical because of the computational cost. To circumvent this, local modeling methods are used. In the local modeling method, a boundary condition is assumed on the port plug, such that particles that leave the port plug do not require transport in the surrounding global model. For this purpose, vacuum and reflective boundaries are assumed, both of which provide poor approximation of the true transport physics in the global model. To improve on current techniques, a surrogate model is presented that provides a physics-informed boundary condition for the component. A neural network is trained to reproduce the boundary condition on the component that represents the behavior of particles returning from the surrounding geometry. Monte Carlo transport is only necessary within the component, and approximate physics from the surrounding region are retained. This approach allows the design in the component to be iterated without requiring full model transport and joining of the component mesh to the global mesh in each iteration. In this work, the surrogate model is evaluated against vacuum and reflective boundaries-- outperforming both in accuracy, with surrogate predictions of the flux in the port plug differing less than 12% from the global transport solution in any given energy bin. The surrogate boundary condition is also demonstrated to be more performant than global transport for the simplified benchmark geometry.

papers.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
papers.abstract: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants. Crucially, both the elliptic schedule and Zoloflow explicitly incorporate the condition number $\kappa$ of the target distribution and reduce to the classical trig schedule in the limit $\kappa \rightarrow 1$. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow achieves minimax optimality among all oblivious score-span algorithms, attaining total-variation error $\varepsilon$ using $\Theta(\log\kappa\,\log(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ (exact) score queries. For the log-concave case, the elliptic schedule allows sampling with at most $\varepsilon$ 2-Wasserstein-error by requiring merely $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{polylog}(\kappa, 1/\varepsilon))$ score evaluations. Complementing these theoretical results, we empirically evaluate the elliptic schedule on general (non-log-concave) target distributions, including detailed comparisons with alternative schedule proposals on both synthetic benchmarks and existing image generation datasets.

papers.title: Voice-Based Conversational Agents as AI Care Assistants: Evaluating Personalization, Intervention Delivery Fidelity, and Privacy Expectations in Older Adults' Care
papers.abstract: Generative AI enables voice-based conversational agents to play more active roles in older adults' care, including personalizing support and operating alongside clinicians and care partners. This shift creates two challenges: how to personalize support while faithfully delivering evidence-based interventions, and how to manage personal-data use and sharing across AI and care stakeholders. We designed and evaluated ARC, a voice-based conversational agent that operationalizes multidomain lifestyle intervention through sessions with predefined goals, participant context, and evidence-based components. In a 3-day remote study, 80 older adults completed 473 sessions across six session types (9,183 turns; averaging 19.4 turns and 6 minutes per session). Participants reported favorable usability, acceptability, and use intentions.
