papers.title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

papers.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
papers.abstract: Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we propose a Federated Poly-Level Learning (FPLL) framework over a distributed network to tackle the PLL problems with soft constraints in a federated manner. FPLL hinges on a novel non-linear cut, i.e., $L$-cut, for the level-wise relaxation to the PLL problems. Additionally, the proposed federated algorithm is designed with adjustable parameters that allow for a flexible trade-off between its computational complexity and performance efficiency, enabling users to tune it according to specific application requirements. We also carry out non-asymptotic analysis to derive the iteration complexity for the proposed FPLL to achieve the $\epsilon$-Pareto stationary point. Extensive experiments have been undertaken to elucidate the superior efficacy of the proposed method.

papers.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. Identifying distinct burst populations and investigating their variations across active episodes provide important insights into the physical origins of repeating FRBs. In this paper, we apply an unsupervised machine learning approach to bursts from three active episodes of FRB 20121102A observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST). Our analysis reveals four distinct clusters primarily distinguished by their spectral properties. Notably, Cluster 1 exhibits bimodal-like distributions in central frequency and bandwidth and contains nearly all high-energy bursts, with a mean energy about an order of magnitude higher than those of the other clusters. It also occupies a distinct region in the width--fluence parameter space. These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics. Furthermore, the fractions of different burst clusters vary across active episodes. Cluster 1 accounts for about 27\% of the bursts in 2019, compared with about 8\% in 2022 and 2023. Cluster 2, with higher central frequencies and narrower bandwidths, has the largest fraction in 2019 and 2022, whereas Cluster 3, with broader bandwidths and intermediate central frequencies, has the largest fraction in 2023. These variations may indicate changes in the physical conditions of the emission regions or the local propagation environment across active episodes.

authors.name: Xiao Li
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Starlight: Whittle-Driven Fidelity Rescue for Satellite-Terrestrial Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: A planetary-scale quantum internet is constrained by exponential attenuation in terrestrial fibers. Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites provide a low-loss vacuum backbone, but limited satellite resources must be allocated among competing connections under continuously evolving and heterogeneous physical conditions. Existing satellite scheduling remains largely provisioning-oriented, optimizing satellite-resource assignment for aggregate entanglement delivery. Recent age-based approaches instead incorporate chronological freshness into entanglement scheduling. Neither line of work directly identifies the connections most urgently requiring satellite assistance as their physical states evolve. We propose Starlight, a demand-driven satellite-terrestrial entanglement routing architecture that targets degrading connections before their terrestrial entanglement becomes unusable. Starlight introduces Effective Age of State (EAoS), a physics-aware metric that maps heterogeneous decoherence and swapping-induced fidelity penalties onto a unified additive coordinate. Representing each connection by evolving EAoS, we formulate rescue scheduling as a Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) problem and derive a closed-form Whittle-style index approximation for top-K selection. Starlight further employs a two-timescale control plane and an asynchronous dispatch-and-mask pipeline to suppress redundant in-flight allocations. Simulations show that Starlight achieves up to 84.5% average satisfaction under constrained rescue capacity and sub-0.5-ms orchestration at 1,000 connections, while remaining robust to heterogeneous memory decay and stochastic atmospheric degradation.

authors.name: Bangguo Yuan
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: SCAR: Bridging Coarse Retrieval and Fine Localization through Candidate Reranking
papers.abstract: Natural-language point-cloud localization typically retrieves candidate map cells and then predicts a position inside each candidate, yet the final output is still determined by retrieval order. A retrieval score measures region-description relevance, not whether the coordinates a region yields are accurate: a relevant region may produce a displaced prediction, and a lower-ranked region may contain a successful one. We study the final selection problem after the candidate pool and Fine predictions are fixed---how to choose the coordinate most likely to localize successfully, and under which conditions the gain holds. We propose SCAR (Spatial Consistency-Aware Reranking). SCAR treats each cell--Fine-coordinate pair as a localization hypothesis, interprets directional relations as functions of position, and reads spatial support at the backbone's actual Fine point (Fine-conditioned Evidence Readout). It organizes this readout with center support, semantic presence, retrieval score, and geometric offsets into a 23-D representation, trains a shared scorer with localization-success labels, and at inference reranks existing hypotheses and returns their original coordinates. Experiments cover four public backbones and a corrected Des4Pos reimplementation across five domains. Excluding one protocol-reference configuration, exploratory TEST point estimates on the remaining 24 configurations show Top-1@5\,m above Original on 23 and Cell R@1 above Original on all 24. On development-set VAL, the Fine readout improves Top-1@5\,m by 5.77 percentage points (pp) over a center surrogate on corrected Des4Pos*KITTI, and the complete scoring scheme improves it by 13.98\,pp over FSR on MambaPlace$\times$nuScenesFull; the latter measures the complete scheme, not learned ranking alone.

papers.title: Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.

papers.title: Time-Consistent Evaluation of Hierarchical Code Graphs for SWE Agents
papers.abstract:
Evaluating repository-aware software engineering (SWE) agents requires strict separation between pre-existing repository knowledge and future code evolution, yet standard benchmarks frequently suffer from temporal contamination and prompt-level solution leakage. Building on the time-consistent benchmark protocol of Sun (2026), we enforce strict zero-leakage isolation across DragonFly in C++ and React in JavaScript/TypeScript, locking repository snapshots and knowledge graphs at historical cutoff commits $T_0$ and evaluating 100 post-$T_0$ pull requests across four prompt granularities: Minimal, Concise, Contextual, and Guided.
  Under this zero-leakage protocol, we conduct a matched evaluation of three context-augmentation regimes: (1) an unaugmented Baseline, (2) a flat syntax-level Tree-sitter AST graph, and (3) ServiceExplorer, a deterministic two-level hierarchical dependency graph capturing Level-1 system/package containers and Level-2 architectural modules. Across 7,200 paired evaluations spanning six foundation models across the MAI-Code Flash, Claude, and GPT-Sol families, ServiceExplorer consistently outperforms both Baseline and Tree-sitter AST across every model, repository, and prompt granularity ($+15.6\%$ to $+86.2\%$ relative $F_1$ lift, $p < 10^{-4}$), while tripling exact full-PR localization on DragonFly. Crucially, equipping an efficiency-tier or prior-generation model with ServiceExplorer consistently surpasses the unaugmented Baseline $F_1$ of the next-generation model across all evaluated families.

authors.name: Jie Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jian
authors.institution: Hunan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Generalized hydraulic neural operators turbocharging sewer digital twins
papers.abstract: Hydraulic digital twins are emerging as the next-generation paradigm for operating and managing sewer systems. Conventional hydraulic digital twinning relies on running physics-based models (e.g., Saint-Venant equations), which are computationally expensive and often too slow for real-time applications. Although surrogates (e.g., neural networks) can be fast, existing approaches are typically non-generalizable, requiring costly retraining for unseen pipes, networks, or flow conditions. Here, we develop a fast, generalized and differentiable multi-branch neural operator trained on solutions of the Saint-Venant equations that predicts in-pipe hydraulics. The learned operator reproduces complex hydraulic dynamics with high fidelity while achieving thousand- to million-fold speedups for online prediction, data assimilation, and diagnostics. Equally importantly, the learned operator generalizes to unseen pipes, networks, and flow conditions without retraining. These advances address key computational barriers to real-time sewer digital twins, opening new opportunities for more responsive flood-risk management and protection of urban water environments.

authors.name: Ruozhou Lin
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

authors.name: Wenchong Tian
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. In this work, we explore building the student directly from the teacher's weights. We propose Concertina, which folds every group of N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block that is executed N times. Each loop step carries a low-rank correction initialized from the layer it replaces, and a per-token gate mixes these corrections, to let every token recover the behavior of the original layers from a single shared block. We further design a distillation data recipe that balances general, mathematical, academic and targeted multiple-choice data, to recover all capabilities of the teacher together rather than one at the expense of another. On Qwen3-4B, a 2.27B Concertina model distilled on 22B tokens retains about 90% of the teacher on commonsense and mathematical reasoning and 84% on average across eight benchmarks. It outperforms same-size dense and layer-sharing baselines, as well as Qwen3-1.7B, which is trained on over a thousand times more data. These results suggest that a compact model need not be retrained at scale, since folding the teacher into itself and distilling it on the right data recovers most of its capabilities. Code is available at https://github.com/myboker/concertina.

authors.name: Haofan Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Nuclear dimension of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that for every discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry with Yu's Property A, the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ has nuclear dimension at most one. This answers in the negative a long-standing question of Winter and Zacharias on whether the nuclear dimension of $C^*_u(X)$ always equals the asymptotic dimension of $X$. Consequently, $dim_{nuc} C^*_u(X)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ for every discrete metric space $X$, with or without bounded geometry.

authors.name: Kang Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Causally Constrained and Uncertainty-Aware Cardiopulmonary Risk Prediction
papers.abstract: Routine chest computed tomography (CT) captures pulmonary, cardiac, and vascular phenotypes that jointly stratify lung cancer and cardiovascular disease, the two leading causes of death in lung-screening populations. Yet clinical risk calculators evaluate each disease in isolation and omit CT findings, whereas unconstrained machine learning overfits small hospital cohorts, learns treatment- and illness-confounded risk directions, and conceals uncertainty when patient records are incomplete. Here we present the Causal Envelope Agent (CE-Agent), a two-stage framework that compiles peer-reviewed epidemiological evidence into explicit constraints on risk-factor weights before any outcome is seen, while estimating local baseline risk and newly added CT phenotypes from cohort data. At deployment, closed-form uncertainty propagation accounts for missing clinical or CT inputs within milliseconds per patient, running over two orders of magnitude faster than Monte Carlo sampling and returning calibrated risk intervals that direct chart review and selective imaging to borderline patients. Across 53,452 lung-screening participants from 33 US hospitals and 6,814 multi-ethnic adults, CE-Agent outperforms cardiovascular calculators in lung screening, exceeds the Pooled Cohort Equations on hard atherosclerotic events while correcting their 1.7-fold risk overestimation, and generalizes from a single hospital or CT scanner to external sites while lowering required sample sizes up to fivefold. Applied unchanged to lung cancer, CE-Agent matches established screening models with accurate calibration even when restricted to risk-factor directions alone, and pairing both predictions improves joint cardiopulmonary triage from a single screening visit.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Yang
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Risk Evaluation with Low-Rank Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study distributionally robust risk under perturbations restricted to low-rank matrices whose row and column spaces are shared across observations, focusing on how much worst-case risk this restriction sacrifices and how to compute the restricted worst case. Under moment or Wasserstein budgets, we derive quantitative bounds on the gap between the unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risks, characterize when the gap vanishes, and identify the smallest lossless row and column dimensions. To generate worst-case perturbations, we apply projected gradient ascent to a curvature-corrected concave problem and derive computable risk certificates. We establish global sublinear convergence for the corrected objective and linear convergence to a worst-case distribution when the budget constraint is sufficiently active.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract:
We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag
  \begin{cases} - \Delta u &= \lambda K(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\lambda$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $\lambda$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.

papers.title: Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Inverse problems arise in many applications where the task is to recover unknown parameters from indirect or noisy observations. In contrast to forward problems, where outputs are directly computed from known inputs, inverse problems are designed to infer the underlying variables from the observed effect. Inverse problems are often ill-posed, so regularization is needed to compute reasonable solutions. One form of regularization incorporates prior knowledge about the unknown parameters in the form of prior distributions. However, in many settings, large prior covariance matrices pose computational bottlenecks for solving inverse problems. To address this, we study approximations of large covariance matrices via structured Kronecker-Toeplitz products and demonstrate how these approximations can be used to solve inverse problems. We exploit the Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block structure induced by the covariance kernel to construct compact approximations that are orders of magnitude cheaper to store and invert. These approximations are deployed as prior covariance surrogates in Bayesian inverse problems solved via generalized hybrid iterative methods. We demonstrate that the Kronecker-Toeplitz approximation attains lower relative approximation error than existing matrix approximations, exhibits rapid error decay with rank, and enables efficient matrix-vector products. Applications to 2D seismic tomography reconstruction problems illustrate the practical utility of these methods.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
papers.abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

papers.title: Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers
papers.abstract: We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by \'etale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.

papers.title: EViDS: An Environment--Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Simulation Platform for Intelligent Chassis Development
papers.abstract: The development of intelligent chassis increasingly requires the integration of environmental and perception information with high-fidelity vehicle dynamics to support environment-aware intelligent chassis control. However, existing autonomous-driving simulators and professional vehicle-dynamics tools are generally developed for different purposes, making it difficult to integrate environmental information, vehicle dynamics, and chassis algorithms. This paper proposes EViDS, an Environment-Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Simulation Platform for Intelligent Chassis Development. EViDS integrates CARLA-based environment and sensor simulation with CarSim-based high-fidelity vehicle dynamics. Reference-pose-based state alignment and multi-rate interaction maintain spatial and temporal consistency, while ray-casting-based tire-road interaction transfers environmental information to the vehicle-dynamics model. Scenario configuration, synchronized data acquisition, and algorithm interfaces further support intelligent chassis development. The platform is evaluated through environment-dynamics interaction tests with vehicle-dynamics consistency comparisons, together with intelligent chassis applications. Results show that EViDS preserves vehicle-dynamics characteristics, reliably transfers environmental information, and supports online closed-loop intelligent chassis control, providing a unified simulation basis for environment-aware intelligent chassis development and validation.

papers.title: Simulating Space Bounded Read-$k$ PTMs with Space Bounded Read-Once PTMs
papers.abstract: We show that read-$k$ Probabilistic Turing Machines with bounded space $S$ and running time $T$ can be simulated by read-once Probabilistic Turing Machines with error $\varepsilon$, running in space $ O(k^2 (S + \log (n+ T)) + \log (1/\epsilon))$ and time $\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \cdot 2^{O\left(k^2\left(S+\log(n+T) \right)\right)}$. As a direct consequence we show that read-$k$ $\mathsf{BPL}$ is equal to $\mathsf{BPL}$, for any constant $k$. Recently OpenAI announced that $\mathsf{BPL} = \mathsf{L}$. If this is true then our result immediately implies that read-$k$ $\mathsf{BPL}$ is equal to $\mathsf{L}$.

authors.name: Shengtang Huang
authors.institution: Hubei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
papers.abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historical chlorophyll-a fields and climatological information. Compared with the operational 0.25$^\circ$ Copernicus global ocean biogeochemical forecasting system, ChlCast reduces mean absolute error and root mean square error by 70.74% and 47.63%, respectively, against satellite-derived Level-4 chlorophyll-a fields, and by 35.03% and 13.07% against independent BGC-Argo in situ observations. Coastal case studies further show that the 4-km forecasts retain coastal gradients and localized concentration maxima that are weakened by coarse-grid averaging. These results demonstrate the potential of observation-driven deep learning for high-resolution forecasting of surface chlorophyll-a variability at the near-global scale.

authors.name: Yong Jiang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Zheng Jiang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Suixiang Shi
authors.institution: National Marine Data and Information Service

papers.title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
papers.abstract: We present a multidimensional statistics-informed neural network (SINN) framework for learning and generating trajectories of multicomponent stochastic processes. SINN is built upon a deterministic recurrent neural network that takes streams of white-noise sequences as input and generates ensembles of stochastic trajectories whose statistical properties match those of the underlying stochastic dynamics. While SINN has been demonstrated for various one-dimensional non-Markovian processes, extending it to multidimensional processes is essential for real-world applications. Here, we present key developments toward this goal. First, because direct estimation of multivariate probability density functions (PDFs) becomes computationally challenging with increasing dimension, we represent joint-distribution information using collections of one-dimensional PDFs constructed from linear combinations of the process components. Second, to accommodate the larger set of statistical objectives required to characterize multidimensional processes, we adopt a self-adaptive loss-balancing strategy that dynamically weights the components of the total loss function. Third, we introduce a reference-normalized validation framework that interprets statistical discrepancies relative to the finite-sample variability between independent target ensembles. We also investigate the role of the input white-noise dimension in SINN performance. We evaluate the proposed approach using a Langevin benchmark based on two coupled Duffing oscillators and further demonstrate its applicability to the Langevin dynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice Lotka-Volterra model. Our results demonstrate that the multidimensional SINN framework provides a practical approach for modeling multidimensional stochastic dynamics.

papers.title: ERA: Error-Resistant Autonomous Object Navigation with Predicted Depth
papers.abstract: Depth and 3D foundation models can predict geometry from RGB images, allowing zero-shot object navigation without a depth sensor. However, when predicted depth is mapped as if it came from a sensor, view-dependent errors accumulate in the map, remove exploration goals, and end the search before the agent can observe and correct them. We propose ERA, a training-free object navigation system that replaces the depth sensor with depth predicted from RGB images and poses. ERA follows a paradigm we call Move with Error: movement provides new views that correct map errors, and the corrected map enables further movement. It realizes this paradigm with revisable occupancy and with exploration from reachable viewpoints, which continues the search when no frontier remains, and verifies the target across views before stopping. On three benchmarks, ERA achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods without depth sensors. Its map and exploration components also raise VLFM's success from 10.8% to 61.7% under the same predicted depth. We further deploy ERA on a real robot.

authors.name: Shunyang Huang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
papers.abstract: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

authors.name: Zixuan Jiang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Toward the Minimal Set of Information Inequalities in Regenerating Codes: An Algebraic Approach
papers.abstract: Information-theoretic outer bounds for exact-repair regenerating codes can be formulated as linear programs, but the associated Shannon-type systems contain many implicit equalities and redundant inequalities. We directly specify a reduced system for the $(n,n-1,n-1)$ exact-repair model using the closure structure induced by its repair dependencies. Nonempty closed sets index the reduced joint-entropy coordinates, and inseparable edges determine the defining inequalities. We prove equivalence with the initial system by characterizing its implicit equalities and establishing sufficient redundancy criteria. We also give an algorithm that constructs the directly defined system for any $n$, count its entropy coordinates, and derive an explicitly computable upper bound on its number of inequalities. For every $n\ge2$, we prove that the reduced system has no implicit equalities and that each distinct defining inequality is nonredundant and defines a facet in the nonempty closed-set coordinate space. Exact enumerations for $n\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ verify the reported system sizes.

papers.title: Resource Management and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-IRS Assisted Maritime Edge Computing Networks
papers.abstract: With the exponential growth of maritime wireless devices and the rapid development of maritime applications, traditional maritime communication networks encounter communication and computation limitations in supporting computation-intensive and latency-critical tasks. Edge computing and Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) have emerged as promising techniques to improve communication and computation services for maritime devices with limited computation capabilities and battery capacity. This paper studies an IRS Mounted on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UIRS) assisted maritime edge computing network, in which the UIRS is deployed to assist the transmission from Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) to the edge server via Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) protocol. We propose a resource management and trajectory optimization scheme by jointly optimizing subslot duration, offloading ratios, transmit power, edge computation capability allocation, UIRS phase shifts and UIRS trajectory, aiming at minimizing the overall energy consumption. Since the non-convex nature of the optimization problem, we propose a two-layered method by decomposing the original problem into two subproblems. The top-layered subproblem is solved by the Semi-Definite Relaxation (SDR) method and the underlying-layered subproblem is solved by the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme can effectively and efficiently reduce overall energy consumption.

authors.name: Bin Lin
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xu Hu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Projective surfaces with infinite fundamental group and trivial profinite completion
papers.abstract: For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\) of odd order, we construct a smooth complex projective surface with infinite topological fundamental group and trivial \'{e}tale fundamental group. The isomorphism types of its finite subgroups are precisely those of the subgroups of \(A\). The surface is Kobayashi hyperbolic and has Stein universal cover.

papers.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
papers.abstract: Moir\'e metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moir\'e metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moir\'e unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted. We demonstrate this approach using reflective moir\'e metasurfaces constructed from patterns with p6m, p3m1, and p4m plane-group symmetries, achieving one-, two-, three-, four-, and six-beam radiation states with continuously tunable steering trajectories. Beyond symmetry-based design, we identify two additional degrees of freedom for beam multiplicity control. Selecting different rotation centers reshapes the phase distributions of the dominant Fourier coefficients, enabling further manipulation of beam multiplicity and spatial arrangement, while varying the relative twist angle alters the pairing of Fourier components, inducing transitions between distinct beam multiplicities. These findings establish a systematic framework for versatile and reconfigurable multibeam wavefront engineering.

authors.name: Shaojie Ma
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Shuo Liu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Rate Optimal Streaming Codes Under an Extended Delay Profile for Three-Node Relay Networks
papers.abstract: We study streaming codes for a three-node relay network with burst lengths $b_1,b_2$ and an end-to-end decoding delay $T$. Let $u=\max\{b_1,b_2\}$ and $v=\min\{b_1,b_2\}$, and write $T-v=pu+q$, where $T\ge u+v$ and $0\le q<u$. We develop two binary constructions, SR and SR-2, using extended delay profiles that allow the relay to forward causally invertible combinations of current and past source symbols. The SR construction attains the non-adaptive rate upper bound whenever \[ \frac{T-u-v}{2u-v}\le\left\lfloor\frac{T-u-v}{u}\right\rfloor. \] SR-2 enlarges this range under the sufficient condition \[ q(v-q)\le(p-1)u(u-v). \] These constructions complement the known divisibility and large-delay regimes. We also establish two limitations of systematic ordinary coordinate forwarding. First, it cannot attain the rate upper bound when $0<T-u-v<v$. Second, for equal burst lengths $b$, it attains the bound if and only if $b\mid(T-2b)$; a quantitative upper bound gives a strictly positive rate gap in every nondivisible case. These converses allow nonlinear components and predetermined time variation within the stated ordinary-forwarding architecture. Existing adaptive schemes for equal bursts approach the same rate upper bound asymptotically using time-varying convolutional codes and lie outside the non-adaptive setting considered here.

authors.name: Ke Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yaqiang Zhang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
papers.abstract: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslant\mu_2/(\mu_n-\delta)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $\mu_2$ and $\mu_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $\delta$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.

authors.name: Yifan Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Identification and Inference of Bi-directional Causal Effects in Mendelian Randomization without Instrument Selection
papers.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instruments to estimate causal effects. Bidirectional MR usually uses two reversed unidirectional analyses, but feedback can invalidate instruments in at least one direction and induce correlated pleiotropy. We model both traits as a stable cyclic system and estimate both directional effects from GWAS summary data without instrument selection or a prespecified valid-instrument subset. After LD score normalisation, marginal associations form a heteroscedastic noisy independent component analysis model, assuming the variants' direct effects on the two traits are independent. If those effects are non-Gaussian, this identifies the total-effect matrix up to scaling and permutation; no-self-feedback and stability of the system further resolve these ambiguities. We develop an estimator based on noise-adjusted second- and fourth-order moments, avoiding inversion of the high-dimensional linkage disequilibrium matrix and having computational cost linear in the number of variants. Under weak local dependence, we establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and validity of a chromosome-respecting moving block bootstrap. Simulations show negligible bias, generally reliable interval coverage, and higher rejection rates for nonzero directional effects than focusing-based tests. Three real-data applications illustrate how joint analysis of feedback systems can yield causal decompositions differing from two separate unidirectional analyses.

authors.name: Liyuan Mo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
papers.abstract: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.

papers.title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
papers.abstract: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception. We propose a decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combining a {pilot-aware complex transformer} (PACT) estimator, banded linear minimum mean-square error equalization, and neural normalized min-sum decoding. PACT jointly estimates the frequency-domain channel and effective time-domain PN through interacting complex-valued branches. Decoder-derived pseudo-pilots and continuous constellation-aware confidence guide second-round refinement through PACT inputs and attention, with parameters shared across rounds. At $E_b/N_0=30$~dB, the PACT receiver achieves approximately $70\%$ and $57\%$ lower code-block error rates than the best-performing learning-based baseline in the two benchmark settings, respectively. Frozen-weight tests further demonstrate applicability across channel/PN models, carrier frequencies, and FFT/bandwidth configurations.

papers.title: Beyond Attack-Based Accuracy: Rethinking Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Through Structural Gradient Alignment
papers.abstract: Visual adversarial robustness remains a fundamental security property as vision systems evolve from conventional classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs) and large vision-language models (LVLMs), with visual inputs remaining an attack surface across generations. Yet existing evaluation methods often depend on prescribed attacks, in-distribution data, extensive probing, or classifier-specific formulations, limiting external auditing of diverse models. We introduce Structural Gradient Alignment (SGA), a complementary robustness metric measuring the structural alignment between input content and objective-conditioned local model sensitivity. SGA uses a few randomly sampled, unlabeled public probes that need not follow the downstream task distribution and only one input-gradient computation per model--probe pair. Across 38 distinct DNNs, VLMs, and LVLMs, SGA produces rankings consistent with attack-based references. Without robustness references, uncalibrated SGA achieves $83.72\%$ average pairwise agreement across eight public-probe conditions, outperforming the strongest overall baseline in all eight by $9.38$ percentage points on average. With known robustness orders of anchor models, calibrated SGA increases agreement to $85.36\%$. These results demonstrate an attack-agnostic, computationally efficient robustness signal across conventional DNNs, VLMs, and autoregressive LVLMs, downstream tasks, threat norms, probe distributions, and evaluator-knowledge settings. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/azrealwang/SGA.

authors.name: Zhe Jin
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Consistent Bayesian Adaptive Quotient Graph Framework for Graph-Informed Random Partition Models
papers.abstract: Bayesian graph-informed random partition models are widely used to model heterogeneity in structured data. A prominent approach assigns a prior directly on the space of contiguous partitions of a pre-determined graph G; however, such models are not data-adaptive and can be computationally infeasible for large graphs. To address these limitations, we propose a Bayesian adaptive quotient graph framework that induces partitions through a two-level hierarchical prior: a prior is first imposed on quotient graphs of G, followed by a conditional prior on a reduced contiguous partition space induced by each quotient graph. We develop high-level assumptions that guide the construction of the two-level prior such that the reduced space retains desirable partitions. We further establish high-level assumptions for posterior concentration on desirable quotient graphs and partitions. The framework can be readily embedded into many existing Bayesian hierarchical models with latent cluster structures as a contiguous random partition prior. As a specific example, we apply the proposed framework to the spatial random partition model proposed in Huang and Sang (2026). The resulting model adapts to the unknown number of clusters, achieves a faster clustering-consistency contraction rate, and yields substantially lower partition error and computation time in simulations. Finally, we apply the resulting model to a large spatial transcriptomics dataset to demonstrate its practical utility.

papers.title: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
papers.abstract: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. The reduced longitudinal focusing, combined with high total $R/Q$ of these cavities, can make the beam susceptible to the periodic transient beam loading (PTBL) effect, a multibunch instability characterized by slow oscillations in bunch centroids and lengths and by its resistance to conventional feedback damping. In this work, building on a recent proposal of applying reactive feedback to control the PTBL effect, we developed a frequency-domain theoretical model, including the feedback voltage in the linearized Vlasov equation to derive a Lebedev equation modified by the feedback transfer function. The reactive feedback was also implemented in the time domain in the macroparticle tracking code \texttt{STABLE}. The methods were applied to the parameters of the double-rf system of the MAX IV storage ring. Both approaches show that, above a threshold gain, an idealized pure reactive feedback is able to suppress the PTBL effect, with good agreement between theory and simulations across beam currents and $R/Q$ values. Realistic hardware limitations were included in the analysis, determining the limits for feedback gain, latency, and bandwidth, which are compatible with existing bunch-by-bunch feedback systems. Using the HALF storage ring parameters, the semi-analytical results indicate that the reactive feedback can be extended to suppress the PTBL effect in triple-rf systems, albeit at higher threshold gains than for double-rf systems.

papers.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
papers.abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. Sustaining performance therefore requires both keeping evolving plans feasible and comparing the value of resource allocations with the alternatives they displace. Recent benchmarks increasingly evaluate LLM agents in continuing operations, but give less attention to how agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing resource allocations as opportunities change. We introduce OutfitterBench, where agents manage an outdoor-equipment rental business for 200 days, purchasing from a 46-product catalog and handling roughly 1,100 reservation requests. Under a fixed capital ceiling, reservations and uncertain walk-in demand compete for reusable equipment whose availability changes over time. Experiments with seven frontier LLMs show that several agents underperform a simple rule-based baseline, while only the leading agent consistently surpasses it. Trajectory analysis shows that some agents apply known constraints inconsistently and make new decisions that conflict with existing commitments. Agents with more reliable fulfillment can still secure low returns from comparable commitments or delay resource reallocation. The leading agent better connects preparation with economic choices but also misses opportunities for more profitable asset use. These findings highlight limitations in sustaining coherent resource plans and reassessing their value over time. The benchmark code is publicly available at https://github.com/adminblackjack/OutfitterBench.

papers.title: RiverScan: Learning to Accumulate on River Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate runoff prediction across large river basins requires models to capture heterogeneous local hydrological responses and their accumulation downstream. River-network connectivity provides a natural structure for this task, but using it effectively requires learning how to combine contributions from subcatchments of different sizes. We frame this challenge as learning to accumulate and introduce RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence. RiverScan recursively combines local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states in topological order. Contributing-area fractions account for subcatchment size, while learned retention controls how upstream information persists downstream. Experiments on 608 stations in the Danube basin show that RiverScan outperforms the evaluated temporal and graph baselines in overall predictive performance. Structural controls and ablations demonstrate that composing heterogeneous subcatchment representations in a manner aligned with hydrological accumulation substantially improves runoff prediction, with the benefits of correct topology growing along the river-network hierarchy. These findings establish physically structured accumulation as an effective inductive bias for hydrological modeling and motivate finer-grained, fully distributed AI-based hydrological models.

authors.name: He Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SPLIT-MOR: Fast and Accurate Model Order Reduction for Nonlinear Transient Thermal Simulation of 2.5D/3D ICs
papers.abstract: Fast and accurate transient thermal simulation is essential to thermal reliability analysis and dynamic thermal management of advanced packages, and model order reduction (MOR) techniques are widely applied to overcome the efficiency bottleneck of rigorous numerical methods. However, nonlinear terms including temperature-dependent leakage power, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity prevent the application of conventional linear MOR, while hyper-reduction solutions require costly nonlinear training data. In this work, we propose SPLIT-MOR (Subdomain-wise Piecewise Linearization with Interval Tensors), a novel nonlinear MOR method that requires no additional training set. SPLIT-MOR computes reduced component tensors by subdomain clustering and temperature-interval partitioning in the offline stage, and updates the reduced coefficient matrices and load vectors efficiently in the online stage. Experimental results show that the online solving time of SPLIT-MOR achieves up to an 830x speedup over COMSOL and a 7.5x speedup over the state-of-the-art hyper-reduction method MDEIM, with a 27x total reduction in the offline time. The relative average error remains below 0.11%, and the maximum error is below 0.86 degrees Celsius, demonstrating the high accuracy of our method.

papers.title: X-Strata: Separating Aneurysms and Overlapping Vessels into Layers from 2D X-ray Angiography
papers.abstract: An X-ray angiogram sums every structure along a ray into one pixel. When vessels cross an aneurysm, they obscure part of it and mix their contrast into its filling curve. We present X-Strata, a network that separates a cine angiogram into three layers: the complete aneurysm sac, the vessels in front of it, and the vessels behind it. Contrast timing indicates how much each layer contributes to a pixel, and parallax between two views indicates their order, which a single view cannot determine. X-Strata first estimates the layers and their contrast curves, then uses the second view to assign vessels to the front or back layer, and lifts all layers into 3D. It learns from layer labels projected from same-session 3D rotational angiography, but needs only 2D cine runs and their acquisition geometry at inference. On 220 held-out patients from three centers (122 external), two-view X-Strata ranks first among 14 baselines, including VGGT and C$^2$RV, in recovering the sac where vessels overlap it (Dice 0.693 internal, 0.641 external) and in ordering the layers (balanced accuracy 0.703, 0.659). Its order accuracy exceeds that of all 11 end-to-end baselines by at least 4.1 points internally and 3.3 externally (Holm-adjusted $p < 0.001$) and grows with view separation. Recovered 3D sac surfaces have a median Chamfer distance of 0.34 mm on the internal cohort. X-Strata may therefore provide layered aneurysm and vessel information, including 3D sac shape, for patients who undergo only 2D angiography.

authors.name: Yakun Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hao Gao
authors.institution: Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
papers.abstract: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.

papers.title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract:
Hallucination benchmarks for text-to-image generation are predominantly designed around diffusion models, limiting their diagnostic value for visual autoregressive (VAR) models and the development of mitigation methods. We identify two limitations in existing prompt construction paradigms: many prompts are no longer challenging for modern generators, while category-based construction relies on recurring object-attribute-relation templates and rarely tests interactions among multiple visual requirements within a single image.
  We introduce InfiHall-Bench, a controlled benchmark of 411 prompts constructed by systematically composing five foundational and visually verifiable skills: attribute binding, spatial relation, action relation, part consistency, and scene consistency. Each prompt covers 4.05 annotated skills on average, enabling the evaluation of hallucinations under diverse combinations of visual requirements. Using this benchmark, we find that hallucinations in VAR models exhibit a scale-wise persistence pattern: semantic errors can emerge at different autoregressive scales and are rarely corrected by subsequent fine-scale steps.
  Motivated by this observation, we propose Confidence-Masked Hallucination Mitigation (CMHM), which estimates the prediction confidence of target visual tokens at each autoregressive scale during teacher-forced fine-tuning. CMHM downweights reliably predicted tokens, allowing optimization to focus on uncertain predictions across scales. Experiments show that InfiHall-Bench distinguishes models that existing compositional benchmarks rate as comparable, while CMHM consistently outperforms uniform LoRA fine-tuning for VAR-based text-to-image generation.

authors.name: Yuxia Qiao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
papers.abstract: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another. We introduce GT-FENG (General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding), the first general framework to unify contextual/temporal correctness and rule-based error attribution across law, policy, and other rule-governed domains. GT-FENG checks answers against the applicable rules and identifies documented rules that match incorrect answers. It shows that when multiple rules give the same value, the answer alone cannot tell which rule the model used. In Medicaid income-limit answers from two models, documenting the asked state's own records reduces the number of wrong answers that match only other states' values by 68-78%, and more than half of stable wrong answers then match two or more documented sources. GT-FENG provides a foundation for evaluating language models in rule-governed domains and for future benchmarks and evaluation toolkits. We release GT-FENG as an open-source Python package, gtfeng.

papers.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a unital \(\sigma\)-weakly closed subalgebra \(\mathfrak A\) of a von Neumann factor \(\mathcal M\) of type \(\mathrm{II}_1\), whose diagonal is \(\mathfrak D=\mathfrak A\cap\mathfrak A^*=\mathbb CI\). We show that there exist uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations from \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\mathfrak D\) with respect to each of which \(\mathfrak A\) is a maximal subdiagonal algebra. Let \(\tau\) denote the unique normalized faithful normal trace on \(\mathcal M\). The conditional expectation associated with \(\tau\) preserves this trace, whereas none of the other conditional expectations is preserved by any nonzero finite trace on \(\mathcal M\). This gives a negative answer to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras in \emph{Amer. J. Math.} \textbf{89}(1967), 578--642.

papers.title: INC-SRv6: In-Network Route Exploration and Fast Failover Using Segment Routing Headers in Dynamic UAV Networks
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks require a network provisioning mechanism that guarantees delivery and latency quality of service (QoS) under dynamic conditions in next-generation airborne mesh networks by continuously learning and repairing multi-hop paths under rapid link turnover without flooding the control plane. This paper presents INC-SRv6, an in-network computing routing mechanism that repurposes the IPv6 Segment Routing Header (SRH) and its Segments Left (SL) pointer into a self-learning, fast-failover distributed control plane. Rather than treating the SRH as a static source-committed vector, INC-SRv6 uses the active SL pointer to partition the segment list in flight: slots ahead of SL provide capacity for hop-by-hop next-hop recording, while the suffix behind SL serves as an in-band multi-destination reachability vector. Through this dual-zone header discipline, transit routers extract distance-weighted reachability updates from arriving suffixes, gate admission by single-pass confidence with bounded binary probing, advance or reverse SL deterministically, and restore pre-transmission SRH state for local failover upon link loss. Simulations across 200-node 3D UAV networks show that under high-speed flight and repeated 20% relay outages, INC-SRv6 improves packet delivery over reactive routing (92.12% versus 89.12%) while cutting 95th-percentile tail delay from 121.26 to 8.84 ms and control packets by 35.8%, with a 4-byte compact uSID stride model reducing SRv6 control bytes by over 52%.

papers.title: Predicting Individual Dark Matter Halo Concentrations from Their Assembly Histories
papers.abstract: We present an empirical model for predicting concentration parameters of individual dark matter halos in cold and warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies over z=0-5. Constructed using a large suite of cosmological N-body simulations, our model separately incorporates cosmic expansion (linear growth factor), mass scale (linear density fluctuations), halo mass assembly histories via the Extended Press-Schechter (EPS) scaled formation variable, plus a WDM damping term tied to the half-mode mass. It works for both virial and 200 $\rho_{crit}$ halo definitions. Across all tested cosmologies and redshifts, our global logarithmic fit gives concentration scatter ~0.09 dex for relaxed halos and ~0.09 to 0.10 dex for all halos. While relaxed halos maintain nearly constant scatter near 0.09 dex, the scatter of all halos at z>3 increases from 0.10 to 0.18 dex, revealing substantial violent-relaxation impacts on high-redshift halo structure. At fixed mass, concentration scatter is dominated by assembly history. We extract the scaled formation variable's probability distribution function (PDF) from merger trees and find departures from standard EPS theory. This PDF is narrower in WDM than LCDM due to suppressed small-scale perturbations and rapid, delayed monolithic collapse near the WDM truncation scale. Monte Carlo realizations with our formulae reproduce concentration distributions and match our prior peak-concentration model, whereas standard EPS underestimates concentrations from delayed-formation bias. Our framework offers a transparent, computationally lightweight tool to predict individual halo concentrations across diverse cosmological models.

authors.name: Tian-Cheng Luan
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exact Failure Probabilities for d-Choice Cuckoo Hashing
papers.abstract: In d-choice cuckoo hashing, each of n items must be placed in one of its d candidate slots in a table of M slots, and every slot holds at most one item. We give a polynomial-time dynamic programming algorithm to compute the exact probability that no valid placement exists. Our method also handles the variant with separate tables.

authors.name: Chenyang Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Complete TE/TM Separability in Fully Anisotropic Waveguides
papers.abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for complete transverse-electric/transverse-magnetic (TE/TM) separability in waveguides homogeneously filled with a fully anisotropic and lossless medium. The permittivity and permeability tensors are Hermitian positive-definite and may contain nonzero transverse--longitudinal coupling terms. Complete TE/TM separation occurs if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the corresponding transverse--longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality relation after complex conjugation. The longitudinal constitutive entries remain independent apart from positive definiteness. The condition is derived directly from the source-free Maxwell equations, and independent analyses of the TE and TM modes lead to the same material relation. Since no boundary condition enters the derivation, the criterion is independent of the boundary type. Full-vector waveguide mode analyses using our in-house programs for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides, with material tensors satisfying and violating the condition, agree with the theoretical results.

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jie Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
papers.abstract: In mineral exploration, verifying geological hypotheses relies on designing a variety of geochemical experiments. While large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate downstream geoscientific data analysis, a crucial upstream capability remains largely unexplored: automated geochemical experimental design, i.e., deciding which experiments to conduct before committing to costly laboratory work. Evaluating this capability of LLM agents is difficult for two reasons. First, geochemical experiments exhibit high methodological diversity and subjectivity: to test the same hypothesis, different geologists may choose different minerals and instruments, so no single protocol can serve as the reference answer. Second, open-ended experimental plans resist representation as structured labels, which makes objective scoring difficult. To address these challenges, we introduce MineralExp, a benchmark that reformulates geochemical experimental design as a hypothesis-based experiment selection problem, i.e., a multi-label classification problem. We abstract concrete instrument names and procedural details into a shared taxonomy of 19 experimental types across five mineral-system processes: Source, Transport, Deposition, Modification, and Preservation. This taxonomy yields deterministic multi-label targets while accommodating diverse experimental protocols. Constructed from published ore-deposit literature and verified by domain experts, MineralExp comprises 277 cases and 1,572 reference experimental plans. Given a geological hypothesis and initial context, an LLM agent selects the relevant tasks and generates concrete experimental plans, which are scored by multi-label classification metrics and an LLM-as-a-Judge metric. The experimental results show that current agents generally achieve high recall but low precision, tending to propose more experiments than are necessary to test the hypothesis.
