papers.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
papers.abstract: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from $0\%$ in single-pass synthesis to $81\%$. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by $2{\times}\text{--}5{\times}$ and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

authors.name: Xufeng Zhan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yuanzhi Liang
authors.institution: Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences

papers.title: Training-point consistency of kernel ridge regression with varying correlation scales
papers.abstract: The scale parameter in kernel ridge regression plays a pivotal role in modeling the correlation structure of data. In modern applications, sampling density and the underlying correlation range often change simultaneously, making a fixed-scale assumption highly restrictive. However, establishing asymptotic theories under varying scale parameters is fundamentally challenging. To address this gap, this paper develops a unified theoretical framework for kernel ridge regression under varying scale parameters. We establish that, on uniform tensor grids with product exponential kernels, the consistency of the training-point risk holds if and only if the effective local sample size diverges to infinity. This sharp criterion universally covers all regimes along arbitrary deterministic scale sequences, seamlessly unifying the long-range, fixed-scale, and short-range. Furthermore, we provide an explicit, signal-independent construction of a deterministic regularization penalty that guarantees this consistency. Numerical experiments illustrate the criterion and the corresponding penalty across all the three regimes.

authors.name: Weiyan Mu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
papers.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

authors.name: Jianjun Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\bar\sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)=f, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+\delta, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

papers.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
papers.abstract: Recent advances in weight-space programming (WSP) have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can directly inspect and modify neural network weights without conventional gradient-based training. While this capability opens new possibilities for model improvement, it also raises an important security question: Can LLMs exploit weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks? To answer this question, we present an empirical security study of LLM-driven weight-space programming for backdoor injection. Specifically, we investigate whether general-purpose LLMs can directly modify the weights of target models according to natural-language instructions, without accessing task-specific data, performing forward passes, or computing gradients. We evaluate five LLMs as weight editors across three target architectures: an MLP on MNIST, ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on AG News. Our experiments reveal three key findings. First, LLM-driven weight editing can successfully inject backdoors across different architectures while largely preserving clean performance. Second, successful attacks can require remarkably few parameter modifications, including only six parameters for the MLP and 0.02% of the weights for a fine-tuned Qwen model. Third, editing capabilities vary substantially across LLMs and target architectures: although all five LLMs successfully backdoor the MLP, only GPT-6 Astra succeeds across all three targets. These findings highlight an emerging security risk of weight-space programming and underscore the importance of safeguarding LLM-driven weight editing.

papers.title: Influence of transverse oscillatory shear on the viscous fingering instability
papers.abstract: Oscillatory shear can delay the onset of viscous fingering. In addition, uniaxial translational shear also breaks the symmetry of the resulting pattern so that the interface evolves differently depending on its direction of propagation relative to the shear axis. We observe a delayed fingering onset and reduced subsequent finger growth rate for all directions as shear speed or amplitude increases. However, shear widens fingers growing in the direction perpendicular to shear and elongates those in the parallel directions. After onset, neighboring fingers in the perpendicular directions can reconnect near their base when the shear amplitude exceeds approximately five times the excess linear finger wavelength at the onset. Concentration profiles reveal smoother azimuthal edges and overlapping structures behind the tips. These observations show that shear smears individual fingers and connects neighboring ones. This correlates lateral fingering interactions with radial propagation.

papers.title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
papers.abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Li\'enard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.

papers.title: Open-World Scene Deocclusion
papers.abstract: Recovering the complete appearance of occluded objects from a single image is a fundamental problem for scene understanding and image editing. Real-world scenes are challenging due to clutter, complex spatial occlusions, and diverse object categories. Existing methods often struggle when occlusion involves background surfaces or objects that are not explicitly detected, and fail to resolve the cyclic occlusion dependencies that frequently occur in natural scenes. We introduce a training-free, open-world scene deocclusion framework that recovers the full amodal appearance of detected or user-selected objects from a single RGB image, decomposing the scene into depth-ordered RGBA layers that are geometrically plausible, semantically faithful, and visually consistent with the visible scene. Extensive experiments show that our approach improves scene-level deocclusion, producing coherent and realistic reconstructions in real-world settings. Code will be available on the project page: https://sashjk.github.io/owsd/

papers.title: A Unified Framework for First- and Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods for Planar Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{\"u}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.

authors.name: Yujing Yan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Truthful compromise and insurance on a sphere
papers.abstract: Can public choice without transfers insure conflicting interests when action intensity is fixed? We require truthful reporting for every increasing-concave evaluation of alignment with private ideals. On a sphere, efficiency at profiles with at most three ideal directions forces fixed-weight random dictatorship; weaker tests suffice in two and three dimensions. From four dimensions, binary efficiency permits committees to insure members by placing outcome risk orthogonally to their reports. We identify restrictions shared by all mechanisms with these incentives and binary efficiency: binary winning probabilities determine mean outcomes at every profile and individual alignment distributions at planar three-camp profiles. When these probabilities depend only on camp size, complete insurance at balanced equilateral disagreement requires dimension proportional to population. In contrast, committees reduce each participant's welfare loss relative to certain zero alignment to any prescribed positive fraction of the equal-weight random-dictatorship loss in a population-independent dimension.

papers.title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
papers.abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_x\Phi(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--{\L}ojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.

papers.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
papers.abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.

papers.title: Stage-wise Lineage-aware Dropout for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is prone to overfitting because only a limited number of images are available to constrain scene geometry. Dropout is one regularization strategy for alleviating this problem. We introduce the concept of a lineage family to describe a set of Gaussian primitives derived from the same founder through cloning or splitting operations. The founder Gaussians refer to all Gaussian primitives generated during initialization. Descendants within the same family often jointly contribute to the refinement of adjacent local regions. However, dropping individual Gaussians can be less effective due to the compensation effect from neighboring Gaussians for the dropped ones. To address this issue, we propose Stage-wise Lineage-aware Dropout(SLD), which applies lineage-family dropout during the structural regularization stage and switches to individual dropout during the later refinement stage. We further propose Lineage-Balanced Densification(LBD), which operates during densification by constructing an expanded candidate pool and reallocating the densification budget according to the mean gradient scores and existing descendant sizes of different families. Experiments on the LLFF, MipNeRF360, and Blender datasets show that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance in sparse-view reconstruction

papers.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). MDLM post-training therefore relies on a surrogate objective based on the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), and recent work estimates a blockwise variant of this objective via Monte Carlo methods to support blockwise generation. However, existing estimation schemes randomly sample the block index, so they may evaluate the same block more than once and leave some blocks unevaluated. This introduces variance arising from block selection into the estimates. In this work, we propose a full-block estimator that evaluates every block exactly once and averages the results. We theoretically show that the proposed estimator remains unbiased while eliminating the between-group variance arising from block selection, thereby achieving lower variance than the baseline for the same sample size. In experiments on five benchmarks spanning mathematics, planning, and coding, our method achieves the highest accuracy on four benchmarks and outperforms the random block sampling baseline by an average of 12.79 points.

papers.title: VACO: Vertex-Aligned Decoding for Dense Hand Contact Estimation from a Single Image
papers.abstract: Dense hand contact estimation from a single RGB image is a foundational primitive for dexterous manipulation and 3D interaction analysis. Direct predictors typically decode the entire per-vertex contact map from one shared query, leaving individual vertices ungrounded in the image and smearing contact across adjacent, non-touching surfaces. We present VACO, a vertex-aligned decoder in which each MANO vertex samples local image features at its projected location. A hand-reconstruction backbone, jointly trained for reconstruction and contact, predicts these locations at inference without an auxiliary reconstructor. Training uses noise-perturbed ground-truth projections and end-to-end feature adaptation to improve robustness and contact-sensitive features. A single VACO checkpoint sets a new state of the art on five benchmarks spanning hand-object, hand-human, hand-scene, and bimanual interactions. It improves F1 by +20.7 pp over the strongest prior direct predictor on Hi4D and generalizes to the held-out HOT3D and HOCap, with gains of +5.5 and +2.7 pp. The resulting contact predictions also improve downstream HOI reconstruction.

papers.title: Graph Neural Network Prediction of Frequency Nadir and RoCoF Under Topology Variations
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of frequency dynamics under varying network topologies is essential for rapid frequency security assessment, whereas repeated electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations are computationally intensive. This paper develops a topology-aware graph neural network with a radial basis function Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RBF-KAN) regression head, termed RK-GNN, to predict frequency nadir and maximum absolute rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). Scenarios combine load scaling, regional load redistribution, and generator redispatch with intact, N-1, and N-2 transmission topologies. After checks for network connectivity, generator reference limits, and numerical consistency, the retained scenarios are simulated in PSCAD to construct the reference dataset. The RK-GNN is evaluated against a conventional deep neural network (DNN) and a baseline GNN. On the IEEE 39-bus system, the RK-GNN reduces the mean absolute errors (MAEs) of nadir and RoCoF by 48% and 59% relative to the DNN and by 42% and 61% relative to the baseline GNN. Incorporating the bridge indicator and disturbance hop distance yields further MAE reductions of 27% and 54%. These results show that the proposed topology-aware architecture provides accurate prediction of both frequency metrics under varying topologies and substantially reduces the need for repeated EMT simulations.

papers.title: Bridge: Database-Grounded Interactive Disambiguation for Text-to-SQL
papers.abstract: Ambiguity remains a persistent challenge in text-to-SQL, where an underspecified natural-language question may admit multiple plausible SQL interpretations. Recent work attempts to recover the user's intended interpretation through iterative clarification, but typically relies heavily on LLM parametric knowledge for ad hoc reasoning, leading to limited ambiguity-resolution effectiveness and high LLM cost. We further observe that many ambiguity errors stem from ambiguous column grounding, which remains poorly handled. Therefore, we propose Bridge, a database-grounded disambiguation framework built on an existing iterative protocol. Bridge supplies the LLM's ambiguity detection with offline-distilled knowledge about potential ambiguity relations among columns in the target database. Offline, Bridge constructs a Column Ambiguity Graph by first identifying potentially ambiguous column pairs using complementary database-grounded signals, followed by LLM-based verification. Online, columns and values mentioned in a previous incorrect SQL prediction are used as anchors to retrieve alternatives from the Column Ambiguity Graph and an offline-constructed value similarity index, respectively. The results are integrated for further pruning and consolidated for subsequent ambiguity detection. Extensive experiments on BIRD-dev without the benchmark-provided evidence show that, at comparable LLM cost, Bridge outperforms the strongest baseline by 11.60% in execution accuracy and improves the recall and precision of column usage in the final SQL by 5.25% and 12.37%, respectively.

papers.title: Weighted Euler transforms, real-rootedness, and $\gamma$-positivity
papers.abstract: For $a>0$ and a polynomial $F$ of degree $m$, let $H_{a,F}$ denote the weighted Euler numerator of $F$, defined as the numerator of the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}(a)_kF(k)x^k/k!$ with denominator $(1-x)^{a+m}$. For every $a>0$, we show the following preservation result: if the numerators $H_{a,F}$ and $H_{a,G}$ have only real nonpositive zeros, then the same holds for $H_{a,FG}$. The proof relies on an explicit multiplication formula in falling-factorial coordinates and a characterization of multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases due to Br\"and\'en and Ottergren. Furthermore, when the symmetric degrees coincide with the ordinary degrees of the input polynomials, the same operation preserves $\gamma$-positivity. For positive integers $a=r$, the weight is the Ehrhart polynomial of the standard simplex $\Delta_{r-1}$. This yields geometric preservation theorems for products with a single simplex factor, as well as applications to Gorenstein polytopes and a Reeve tetrahedron example.

papers.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can share experts across layers or computational steps, pooling training information from different contexts. This can reduce local prediction error, but multi-step systems are ultimately evaluated by their final outputs. We study when these local gains survive composition. In specified linear regression models, we derive exact sharing and merging criteria by balancing variance savings against bias from sharing across roles with different target behavior. Under a common fixed linear propagation map, we characterize expected squared final-output risk, retaining error directions and correlations. We construct cases where sharing lowers average local error yet increases final-output error. Within this setting, we also identify when orthogonal full pooling with isotropic noise preserves every local improvement at the final output. For general routed computations, we derive conditional end-to-end error bounds that account for distribution shifts, errors in surrounding components, and changes in expert selection. Separately, we show that correct predictions and route labels alone do not establish that individual experts implement the attributed operations. Controlled experiments realize a strict local-to-final risk reversal. In low-data symbolic settings, trained Transformers exhibit statistically supported teacher-forced one-step gains without statistically resolved free-running final-output gains. Separate intervention tests distinguish successful multi-layer actions from single-expert attribution and generalization to unseen transitions. Together, these results distinguish when sharing improves local estimation, when those gains survive to the final output, and what evidence is needed to attribute reusable operations to individual experts.

authors.name: Tiantong Wang

papers.title: MacroGS: Macro-Pixel Shared Gaussian Primitives for Arbitrary-Scale Light Field Super-Resolutio
papers.abstract: Arbitrary-scale light field spatial super-resolution reconstructs high-resolution views at any requested scale from low-resolution multi-view observations. Gaussian primitives enable continuous reconstruction, but generating separate primitive sets for each view redundantly encodes shared scene structure across views and causes the primitive count grow linearly with the number of views. To avoid such redundancy, we propose MacroGS, a feed-forward decoder that jointly predicts a single shared Gaussian set per macro pixel rather than generating separate sets for each view. Disparity-dependent replacement and angle-conditioned appearance allow each set to be reused across all output views, keeping the predicted primitive count independent of the number of views at each requested scale. The decoder iteratively predicts per-primitive disparities, retrieves the corresponding multi-view features, and updates the primitive states. Gaussian splatting and residual refinement then reconstruct the output light field. Despite being learned without geometric supervision, the predicted disparities strongly correlate with underlying scene geometry. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that MacroGS integrates effectively with diverse light field encoders, improving reconstruction quality at fixed scales while achieving leading performance across most evaluated arbitrary-scale settings. The decoder also achieves speedups of approximately $2$-$10\times$ over state-of-the-art implicit light field decoders and $10$-$18\times$ over the view-wise Gaussian baseline.

papers.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.

papers.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
papers.abstract: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. Preregistered experiments trace the contagion to imitation of the history's style. History also moves a model away from its own fingerprint: active probes are not camouflaged, but when calibrated on fresh conversations they flag \emph{honest} models on long contexts at rates up to 1.00, and a standard MMD equality test rejects all nine models we test. Both failures come from comparing a history-dependent reply with a history-free reference. We propose \textsc{Lineup}, which samples references from the claimed model \emph{on the same history} and tests the audited reply by its rank among them. \textsc{Lineup} controls false positives by exchangeability and needs no fitted threshold or log-probabilities. With contemporaneous references on two closed models, its false-positive rate is 0.056 (preregistered bound 0.10), and it detects 0.81 of substitute sessions across six pairs after four audited turns.

papers.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
papers.abstract: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time. In medium Earth orbit (MEO)--low Earth orbit (LEO) networks, periodic reports leave CPU states stale or missing, making offloading sensitive to uncertain capacity and shared-destination congestion. We propose PUMA-Former, an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative offloading under incomplete information that balances completed work, service delay, and execution cost. A MEO coordinator maintains distinct-report memory and closes the loop between available evidence, capacity estimates, allocation commands, and execution feedback. Latent-delay attention weights plausible measurement-age hypotheses, and historical innovations refine CPU estimates around the latest received report. Queue-error-aware fusion incorporates auxiliary pressure while accounting for backlog uncertainty. The inferred resource moments condition a structured Transformer allocator for joint destination, partition, bandwidth, CPU, and power decisions. Bounded risk-aware calibration then adjusts workload splits to reflect uncertainty and shared destination load. In traffic-driven development evaluation, PUMA-Former increases admitted compute-work completion by 8.62%, reduces mean modeled service delay by 34.78%, and reduces mean episode-P95 delay by 71.08% relative to ATLA-adapt. It also improves completion and normalized energy over fixed-half round-robin offloading. Service gains over the learning baselines involve higher normalized energy.

papers.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
papers.abstract: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. Our key insight is that temporal pattern learning can benefit from abundant external time series, while spatial dependency learning remains grounded in real spatio-temporal observations. Guided by this insight, T2ST retrieves matched sequences to reinforce sparsely observed temporal patterns and selects reliable complementary sequences to broaden temporal coverage. Temporal relation distillation aligns relationships among historical patches, while multi-scale prediction distillation transfers forecasting behavior at fine and coarse temporal resolutions, enabling knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. Using only 10\% of the original spatio-temporal data, T2ST enables STFMs to achieve overall forecasting performance competitive with or superior to their full-data counterparts across six long-term and twelve short-term forecasting datasets. These results establish a new paradigm for data-efficient training of spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/T2ST-65F3/.

papers.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive. Here, we build a similarity network from the input embeddings of six open LLMs and map generation onto it. The token-embedding network is scale-free while heavy-tailed, as are random embeddings with matched covariance, but far more fragmented. Distillation barely changes this topology because input embeddings are largely inherited. The knowledge space is thus deterministic from pre-training. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbours and, in most models, no more often than in shuffled order, so generation is not a walk on the predefined network, although the tokens it visits are concentrated within it. Through the logit lens in a layer- wise manner, tokens settle late in depth in most models, and repetitive models remain confined to small domain-specific sub-graphs. These observables could serve as inference-time monitors of degeneration. We thus provide a fresh perspective on understanding LLM generation in the microscopic way from node or link prediction by graph learning.

papers.title: Exact-Quota Facility Location: A Transfer Framework and Three Approximation Guarantees
papers.abstract:
Facility location with outliers asks which facilities to open and which clients to serve, subject to a prescribed service quota. We give a framework for transferring facility-location cost certificates to this exact-quota setting. The framework yields deterministic polynomial-time approximation guarantees of $571/376<1.52$ for metric facility location with outliers, strictly less than $1.853$ for priority facility location with outliers, and $2.16995<2.17$ for squared-metric facility location with outliers. Each algorithm serves the prescribed number of clients and pays the original facility-opening costs.
  The framework separates initialization from improvement. A growth process is stopped when it first reaches the quota; deleting excess clients from its last batch leaves a payment deficit supported on a bounded number of facilities. Greedy additions then reoptimize the served client set. A threshold-coverage representation makes the resulting service cost supermodular and allows the usual density analysis to compare different client sets. Finally, enumerating and prepaying a constant number of expensive facilities absorbs the exceptional costs. A transfer theorem states exactly which initialization certificate is sufficient and how many prepaid facilities it requires.
  The three applications supply this certificate in different ways. The metric case uses a quota prefix of reassigning JMS; the priority case uses persistent contributions and a cleanup ordered by service level; and the squared-metric case uses a local factor-revealing certificate valid for arbitrary client subsets of the same run. We provide complete finite proofs of the numerical interfaces, including an exact rational certificate for the squared-metric bound.

papers.title: PROOF: Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion
papers.abstract: Vision-based perceptive locomotion has enabled legged robots to achieve agile and terrain-aware locomotion across complex environments. However, the reliability of such systems heavily depends on visual observations, which are inherently susceptible to occlusion, reflective surfaces, and illumination variations, often resulting in catastrophic locomotion failures under degraded perception conditions. In this paper, we present PROOF (Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion), a perceptive locomotion framework that enables robust locomotion under severe visual disturbances. Our method adopts a two-stage teacher-student learning paradigm that explicitly models perception reliability: the teacher learns both perception-driven and proprioceptive fallback behaviors, while the student predicts exteroceptive features with uncertainty and suppresses them under out-of-distribution inputs. We evaluate our method on a Unitree Go2 quadruped equipped with a RealSense D435 depth camera in real-world settings. Under normal visual conditions, our method enables the robot to successfully perform high-dynamic parkour maneuvers, including traversing large gaps, elevated platforms, and narrow beam terrains. Under severe visual degradation, such as heavy occlusion and strong illumination changes, the robot continues to maintain stable and robust locomotion performance.

papers.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
papers.abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. Unlike goal-only evaluation, our benchmark measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware, and accessibility-aligned metrics. We benchmark modern vision-language models and find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles, suggesting accessibility-aware navigation requires dedicated datasets, tasks, and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. All data and code open-source at https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN.

papers.title: The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
papers.abstract: We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.

papers.title: LitArc-Bench: Disentangling Text-Specific Reader-Response Dynamics from Position and Lexical Affect
papers.abstract: When model predictions track an unfolding human affect trajectory, alignment may reflect narrative position, affective words, or text-specific reader-response dynamics. We introduce LitArc-Bench to separate these explanations: 39 Chinese-language literary excerpts segmented into seven checkpoints, with 430 questionnaires from 81 adults in two classroom groups (9,020 VAD ratings). We compare three future-blind model runs with leave-one-text-out position priors, lexical affect, and human-human references. Position alone reaches r = .470 for arousal, making raw alignment insufficient. Yet all six V/A transition advantages over a joint position-lexicon control have text-bootstrap intervals above zero. Cross-fitted models match the correct human text better than 38 mismatched texts in all nine model-dimension cells (p < .0001); a text-invariant negative control returns chance (p = 1). On human transitions at least 0.5 points against the position trend, models recover 69-76% of valence directions and 53-68% for arousal and dominance. Under crossed participant-text resampling, all nine identity intervals remain above zero; joint-control advantages are robust for valence and directional but less certain for arousal. High shape agreement still coexists with scale bias. LitArc-Bench identifies which components of literary reader response are recoverable beyond shallow explanations and why shape, calibration, and human variability require separate evaluation.

papers.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising way to mitigate task interference through expert specialization and combination. However, while existing MoE-based methods avoid overwriting shared parameters by allocating separate experts for each task, this progressive expansion incurs severe cross-task redundancy and linear parameter growth. Specifically, experts across tasks often learn overlapping functions alongside task-specific capabilities. For instance, ScienceQA and TextVQA both locate relevant image regions. To curb parameter redundancy without inducing forgetting, we propose Consolidating and Preserving MoE (CoPre-MoE). For each incoming task, CoPre-MoE first learns task-specific MoE to capture specialized capabilities. To eliminate redundancy and reduce parameter growth across tasks, we design a shared-and-private expert architecture. Specifically, we first evaluate functional overlap to selectively consolidate overlapping experts across tasks into a fixed-capacity generic expert pool. We then factorize the remaining task-specific experts into shared projection bases and compact task-specific cores within a private expert pool. To mitigate forgetting, we construct the router by pairing each expert with learnable retrieval keys, where historical keys remain frozen during continual updates while newly added keys are regularized with an orthogonality penalty. At inference, input-dependent routing dynamically combines both pools without test-time task labels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPre-MoE achieves superior performance while substantially reducing parameter overhead.

papers.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
papers.abstract: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.

papers.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
papers.abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

papers.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
papers.abstract: We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.

papers.title: Exceptional sequences of line bundles on $\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_\ell=\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)\subset\mathbb{P}^\ell\times(\mathbb{P}^\ell)^\vee$ be the incidence variety of points and hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^\ell$. We prove that for every $\ell\ge 3$, every exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ of maximal length $\ell(\ell+1)=\operatorname{rk} K_0(X_\ell)$ is full. Together with the case $\ell=2$, due to Altmann, Hochenegger and Witt, this shows that for all $\ell\ge2$ an exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ is full if and only if it has maximal length. The proof translates exceptionality into a combinatorial condition on lattice points of $\operatorname{Pic}(X_\ell)\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$ and reduces fullness to sequences containing a non-orthogonal descent. A capacity count for admissibly ordered subsets rules out all but one family of descents; for that family we classify the possible configurations and verify generation using Euler sequences and Koszul complexes.

papers.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
papers.abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative based on center-distance matching. Using this benchmark, we evaluate open-source and proprietary vision-language models under a direct single-pass setting, as well as settings with auxiliary components (OCR and character grounding) coordinated via pipelining or agentic harnessing. Results show that even top-tier proprietary models perform surprisingly poorly in the single-pass setting, while pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements. Notably, an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieves the best performance, establishing it as the strongest baseline for future G-CGEC research. Through ablations and fine-grained analysis, we find the task remains far from solved, with linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding as the primary bottlenecks. This underscores the need for models that better integrate visual perception with linguistic reasoning and visual grounding.

authors.name: Junwei Bao
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Vision-Language Models Reproduce a Human Mental-Extrapolation Bias in the Watanabe Illusion
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for visual judgments, yet whether they share human perceptual biases, and where in the model such biases arise, is unclear. We addressed this with the Watanabe Illusion, a stimulus not previously studied quantitatively: an oblique segment inside a circle whose extension geometrically hits the topmost of 11 dots, yet human observers (n = 131) reported a dot near the middle of the column. Five VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-32B and 7B, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5 Instant, Gemini 3.5 Flash), given the identical stimulus and wording, all deviated in the same direction. In the open-weight Qwen2.5-VL-32B, linear probes on the vision encoder recovered the line angle and the target dot six to eight times more accurately than its behavioral responses. A layer-wise logit lens showed that the correct answer dominates in the middle layers of the language model and is overwritten in late layers only under a visual-judgment frame. Naming the illusion, requesting suppression of prior knowledge, forcing a visual chain of thought, and 390 semantic preambles left the response center unchanged; only disclosing the correct answer moved it. VLMs may therefore carry human perceptual biases at the language-generation stage, where they resist declarative correction.

papers.title: Evaluate Laughlin spectral gap lower bound in vortexable bands
papers.abstract: Vortexable Chern bands admit exact Laughlin-type zero modes of local parent interactions, but their existence alone does not guarantee a finite excitation gap. Here, we derive a computable, particle-number-independent lower bound on the spectral gap of Laughlin parent Hamiltonians in a class of vortexable bands obtained by multiplying lowest-Landau-level wavefunctions by a spatially varying envelope. The bound depends only on two quantities: the spread of projected orbital normalizations and a lower bound on the weighted local pair repulsion, both determined by one- and two-particle operators. The proof employs an auxiliary fermion-loss construction to control orbital orthogonalization, with an error bounded relative to the interaction energy uniformly in particle number. We demonstrate that Landau-level averaging permits strictly positive gap bounds even under substantial spatial modulation, including envelopes with nodal lines. Beyond the scalar-envelope construction, we extend the analysis to multicomponent orbital textures and deformations of the vortex coordinate. These results establish rigorous gap criteria for Laughlin parent Hamiltonians, providing a foundation for understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in vortexable bands.

papers.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. We propose VEPO(Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization), a training-time method that transfers reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external models. VEPO first localizes key visual evidence using English queries via mid-layer cross-modal attention, then constructs preference pairs that share the same correct answer but differ in evidence sufficiency (full image vs.\ key-region masked image). Direct preference optimization on these pairs encourages low-resource inputs to prefer answers supported by complete visual evidence. Experiments on multilingual POPE and MME with Chinese, French, and Hindi show consistent hallucination reduction and perception gains, with the largest improvements on the lowest-resource language. Analyses further confirm that VEPO sharpens question-relevant attention and that evidence-guided masking outperforms random masking.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
papers.abstract: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ \Delta^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_t\Delta u=e^{24\pi^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.

papers.title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
papers.abstract: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.

authors.name: Yin Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
papers.abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

authors.name: Shuzhou Wang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
papers.abstract: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $\epsilon$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.

papers.title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation
papers.abstract: A small labelled dataset is memorized long before the training budget runs out, and the one-hot labels that remain to be fitted then mostly sharpen confidence. Model annealing spends the rest of the budget on review and consolidation, relearning from the network's own knowledge. Training is divided into episodes whose learning rate is raised again and cooled, every cooled state joins a memory of past selves, and each new episode learns from the labels, from the tempered predictions of this memory, and from adversarial dreams sought where student and memory disagree most. The memory averages predictions rather than weights, and the deployed network is the last student, so inference costs nothing extra. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and Imagewoof, four architecture families and 5\% to 100\% of the labels, model annealing raises the top-1 accuracy of the AdamW-trained ConvNeXt, ViT and MLP-Mixer over cross-entropy training in 28 of 33 configurations, by 1.3 points on average, and is on par in accuracy with snapshot distillation, the closest competitor. On these families it is better than both in likelihood, calibration and robustness to corruptions and small adversarial perturbations. For an SGD-trained ResNet-18 it lowers accuracy but still improves robustness to small adversarial perturbations. Separating the reheated schedule from relearning shows that relearning helps every family and that the losses come from reheats, which undo most of this network's fit to its training set. How early the accuracy of a cross-entropy run saturates largely separates the AdamW families from ResNet-18 but does not predict the gain within them. With little data, relearning from the latest snapshot without dreams, as snapshot distillation does, compounds overconfidence in the AdamW families from episode to episode. The memory and the dreams each curb most of this drift, and together they remove it.

papers.title: SZZBench: Controlled Git Histories with Explicit Oracles for Diagnosing SZZ Implementations
papers.abstract: The SZZ algorithm traces a bug-fixing commit back to the commits that introduced the bug. Its labels underlie defect-prediction data sets and many mining software repositories studies. SZZ implementations are mostly evaluated against oracles mined from real projects. Such oracles are realistic, but each case mixes the history factors that make an implementation succeed or fail, and an aggregate score cannot show why. We present SZZBench, a tool that shows why: it generates ordinary Git repositories from declarative scenarios with explicit oracles, scores the predictions of any SZZ implementation under declared evaluation policies, and reads each result against 26 naive baselines, such as always answering the second commit. SZZBench also checks the declarations of new scenarios, such as the tier, against the results of the naive baselines. Currently, SZZBench ships 279 scenarios in 17 categories and adapters for four SZZ tools. Running these tools in nine configurations without changing their code, we find that PyDriller passes 161 scenarios and a rule that always answers the second commit passes 160, yet only 97 scenarios are passed by both: the two succeed on different scenarios, which the number of passed scenarios hides and the per-scenario results reveal. SZZBench is available at https://github.com/higolab/SZZBench.

authors.name: Caihua Luo
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: On Structure-Aware SAT Solving
papers.abstract: Although modern SAT solvers have made remarkable progress, they still exploit formula structure only to a limited extent. We present two techniques that make SAT solving more structure-aware and provide experimental results showing their promise. The first technique ``$\mathit{melts}$'' the formula by reducing interaction between its parts. This is achieved by adding new variables, using existential quantifiers, and applying a procedure called partial quantifier elimination. The second technique exploits the notion of a $\mathit{local}$ $\mathit{proof}$. The latter establishes that a formula is unsatisfiable by proving that certain literals of its clauses are redundant. We show that using local proofs makes SAT solving more formula-specific.

papers.title: A solution to Petty's polar projection problem
papers.abstract: In 1971, Petty asked whether a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant 3$, must be an ellipsoid if its projection body is a dilate of its polar. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to this question.

authors.name: Yiqian Zhang
authors.institution: Tianjin Research Institute of Water Transport Engineering

papers.title: Emulating physics-based XCO2 retrievals across OCO-2 viewing modes with compact neural networks
papers.abstract: Operational full-physics retrieval of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide from satellite spectra is computationally demanding. We use singular value decomposition to compress spectra from the Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 separately by band. Compact multilayer perceptrons use the resulting spectral scores, prior information, and viewing geometry to predict the difference between the full-physics retrieval and its operational prior. Adding the predicted difference to the prior yields an estimate of the retrieved mole fraction. The models were trained on 2015-2019 observations and validated on 2020 observations. In 2021-2025 tests, the mean annual root-mean-square errors relative to the Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Observations from Space retrieval product were 0.89, 1.35, and 1.43 parts per million for ocean glint, land glint, and nadir observations, respectively. On East Asian nadir observations screened using the published criteria for the spectral Transformer, our model yielded a lower mean annual error than reported for that model in 2020-2022. These results show that compact neural networks using compressed spectra can efficiently emulate the full-physics retrieval across multiple viewing modes and years.

papers.title: Estimating a Rational Inattention Discrete Choice Model: A Semiparametric Approach
papers.abstract: People's choices depend on both the payoffs of the available options and what they learn about those payoffs before deciding. This paper shows how choice data identify both unobserved payoff heterogeneity and the cost of information acquisition in a rational inattention discrete-choice model. I establish conditions for semiparametric point identification using exogenous payoff and information-cost shifters, without imposing parametric forms on the taste-shock distribution or on how the unit cost of information varies with observed characteristics. In the model with binary choice, I construct an unobserved choice threshold whose cumulative distribution function is the choice probability as a function of the payoff shifter. Moments of this threshold identify the payoff coefficients and the unit cost of information at each value of the information-cost shifter. A deconvolution argument then identifies the taste-shock distribution. I then extend identification to the model with multinomial choice. To estimate the model, I propose a sieve minimum-distance estimator based on observed market shares and establish its consistency. For inference, I construct confidence regions by test inversion because binding parameter constraints can make the estimator's limiting distribution nonnormal. In an application to Amazon Mechanical Turk, model counterfactuals show that lower unit costs of information raise the average task-taking probability and reduce wage elasticity.

authors.name: Hanqi Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior that users already rely on. Periodic manual retraining is too delayed and labor-intensive for this setting. To address these challenges, we present G-CAST, a governed continual self-training system that converts daily production evidence under evolving demand and capability contracts into reward-routed, entropy-prioritized training data and governed reward evolution. Governed checkpoint transition under cumulative evaluation controls each model update, enabling the agent to learn newly introduced behaviors without sacrificing previously accepted capabilities. Experiments on a real production e-commerce agent show that G-CAST achieves stronger adaptation to newly introduced demand while better preserving previously accepted behavior compared with a strong autonomous post-training baseline. Ablations further show that both reward-routed, entropy-prioritized data orchestration and governed reward evolution are important to these gains. G-CAST is now deployed in Yuancai(http://cai.1688.com/), a B2B procurement agent on Alibaba's 1688 platform.

authors.name: Wenzheng Kong
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods for Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for nonconvex objectives and $O(1/k)$ for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.

Over the past two decades, multiobjective first-order methods have been widely studied, which include steepest descent methods (Fliege and Svaiter, 2000), projected gradient methods (Graña Drummond and Iusem, 2004), proximal gradient methods (Tanabe et al., 2019), and nonlinear conjugate gradient methods (Lucambio Pérez and Prudente, 2018). Line search is commonly used the backtracking strategy to select a stepsize satisfying a prescribed decrease condition. This backtracking process may require multiple evaluations of all objective functions, thereby increasing the computational cost. When applied to multiobjective optimization, line search requires a stepsize to satisfy the decrease conditions for all objective functions, which may lead to a very small stepsize (Mita et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2025). Mita et al. (2019) proposed nonmonotone line search strategies to alleviate the small-stepsize issue, although repeated backtracking still be required. To avoid the backtracking process, researchers have recently begun exploring adaptive stepsize strategies.
