papers.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study
papers.abstract: Daily GPU rental-price benchmarks can fail when marketplace quotes are missing. This article stress-tests a fixed equal-weight median rule under four imposed masking mechanisms and four benchmark-level recovery methods. Across 5,800 Monte Carlo realisations in 27 scenarios on 190 held-out days, whole-source outages reduce publication coverage to 0.77 while preserving zero conditional error on published dates; composition-changing loss retains 0.86 coverage but produces 7.74 log points of error. A separate past-only stratum-level ablation reduces error by 4.15 to 6.70 log points in five composition-changing cases, using a richer information set. An observable-signal withholding rule improves the primary error-coverage criterion in 0 of 10 cases. Results concern observed asking-price measurements, not transaction prices or identified real-world missingness mechanisms.

papers.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
papers.abstract: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.

papers.title: Relabeling symmetry and conservation laws in hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic upper-ocean models
papers.abstract: We explicitly identify conserved integrals of hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic reduced-gravity upper-ocean models, both vertically unrestricted and columnar, with Noether quantities associated with particle relabeling. The columnar velocity reduction preserves the Lie-algebra structure, providing a common Euler--Poincar\'e framework for both families. Within this framework, we introduce nonhydrostatic columnar models with polynomial vertical buoyancy structure, extending the hydrostatic stratified hierarchy. Retaining the temporal endpoint pairing, we construct transported relabeling generators and evaluate their vorticity-dependent conserved integrals, assuming that spatial boundary terms vanish. For stratified columnar models, preservation of the effective buoyancy entering the Lagrangian suffices for symmetry even when individual buoyancy coefficients change, yielding conserved quantities that generally are not Casimirs of the full Lie--Poisson bracket. Where the Legendre transform is regular, we state the corresponding brackets and identify their Casimir families. The hydrostatic parent is treated directly through the Euler--Poincar\'e principle because its Legendre transform is degenerate. Integrals following directly from advection are distinguished from those obtained through the Noether pairing.

papers.title: Aligning AI Teams
papers.abstract: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less likely to proactively check for system-level safety failures and more likely to ignore, rationalize, or deflect responsibility for issues when they arise; (4) having a designated safety lead agent ensure system-level safety, and having a coordinator agent publish a safety specifications document are effective at restoring single-agent alignment. We also release magelab, a multi-agent LLM orchestration and experimentation framework. Our findings can help practitioners design agent teams that successfully preserve the behaviors expected of aligned individual agents.

papers.title: Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities
papers.abstract: The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization. Following the approach of Mumford and Morrison, we establish quantitative estimates for linear systems and their contributions to Chow weights, without restrictions on the Picard number.

papers.title: Log-concavity of rank and crank statistics for integer partitions
papers.abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang [Adv. Math. 2021] conjectured that $M(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$, and that $N(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge73$ and $|m|\le n-73$. In this paper, we prove these two conjectures.

papers.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
papers.abstract:
We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $\Gamma/
u$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{m adv}(\Gamma/
u)^{s}$, the vorticity $\omega_	heta$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{
u t})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and \v{S}ver'ak \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.

papers.title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
papers.abstract: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale H\"older family.

authors.name: Xi Cen
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Speed-Variation Distillation for Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: While diffusion models excel at image generation, their denoising trajectories pass through corrupted intermediate states far from the image manifold. We ask whether generation can instead proceed through recognizable images throughout the entire trajectory. We introduce a generative framework built around a variation-reducing degradation process that contracts diverse images toward a shared prototype while preserving recognizable intermediate states. Because such manifold traversal lacks a simple analytical form, we construct the trajectories using generative-prior-based image morphing. We then distill the reverse process into a diversification operator that transforms the prototype into increasingly varied samples. To resolve the one-to-many ambiguity of the reverse process, we associate each trajectory with its initial noise latent and apply perturbations to improve robustness against accumulated errors. At inference, every step yields a recognizable image, allowing early termination and enabling a controllable speed--variation trade-off.

authors.name: Supasorn Suwajanakorn
authors.institution: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: ERGo: Energy-Efficient Hybrid Graph Neural Network Training on Processing-In-Memory Architectures
papers.abstract: Processing-in-memory (PIM) has been proposed as an alternative computing paradigm for training Deep Neural Networks, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Despite these advancements, training GNN workloads on PIM devices necessitates off-chip memory access. This off-chip access is expensive in terms of performance and energy, thereby impacting the overall energy efficiency of the training process on PIM platforms. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid training framework called ERGo that automatically switches from a full-parameter phase to a parameter-efficient phase during the training process with negligible loss in predictive accuracy. The parameter-efficient phase employs low-rank representations of GNN weights, effectively reducing the number of trainable parameters. This helps in reducing the off-chip access during the end-to-end training process on PIM architectures, leading to notable improvements in both performance and energy efficiency. ERGo outperforms the conventional full-parameter GNN training on a PIM-based platform by up to 3.15x in speedup and enhances energy efficiency by 10.5x. Furthermore, ERGo offers additional advantages when utilized on heterogeneous architectures incorporating non-volatile memory (NVM) and static random-access memory (SRAM). Training on the heterogeneous NVM-SRAM architecture typically utilizes NVM for the forward-pass and SRAM for the backward-pass. However, NVM cells suffer from low device endurance and repeated write operations due to weight updates can lead to poor lifetime. ERGo improves the lifetime of NVM devices by freezing the weights and preventing weight updates in the parameter-efficient phase. Experimental results demonstrate that ERGo improves the lifetime of heterogeneous NVM-SRAM architecture by up to 33x in comparison to full-parameter implementation.

papers.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

authors.name: Yerko Contreras-Rojas
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Sul e Sudeste do Pará

papers.title: Waveform-based pulse timing enhanced by self-supervised neural regression models for digital nuclear instrumentation
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of high-sampling-rate digital nuclear devices, their applications in nuclear facilities and related fields become more acceptable, and will possibly become widespread due to the versatility and flexibility of waveform sampling systems. When digitizers reach hundreds of megahertz or gigahertz, their lower limit in time measurement probes into the sub-nanosecond region, expediting their use in a bunch of time-critical scenarios. While conventional algorithms coupled with digital sampling techniques realize fair pulse timing in certain conditions, the potentials are still open to compact and efficient machine learning models. In this paper, we intend to boost the performance of pulse timing with a new paradigm of self-supervised learning on matched waveform pairs. The proposed method combines the mainstream self-supervised loss and the auxiliary weakly-supervised loss on the reference set, jointly improving the timing performance. We apply the method in a gamma/neutron-mixed radiation field, common in nuclear facilities. The simulation and experimental results show that, the proposed method not only outperforms conventional timing algorithms, but also surpasses neural network models based on supervised learning alone. Considering the trained model is lightweight and computationally efficient, it is promising to deploy it on edge devices, like economical microcontrollers with neural processing units.

papers.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
papers.abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

authors.name: Kaixin Deng
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Materials Processing and Die & Mould Technology

papers.title: Neural Simulation-Based Inference for Computational Cognitive Models: A Tutorial
papers.abstract: Computational cognitive modeling is an increasingly essential methodology to elucidate the mechanisms underlying human and animal cognition. By fitting models to empirical data, researchers can perform parameter estimation, model comparison, and model-based neural analyses to assess competing theories, quantify individual differences, and investigate neural representations. Typically, fitting these models relies on likelihood-dependent methods (e.g., Maximum likelihood estimation or hierarchical Bayesian methods). However, for many reasonable cognitive models, computing the likelihood is computationally intractable, in which case these methods become inadequate. This substantially limits the range of theories that researchers can investigate. Simulation-based inference with neural networks (neural SBI) has emerged as a powerful toolkit to overcome this hurdle. By training deep neural networks on datasets generated through model simulations, neural SBI learns the relation between observable data and cognitive models. This approach enables all the applications of standard modeling while bypassing the likelihood computation, without constraints on empirical data size. Despite its successful adoption across diverse scientific fields, neural SBI remains underutilized in cognitive modeling, partly due to a lack of accessible, domain-tailored guidance. This tutorial addresses this gap by providing a clear workflow for applying neural SBI to cognitive models. We also provide practical use cases and recommendations for reducing the computational and simulation burden, facilitating efficient implementation in real-world research settings. By lowering the technical barriers to neural SBI, this tutorial aims to empower cognitive scientists to investigate richer theory spaces and ultimately propel scientific discovery.

papers.title: The elephant random walk with proportionally growing recent memory
papers.abstract: In this work, we study an elephant random walk with recent restricted memory, where at step $n$ the elephant remembers only the last $m_n=\max\{\lfloor cn\rfloor,1\}$ steps for $c\in(0,1)$. We show that the random walk undergoes a phase transition at the critical point $p_c=(3+\sqrt{1-c})/4$, which depends on the memory proportion $c$. For $0<p<p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n}$ is asymptotically normal; for $p=p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ is asymptotically normal; and for $p_c<p<1$, $S_n/n^{\rho}$ converges almost surely and in $L^2$ to a random variable for some constant $\rho\in (1/2, 1)$. This phase transition differs from that of the classical elephant random walk and its remote-memory counterpart, both of which have the same fixed critical point $3/4$.

authors.name: Zhishui Hu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision
papers.abstract: The bi-Kappa distribution models anisotropic space-plasma populations with suprathermal power-law tails. Kinetic simulations represent such a population by computational particles, and a loader draws their velocities from the requested bi-Kappa distribution, which we call the target distribution. When $\kappa$ is close to 1/2, floating-point underflow can remove the largest draws, and a velocity bound changes the loaded distribution. Published Kappa loaders are usually verified by comparing histograms of the speed or of one velocity component with the analytic distribution. Such comparisons do not examine the direction of the velocity or whether the direction is independent of the speed. We build an anisotropic loader on an established Gamma-ratio construction and examine each of these problems. Near $\kappa=1/2$, evaluating the Gamma ratio on a logarithmic scale avoids the loss of draws to underflow in single and double precision down to $\kappa=0.5001$. When draws outside a bound on each velocity component are discarded and redrawn, a small rejected fraction can accompany a large change in the tail. At $\kappa=2$ and $\theta_\parallel=2\theta_\perp$, a bound at 20 times each component's thermal speed rejects a fraction $3.6\times10^{-4}$ of the draws and lowers the 99.9th-percentile speed by 11%. We test the loaded velocities through their direction and their normalized radius, the length of the velocity after each component is divided by $\sqrt{\kappa}$ times its thermal speed. The tests used nine values of $\kappa$ from 0.51 to 10, including $1/2<\kappa\le3/2$, where the second moments do not exist, with $\theta_\parallel=2\theta_\perp$ in double precision. At every $\kappa$, $\chi^2$ tests find the normalized radius out to its 99.999th percentile, the direction, and their joint distribution consistent with the target distribution.

papers.title: Properties of stellar disks and spheroids in simulated galaxies
papers.abstract: The optical morphology of a galaxy is determined by the relative importance of their disk and spheroidal components. Although the scaling laws of disk-dominated or spheroid-dominated galaxies have been studied in some detail, less attention has been paid to the properties of each component in galaxies where both coexist. We use a dynamical decomposition of 3452 galaxies from the TNG100 simulations with stellar masses in the range $10 \leq \log_\mathrm{10}(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 12$ to study how, at given mass, the properties of a spheroid are altered by the presence of a disk, and vice versa. We define spheroids as the non-rotating component made up of all stars in retrograde motion, plus an equal number of co-rotating stars mirrored in angular momentum and energy. Disks simply consist of the remainder of (co-rotating) stars. We find that disk properties (rotation speed, size, formation time) depend sensitively on the mass of the spheroidal component and therefore of the total mass of the galaxy in which both reside. At given mass, disks rotate faster, are more extended, and form their stars earlier as the mass of the spheroidal component increases. On the other hand, at fixed mass, the properties of spheroids are less sensitive to the presence of a disk. Roughly speaking, the classical bulges of simulated disk galaxies closely resemble ellipticals of similar stellar mass. The apparent structural invariance of spheroids to the presence of a disk is somewhat surprising, but it likely results because disks form out of high angular momentum material which surrounds the spheroid and thus have less dynamical influence on a spheroid's structure.

authors.name: Valeria A. Cristiani
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

authors.name: Mario G. Abadi
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Joint World Action Models through Differentiable Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Joint world action models (WAMs) generate future actions and states together, modeling world-action trajectories rather than actions alone. However, trajectory imitation does not ensure that these trajectories are task-effective or consistent with dynamics. We present \textbf{world action trajectory optimization (WATO)}, which optimizes generated actions and future states jointly for control. WATO uses both as references in a dynamics-constrained trajectory optimization problem and differentiates the task loss through the optimized trajectory to train the generator. This makes generated trajectories task-aware and dynamics-consistent while using trajectory optimization only during training. At deployment, WATO directly generates candidate trajectories and ranks them with a world model, without iterative trajectory optimization. Across $7$ visual control environments, WATO improves average success from $79.9\%$ for the imitation joint WAM to $91.7\%$, outperforming strong model-based, goal-conditioned RL, and generative control baselines. Compared with cross-entropy method (CEM), WATO is on average $11.5\times$ faster and uses $600.5\times$ fewer world model evaluations at deployment.

authors.name: Mintae Kim
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Bioscience and Biotechnology

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect
papers.abstract: We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic M\"obius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{\alpha,p}(0,T;L^2(\Omega))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.

papers.title: Domain-repetition patterns in protein domain trigrams are uniform across chromosomes and conserved among multicellular eukaryotes
papers.abstract:
Proteins are built from domains, and the order of domains along a protein can be read like a sentence. We take every run of three consecutive Pfam domains (a domain trigram) and classify it by its pattern of repetition: all three the same (AAA), the first two (AAB), the last two (ABB), the outer two (ABA) or all different (ABC). We ask whether the proportions of these five patterns are conserved across the chromosomes of a genome and across genomes.
  We built a reproducible workflow and applied it to the UniProt reference proteomes of 16 organisms, from Escherichia coli to human, with Pfam 39.0. In Drosophila melanogaster, 3,107 distinct trigrams split into 63% ABC, 13% each of AAB and ABB, and 5% each of AAA and ABA. Every chromosome arm closely matches this pie: each lies within the range expected for a random set of genes of the same size. The human pie has less ABC (55%) and more AAB and ABB (18% each), and 23 of its 25 chromosomes and other components fall within the random-gene range. Pies of trigram occurrences vary more, mostly because of a few giant repeat proteins.
  Across 199 chromosomes and other proteome components of 14 organisms, tested with a gene-level permutation, 4 (2%) differ from their own proteome in distinct trigrams and 10 (5%) in occurrences, chiefly human and macaque chromosome 19, whose KRAB zinc-finger clusters make it rich in AAA repeats. Across organisms, the distinct-trigram pie is closely conserved among multicellular eukaryotes (ABC 55-67%, with AAB and ABB always within 2 percentage points of each other) and shifts towards ABC in yeasts (75-77%) and bacteria (82-86%).
  The proportion of domain-repetition patterns is therefore conserved across the chromosomes of a genome and shared by plants and animals, while repeat-rich giant proteins and tandem gene clusters account for most of the local deviations.

papers.title: DECODE: Decomposable Environments for COntrolled Sequential-Decision Evaluation
papers.abstract: When a sequential decision system falls short of an optimum, its score does not reveal which modifications would improve its decisions. DECODE is a benchmark for testing such modifications through controlled experiments on planning and available information. Its consumer-credit collections generator provides five partially observed environments that share known dynamics matrices and vary a memory parameter and process noise. The experiments change selected inputs or planning rules while keeping the rest of the solver fixed. Each comparison specifies the solver's state inputs, response inputs and planning horizon. On the deterministic base environment, which was selected for a large gap between six-month and one-month planning with the hidden state, extending planning from one to six months increases the scores of two gradient-boosted solvers by 15 to 17 percentage points of the exact optimum, computed with the hidden state and borrower traits. Even at this horizon, the best graded solver, whose repayment response is fitted on logs, remains 15.6 points below that optimum. In a specified intervention sequence, three changes to its state inputs and their evaluation during search lower its score by 6.3 points, and replacing its fitted repayment model with the true response, evaluated with hidden borrower traits, then raises it by 15.6, a net recovery of nine of those points. Because the intermediate effects are conditional on the repayment model and the order of the changes, they do not uniquely assign the gap to separate causes. Within these limits, DECODE makes hypotheses about solver performance testable through specified interventions under known dynamics and explicit information conditions.

papers.title: Holographically motivated Hubble-running dark energy: Phantom-divide crossing in VCDM and observational constraints
papers.abstract: Motivated by power-law dependences on the expansion scale in holographic dark-energy constructions, we study the Hubble-running equation of state $w_{\rm DE}=w_0(H/H_0)^q$ (HoloEoS), where $H$ is the Hubble expansion rate, $H_0$ and $w_0$ are the present values of $H$ and $w_{\rm DE}$, and $q$ is a constant dimensionless exponent controlling the running. We embed this history in VCDM, a type-II minimally modified gravity theory that propagates only the two tensor modes of general relativity. For regular expanding histories with standard matter, we reconstruct the potential $V(\phi)$ of its nondynamical auxiliary scalar field, providing a Lagrangian description of both the homogeneous background and cosmological perturbations. This framework allows HoloEoS to realize a smooth late-time crossing of the phantom divide $w_{\rm DE}=-1$. We confront this VCDM realization with SPT, Planck, and ACT CMB data, updated DESI DR2 distances, and optionally DESY5 supernovae with Dovekie recalibration, comparing it with $\Lambda$CDM and the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parameterization embedded in the same gravitational framework (CPL-VCDM). For the full data combination, the posterior medians and central $68\%$ credible intervals are $w_0=-0.881^{+0.040}_{-0.038}$ and $q=0.453^{+0.143}_{-0.133}$, with a crossing redshift $z_\times=0.476^{+0.106}_{-0.081}$ conditional on $0<z_\times<6$. For this data combination, physical-likelihood optimization by Metropolis--Hastings (MH) simulated annealing gives Akaike information criterion differences of $\Delta\mathrm{AIC}\simeq-3.40$ for HoloEoS and $-4.10$ for CPL-VCDM relative to $\Lambda$CDM. Thus, a Hubble-scale-motivated dark-energy history realized within a specified gravitational theory achieves fitting performance comparable to CPL-VCDM while naturally allowing phantom-divide crossing.

papers.title: Continuous Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using PPG From Methods to Clinical Translation
papers.abstract: Continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring could improve hypertension management by capturing changes that intermittent cuff measurements miss. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is widely explored for cuffless BP estimation because optical sensors are inexpensive, wearable, and already present in many consumer and clinical devices. PPG, however, does not measure arterial pressure: BP is inferred from waveform characteristics or pulse timing, which also depend on vascular tone, arterial stiffness, sensor contact, motion, and individual physiology. This survey reviews PPG-based cuffless BP estimation along the full measurement chain, covering physiological mechanisms, waveform features, pulse arrival time (PAT), pulse transit time (PTT), machine-learning methods, datasets, calibration, validation, deployment, bias, and clinical translation. Studies are assessed by the strength of evidence they provide rather than by reported error alone, with particular attention to subject and temporal leakage, dataset imbalance, calibration dependence and drift, motion artifacts, and the gap between benchmark accuracy and reliable real-world measurement. The review finds that progress depends on more than better prediction algorithms. Future work should prioritize physiologically informed models, diverse longitudinal datasets, transparent reporting of calibration requirements and failure rates, stronger evaluation protocols, and studies that demonstrate practical value in clinical care.

authors.name: Harshitha Manjunatha
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

authors.name: Tooraj Nikoubin
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process
papers.abstract: Tools for interpreting the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on LLMs themselves to both generate and evaluate explanations, creating a self-referential automated interpretation process with minimal human oversight. This automation raises significant reliability concerns, which are exacerbated by the absence of ground truth. In practice, it is difficult to validate explanations or to attribute interpretability failures to their source -- whether they originate from the tool's extracted representations or from the LLM used in the process. To address these challenges, we present DECODE, a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into the automated interpretation process. Our approach decomposes the diagnostic workflow into three progressive stages, isolating failure sources ranging from structural defects to explanation-level misalignments. Drawing inspiration from inter-coder consensus in qualitative analysis, we utilize consensus among independently generated explanations and their evaluation metrics as a proxy for reliability. To further scale human inspection, we employ a three-phase active seeding protocol that strategically recommends high-priority instances for manual review. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study on 16,384 Sparse Autoencoder features, showing that it can efficiently identify and attribute interpretability failures at scale.

authors.name: Dohyun Kim
authors.institution: The Catholic University of Korea Seoul St. Mary's Hospital

papers.title: Tight Quantum Query Bounds for Minimum Cut and Multicut on Dense Graphs
papers.abstract: We determine the dense worst-case quantum query complexity of exact minimum multicut on simple unweighted undirected graphs. With at most $k$ explicit demand pairs, our adjacency-array algorithm uses $\OO(n+\min\{m,n^{3/2}\sqrt{k}\})$ queries; a matching lower bound holds for every $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and sufficiently large $n$, with constants uniform in $k$. In particular, the $k=1$ case gives an $\OO(n^{3/2})$ query algorithm for prescribed $s$--$t$ cut. The upper bound combines degree-sensitive spectral estimates of local improvement with refinement by unions of label classes. These steps retain every original optimum and permit exact acquisition without an additional label-count factor. Separately, we prove an $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ global minimum-cut lower bound on dense connected graphs, matching the existing upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors. It holds for the value and for any optimum shore, even with known degrees and sorted neighbor arrays; regular hard instances have balanced optimum cuts. Both lower bounds use degree-preserving switches and classify optimum outputs across a hidden threshold. Our upper bound concerns input queries, not total running time: computation on acquired data may be exponential, even in the single-demand case. Matching bounds at each prescribed sparse edge count are not established.

authors.name: Runtian Ren
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shengcai Liu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hamming and Johnson-Type Bounds for Joint Error Correction and Detection
papers.abstract: We derive upper bounds on the size of codes for joint error correction and detection over classical $q$-ary Hamming spaces. A $(c,c')$ joint error correcting and detecting code corrects every error of weight at most $c$ and detects every error whose weight lies between $c+1$ and $c+c'$. We establish equivalent conditions for this decoding requirement using Hamming balls and Hamming rings, and derive a joint bound that reduces to the Hamming bound when $c'=0$. We introduce joint perfect codes and show that binary repetition codes attain the joint bound whenever $n=2c+c'+1$. For codes satisfying $d_{\min}=2c+c'+1$, we investigate an alternative joint bound based on ring multiplicity and constant-weight code bounds. A further argument using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and pairwise ring intersections yields a refined joint bound that is always at least as strong as the original joint bound. We then incorporate an additional outer Hamming shell to obtain a Johnson-type extension. This extension provides a strict improvement for binary codes with $c'=1$, $d_{\min}=2c+2$, $c\geq2$, and $d_{\min}+2\leq n\leq3d_{\min}/2-1$. These results connect sphere-packing bounds with the geometry of joint error correction and detection.

authors.name: Yulin Chen
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

papers.title: On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty set $X \subset \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is (first-order) Schreier if $|X| \leq \min X$. These Schreier sets can be generalized recursively to higher-order Schreier sets, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show that the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element $2$ and maximum element $n+4$ is one more than the $n^\text{th}$ term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1, F_2, \ldots$ with $F_2, F_3, \ldots$ (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: Electric Fields Turn Vacancy-trapping Grain Boundaries into Li-Ion Pathways in Li2O
papers.abstract: Ion transport in solids has conventionally been understood from equilibrium diffusion, yet ions in batteries are driven by electric fields. Does field-driven ion transport follow equilibrium behavior? We examined this question in bulk Li2O and at its grain boundaries (GBs) using electric-field molecular dynamics combining a machine learning interatomic potential with a Bader charge prediction model. Although Li diffusion in cubic Li2O is isotropic at zero field, an electric field renders it orientation dependent because Li hops along a limited set of crystallographic pathways that the field biases unequally. At GBs, this anisotropy becomes a qualitative difference: a GB that strongly traps Li vacancies but exhibits a strong field response releases them under a field, whereas a weakly responsive GB retains them despite weaker vacancy trapping. These results show that field-driven GB transport is governed not by static thermodynamics alone but by the angle between the electric field and the diffusion pathways of the constituent grains.

papers.title: Efficient Genotype Classification from 3D MRI in ADPKD via Density-Aware Point Sampling and E(3)-invariance
papers.abstract: Early detection of genetic kidney diseases, especially autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), is crucial because certain genotypes such as truncating PKD1 mutations cause rapid kidney growth and early progression to end-stage kidney disease. MRI-based genotype inference is a potential low-cost complement to genetic testing. However, although many deep learning methods have been developed for classifying various MR images, applying them to ADPKD remains challenging: (1) abdominal MR images are generally too large to be handled by deep learning models designed for smaller images like brain MRI, and (2) the amount of labeled data for ADPKD genetic mutations is insufficient to train deep learning models. In order to address these challenges, we propose E3PN, an efficient 3D MRI-based ADPKD genotype classification network that relies on point sampling and E(3)-invariance. We utilize a point representation of 3D MRI, which consumes less GPU memory than a voxel representation. For further memory efficiency, 3D points are sampled from a mixture distribution over the two kidneys in each image. Since E(3)-invariance has been shown to improve data efficiency, we also incorporate it into our model through coordinate canonicalization. On our ADPKD dataset, E3PN trains 163 times faster and uses 103x less GPU memory than a 3D ResNet, while also improving F1 from 0.165 to 0.226 over both baselines. These results establish a first benchmark for five-way ADPKD genotype classification from 3D MRI and show that point sampling and coordinate canonicalization yield two-orders-of-magnitude efficiency gains with a modest but consistent improvement in F1.

authors.name: Kwanghee Lee
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Uncertainty evaluation of length measurement by spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing
papers.abstract: In this study, we evaluate the measurement uncertainty of spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing, which has significant potential for interferometer-based dimensional calibration services owing to its simple configuration and nanometer-level precision. A super-luminescent diode (SLD) with a broadband spectrum was used as the light source for high-precision length measurement, and a frequency-calibrated spectrometer captured the spectral interference signal. The length measurement results were compared with a laser displacement interferometer. To evaluate the measurement uncertainty, numerical simulations were performed by considering the intensity-noise level of the CCD in the spectrometer and the frequency-axis uncertainty of the spectrometer. Through a comprehensive uncertainty analysis supported by numerical simulations, the combined standard uncertainty of the measured length was evaluated as sqrt((10 nm)^2 + (9.7x10^(-6)xL)^2). The resulting uncertainty budget provides a metrological basis for extending SLD-based SDI with super-Gaussian windowing toward interferometric dimensional calibration tasks over the millimeter-scale range.

authors.name: Sunghoon Eom
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science

authors.name: Chu-Shik Kang
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science

papers.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
papers.abstract: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change. Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame, where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama) lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model. A controlled encoder x supervision study shows that the encoder decides what can be read and the supervision what is read: at a matched budget, counterfactual supervision adds 4.5 points on average and 38 on the speed questions of natural benchmarks. Code and models: https://github.com/kkt94/Llama-V-JEPA-LM.

papers.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
papers.abstract: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $\chi(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $\Phi_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\ge\Phi_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(\chi(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Acoustic condition monitoring often relies on normal recordings with limited operating-condition information. This study proposes an anomalous sound detection system that learns from normal recordings without external pre-training and uses machine-type information to organize training and normal references. A separator learns target-component estimation from mixtures of normal target and non-target recordings. With the separator frozen, regional attention and multi-stage fusion are trained on paired mixtures sharing a target, using contrastive and target-reference consistency objectives. Paired-mixture embedding differences provide covariance statistics for correction with normal-reference centering, followed by cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. On Task 2 development-test data from the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge, the two-block, 64-channel system achieves an overall harmonic mean of 64.56% on average across three independent training and evaluation runs, with a sample standard deviation of 0.33 percentage points. This mean exceeds that of direct paired-mixture learning by 2.23 percentage points and is 0.31 percentage points below that of the evaluated distillation system using an externally pre-trained teacher. For the learned embeddings, cosine nearest-neighbor scoring outperforms the evaluated Mahalanobis scorers based on global normal statistics. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining separation-based representation learning, interference-based correction, and local normal-reference scoring for anomalous sound detection without detailed operating metadata.

papers.title: C-to-Rust Translation Validation at the LLVM IR Level via AI-Assisted Refinement Proof
papers.abstract: Migrating C codebases to Rust is a promising approach to securing legacy software, but existing translators do not guarantee that a translated Rust program preserves the behavior of the C program. Neither rule-based nor large language model (LLM)-based translators have been formally verified, and existing approaches to checking translation correctness are limited to testing and bounded checks, which cannot reason about all possible executions. In this work, we present R2C2, which validates C-to-Rust translation by proving in Rocq that the Rust program refines the C program, i.e., every behavior on the Rust side is also a behavior on the C side. Since no formal semantics defines the behaviors of C and Rust programs in the same terms, we prove refinement between the two programs compiled to the LLVM intermediate representation (LLVM IR). In addition, to resolve the discrepancies between the data representations of C and Rust, we introduce a common abstraction that relates two corresponding representations through an abstract value, and specify the behavior of each library function over abstract values. We construct the refinement proof as a chain of refinement relations, where only one relation is program-specific and proved at validation time, while the others are proved for all programs in advance. Proof construction is automated by AI agents, and since Rocq checks the proofs, the agents need not be trusted. We evaluate R2C2 on LLM translations of 519 C programs drawn from a benchmark suite used in prior work on C-to-Rust translation validation. R2C2 proves the translations of 486 programs correct without bounding their executions and discovers three incorrect translations, providing valid counterexamples that existing translation validation tools cannot find. We also conduct a case study on a small real-world image compression library and demonstrate how R2C2 can handle file operations.

papers.title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
papers.abstract: Generative design of formed sheet panels must preserve geometric manufacturing conditions while exploring layouts and improving performance. STAMP embeds these conditions directly in the shape representation. Each panel is described by its material layout and a reference surface with one height at each occupied position in a plane perpendicular to the drawing direction. Nominal thickness is prescribed along the normal. The representation allows curved surfaces, ribs, and openings. It excludes reference-surface undercuts and keeps nominal thickness fixed without manufacturing penalty terms. Because these conditions belong to the representation, every generated and optimized panel satisfies them regardless of training-set size. Boundary-conditioned diffusion generates alternative layouts, and predictor gradients guide a surface optimization that retains outlines, openings, and designated fixed regions. We demonstrate STAMP on automotive hood inner panels using CarHoods10k. With a comparable number of stored values, depth maps reconstruct surfaces more accurately than point-cloud and voxel baselines. From only five training designs, one of three training runs yields novel and varied layouts. A generator trained on 500 designs, 6.5% of the training set, already reaches the layout variety of the full-data model. Across 11 held-out design families, predictor-based selection among existing dataset designs yields an average gap of 0.18 mm to the best available FEA deformation, versus an expected 1.59 mm for random selection. It does better than random selection in all 11 families. At a 10% depth-change bound, a network not used in the search predicts an average deformation reduction of 24.8% for six generated and existing panels, with a 3.2% average mass increase computed from geometry. Engineers can thus explore and optimize panels within this manufacturing-informed design space.

authors.name: Namwoo Kang
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Rise of Zirconium Metal-Organic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: Zirconium metal-organic polyhedra (Zr-MOPs) assembled from cyclopentadienyl (Cp)-capped Zr$_3$ clusters and carboxylate linkers form a structurally diverse family. Which MOP forms depends on the connectivity of the Zr$_3$ node, the geometry of the linker, and assembly conditions. This review classifies Zr-MOPs into edge- and face-directed tetrahedra, a cube, and cocoons according to the connectivity and geometry of their building blocks. From reported structures, we map which linkers give which MOPs and examine how the Zr$_3$ cluster precursor and the reaction conditions decide between the tetrahedron and the cocoon when one linker can give both. We describe how hydrogen bonding and ionic association organize the MOPs into reticular nets and porous salts in the crystal. Together, these comparisons relate cage geometry to node-linker connectivity and crystal packing to the geometry and distribution of external interaction sites, providing a structural basis for designing Zr-MOPs and their supramolecular assemblies.

papers.title: Structural Self-Teaching for Compositional Generation in Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: We propose Structural Self-Teaching (SST), a novel framework that enhances compositional image generation in diffusion-based unified multimodal models (UMMs) by leveraging their internal understanding path as a source of structural supervision. The generation path of UMMs often struggles with dense compositional prompts, leading to missing objects, attribute binding failures, and spatial errors. In contrast, their understanding path localizes the same phrases in images that satisfy these prompts. SST converts this phrase-level grounding into training-time structural signals for the generation path. Specifically, we extract phrase-conditioned support masks from internal attention maps derived from the understanding path and employ them through two mechanisms. Phrase-local contrastive alignment uses these masks as pooling regions and aligns each generated phrase region with the same region of the target image. A structural scaffold builds a phrase-level layout from the same masks and modulates an intermediate spatial state of the generation path during training. The scaffold is phased out during training and removed at inference. SST requires no external structural annotations for training and no additional input at test time. Extensive experiments across multiple UMMs demonstrate that SST improves compositional fidelity over LoRA fine-tuning on the same data, with no inference-time cost. Project page is available at https://bellos1203.github.io/sst

papers.title: Folding of cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary symmetrizable Cartan data and arbitrary positive braids, we prove that the Laurent homomorphism identifying corresponding seed variables restricts to a surjective algebra homomorphism between the corresponding cluster algebras. We also extend the Kimura--Oya quantum twist automorphisms to arbitrary positive braids after localization at the frozen variables, and prove that their commutative specializations commute with the folding homomorphisms.

papers.title: Identifiability and Spectral Estimation of Mixed Memberships in Heterogeneous Multilayer Networks
papers.abstract: Multilayer network data, arising from multiple sources, repeated measurements, or multi-view interactions, are increasingly common, highlighting the need for statistical methods that jointly leverage information across layers while allowing for layer heterogeneity and computational scalability. Here, we study a multilayer degree-corrected mixed membership model (ML-DCMM), in which nodes share a common mixed membership across layers while degree effects and block connectivity patterns vary by layer. This model encompasses several existing models for multilayer data while preserving identifiability and interpretation. We develop a spectral estimation procedure that integrates layer-wise embeddings with corner estimation for membership recovery. A further refinement that connects the resulting representation to a ParaTuck-2 tensor decomposition is also introduced. We establish theoretical guarantees for the proposed spectral method, showing that the probability of near-corner recovery increases with the number of layers, and we provide the convergence rate for the resulting membership estimator. We establish a minimax lower bound for membership estimation, which does not improve with increasing number of layers. Simulation studies show that ML-DCMM can outperform other approaches under strong layer heterogeneity. In an analysis of London bike-sharing networks, the methodology recovers interpretable memberships and achieves lower held-out edge prediction error under edge-sampling cross-validation than competing models.

papers.title: Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning for Physical Attack on End-to-End Autoencoder Communications
papers.abstract: End-to-end autoencoder communication has emerged as a promising means of achieving efficient data transmission across various domains. Nevertheless, vulnerabilities have recently been revealed in these systems by adversarial attacks, wherein malevolent entities manipulate the transmitted signals to deceive the autoencoder. This paper leverages the applications of evolutionary algorithms to solve a challenging optimization problem of launching physical attacks against end-to-end autoencoder communication. For white-box scenarios, we introduce PAGA (Physical Attack based on Genetic Algorithm), which combines a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization to craft attack signals that degrade autoencoder performance. To gauge the efficacy of these attack signals, we employ a fitness function that assesses their capacity to induce substantial reconstruction errors and misclassification rates. A Multi-Factorial version of PAGA, referred to as PAMFGA, is proposed to deal with practical scenarios where the attackers have limited knowledge about the receiver, also known as a black-box attack. Our experimental results show that the proposed attacks can substantially degrade the reliability of the considered autoencoder communication systems across the evaluated settings. This study also underscores the critical importance of incorporating security considerations into the design and implementation of end-to-end autoencoder communication systems.

papers.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.

papers.title: Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system
papers.abstract: We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{\gamma-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<\gamma<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.

papers.title: Extreme central $L$-values of almost prime quadratic twists of elliptic curves II
papers.abstract: We prove lower bounds for central $L$-values of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve by discriminants with at most five prime factors. Under the rank-zero Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, these bounds give large Tate--Shafarevich groups.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.

papers.title: Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations
papers.abstract: We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the K\"ahler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.

papers.title: Analyzing Learning-Dynamics Across Loss and Prediction Choices for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Denoising generative models predict clean data ($x$), noise ($\epsilon$), or velocity ($v$), while training losses can be measured in any of these spaces. Although the resulting nine combinations are algebraically related, they can yield substantially different denoising accuracy and sample quality. We disentangle the effects of prediction and loss spaces. For a fixed prediction target, we show that changing the loss space is exactly equivalent to timestep reweighting and provide a heuristic analysis of how this reweighting affects generation quality. We then show that a rank-$m$ linear bottleneck compressing a $D$-dimensional noisy input imposes an irreducible squared-error floor of $D-m$ on noise and velocity prediction, whereas clean-data prediction can exploit low-dimensional data structure. Combining this bound with prediction-dependent error conversion yields distinct necessary conditions on bottleneck capacity. Experiments with U-Net and JiT across CIFAR-10, Imagenette, and ImageNet-256 support these theoretical predictions. Under compression, prediction choice strongly affects both denoising accuracy and sample quality, with noise-prediction errors closely matching the theoretical lower bound. Our results provide a quantitative understanding of how architectural bottlenecks interact with prediction and loss choices in denoising generative models.

papers.title: Kobayashi-Hitchin Correspondence on Equivariant and Basic Bundles
papers.abstract: Let $(X,J,\omega)$ be a compact complex manifold with Gauduchon metric and $G$ a Lie group acting on $X$ by holomorphic isometries. We give an explicit proof of the existence of a $G$-invariant Hermitian-Einstein metric on a $G$-polystable $G$-equivariant holomorphic vector bundle adapting the proof of L\"ubke-Teleman. We see that if $G$ is a connected complex Lie group with the bijective exponential map and the action of $G$ on $X$ is locally free, then our existence theorem is equivalent to the existence of a basic Hermitian-Einstein metric on a basic polystable basic holomorphic vector bundle on $X$ foliated by the foliation generated by the $G$-action. As an application, we can say that the foliated Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on a Sasakian manifold $S$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-equivariant Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on the Vaisman manifold $S\times S^1$.

papers.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators
papers.abstract: AI-enabled smart homes are becoming more common across the grid edge. However, there has not been much work on failure response. This area is critical because smart homes operate on the grid edge where failures can cascade down. If a power outage happens within a smart home, a user has to manually troubleshoot their smart home to include tasks such as power load balance and device recovery. We conduct the first resilience analysis of smart home agents across a full power outage, providing a suite of outage simulations in a live environment that measures resilience before, during, and post power outage. We show that smart home agents can act as grid operators in power outages and identify several new failure categories highlighting the current limitations across all of our models. These findings establish the groundwork for smart home agents as grid operators to increase overall resilience on the grid edge.

papers.title: Spatial scaling of heterogeneity transfer from boron concentration to absorbed dose in boron neutron capture therapy
papers.abstract: We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately $90\%$ of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of $6.00~\mu\mathrm{m}$, with a characteristic deposition length of $\ell_B\approx2.05~\mu\mathrm{m}$. Dose heterogeneity increases with both the fluctuation amplitude $H$ and correlation length $\xi$, while the transfer factor $S=CV_D/H$ exhibits an approximate scaling collapse as a function of $\xi/\ell_B$. Analytical Gaussian and lognormal--Gaussian models provide reference predictions for this behavior. At short correlation lengths, the Geant4 response yields a higher transfer factor than a Gaussian response with the same characteristic length, highlighting the influence of the energy-deposition shape on dose smoothing. For $D_{95}$, defined as the dose received by at least $95\%$ of the modeled volume, the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous boron-dose models reaches $(86.62\pm1.07)\%$ at $H=1.2$ and a target ratio $\xi/\ell_B=6$. We show that mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component.

authors.name: Roni Muslim
authors.institution: Asia Pacific Center for Theoretical Physics

papers.title: A $19/5$ lower bound for the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem
papers.abstract: For every power $q\ge2$ of~$2$, we construct a box-free subset of $[q^5]^4$ with $q^{19}$ points, improving the lower-bound exponent in the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem from $15/4$ to $19/5$. In fact, $[q^5]^4$ partitions into $q$ isomorphic box-free sets. The proof uses a finite-field rectangle lemma and orthogonality in a four-dimensional bilinear space. We also deduce a uniform bound $f_4(n)\ge2^{-19/20}n^{19/5}$ and a lower bound for grid-coloring numbers.

authors.name: Dean Matthew Menezes
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity (MF) formulation of Operator Inference (OpInf) for learning non-intrusive, physics-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of nonlinear dynamical systems. OpInf learns reduced operators from projections of snapshot data by solving a least squares regression problem. However, generating high-fidelity snapshots can be computationally expensive, limiting parameter coverage and the temporal extent of training trajectories for many aerospace applications, which can lead to inaccurate or unstable ROM predictions. This work proposes MF-OpInf, which combines limited high-fidelity snapshots with more plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variates-inspired MF least squares formulation to learn a single set of reduced operators across multiple trajectories. Low-fidelity trajectories provide additional parameter coverage and extend beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. The low-fidelity snapshots are also used to construct an improved reduced basis through weighted proper orthogonal decomposition. We demonstrate MF-OpInf on a nonlinear reaction-diffusion problem with parametrized sinusoidal forcing and a two-dimensional incompressible flow past a cylinder with a parametrized inlet pulse. In these experiments, under an equal training simulation budget, MF-OpInf reduces the mean relative prediction error at unseen parameters by up to $87\%$ for the reaction-diffusion problem and $28\%$ for the cylinder flow problem over the test time regime, which extends beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. These results demonstrate that MF-OpInf can improve temporal extrapolation and prediction at unseen parameters without increasing the training simulation budget.

authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin
